body: {#a#}¦ I. The letter {%ă,%} the first of the alphabet and the short vowel inherent in every consonant. See {#akAra#}. <div n="P">II. The pronominal theme which occurs in the declension of {#idam#} and is considered as a substitute for {#idam#} and {#etat#} qq. vv. <div n="P">III. ind. ({#nipAta#}) A particle, a shorter form of {#na#} (see also {#ana#} and {#anA#}); it is used <sup>1</sup> In composition with nouns, when it implies <sup>a.</sup> Negation. <sup>b.</sup> Privation or prohibition. <sup>c.</sup> Diminu- tion (i. e. a little). <sup>d.</sup> Deterioration. <sup>e.</sup> Similarity or comparison; in a few instances it has apparently become an expletive; cf. e. g. {#kupya#} and {#akupya, udAra#} and {#anudAra, eqamUka#} and {#aneqamUka#}. If the noun begins with a vowel, it assumes the form of {#an#}, as {#a#} and {#anta#} form {#ananta#}; this rule is neglected sometimes, if the vowel following the {#a#} happen to be a {#f#}; e. g. {#a#} and {#fRin#} form {#anfRin#} and sometimes {#afRin#}. <sup>2</sup> In con- junction with an inflected verb, when it implies blame or re- proach; e. g. {#a karozi vE tvaM jAlma#} ‘how badly thou dost (it), fool’. Accord. to an artificial E. from {#at#}, kṛt aff. {#qa#}. <div n="P">IV. ind. ({#nipAta#}) An interjection of pity. <div n="P">V. 1. m. ({#aH#}) <sup>1</sup> Vaiśvānara (in an Upan.). <sup>2</sup> Brahman (m.). <sup>3</sup> Viṣṇu. <sup>4</sup> Siva. 2. n. ({#am#}) A name of the (neuter) Brahman.
{#afRin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RI-RinI-Ri#}) Free from debt or obligation; also {#anfRin#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#fRin#}.
{#aMS (aMSa-curAdi-parasmEpadin)#}¦ r. 10th cl. par. ({#aMSayati#} or {#aMSApayati-#} p. p. {#aMSita#}) To divide, to distribute.

{#aMSa#}¦ I. m. ({#-SaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Dividing, distributing. <sup>2</sup> A part. <sup>3</sup> A share or portion. <sup>4</sup> A fraction. <sup>5</sup> The numerator of a fraction. <sup>6</sup> A degree (of latitude or longitude, &c.). <sup>7</sup> The name of an Āditya. <sup>8</sup> (In music.) See {#aMSasvara#}. Also confounded with {#aMsa#} q. v. E. {#aMS#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}, or perhaps more correctly, {#am#}, uṇ(?) aff. {#Sa#}. <div n="P">II. m. n. ({#-SaH-Sam#}) The shoulder, the shoulder blade. (In this sense the word is more correctly written {#aMsa#} q. v.)
{#aMSaka#}¦ I. m. ({#-kaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A part. <sup>2</sup> An heir, a kinsman, a relation. E. {#aMSa#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-kam#}) A day. E. {#aMS#}, kṛt aff. {#Rvul(?)#}.
{#aMSakaraRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) The dividing into shares. E. {#aMSa#} and {#karaRa#}.
{#aMSaBAj#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#BAk#}) An heir, a coheir, one who has a share or portion. E. {#aMS#} and {#BAj#}.
{#aMSala#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Strong, stout, lusty. See {#aMsala#}.
{#aMSavat#}¦ m. ({#-vAn#}) A species of the Soma plant. E. {#aMSa#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#aMSasavarRana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Assimilation of fractions, ren- dering fractions homogeneous, reduction of them to uni- formity. E. {#aMSa#} and {#savarRana#}.

{#aMSasvara#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-raH#}) (In music.) The tonic or modal note. It is defined as ‘the note which displays the pecu- liar melody and to which all the others are subordinate’. Also written {#aMsasvara#}. E. {#aMSa#} and {#svara#}.
{#aMSahara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A sharer, a divider, a coheir. E. {#aMSa#} and {#hara#}.
{#aMSahArin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rI#}) A sharer, a coheir. E. {#aMSa#} and {#hArin#}.
{#aMSAMSi#}¦ Bahuvr. or Avyayībh. ind. Share by share. E. {#aMSa#} repeated, samāsānta aff. {#ic#}.
{#aMSin#}¦ m. ({#-SI#}) A sharer, a coheir. E. {#aMSa#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#aMSu#}¦ m. ({#-SuH#}) <sup>1</sup> A ray of light, a sun- or moon-beam. <sup>2</sup> The sun. <sup>3</sup> Light, splendour, effulgence. <sup>4</sup> Any thing minute or pointed (as a sun-beam). <sup>5</sup> A small end of thread, a small filament &c. <sup>6</sup> Dress, decoration. <sup>7</sup> The name of one of the Grahas (q. v.) which serve for making libations with the juice of the Soma plant. <sup>8</sup> The name of a Rishi. <sup>9</sup> The name of a prince, son of Puruhotra. E. {#aMS#}, uṇ. aff. {#ku#}, or {#am#}, uṇ. aff. {#ku#}, āgama {#Suk#}.

{#aMSuka#}¦ n. ({#-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> Fine cloth, muslin. <sup>2</sup> Cloth in general. <sup>3</sup> A mantle, a wrapper, a linen garment worn round the upper part of the body. <sup>4</sup> White cloth. <sup>5</sup> The leaf of the Laurus Cassia. E. {#aMSu#}, taddh. aff. {#ka#}. Acc. to another E. a Tatpur. composed of {#aMSu#} and {#ka#} ({#kAS#}, kṛt aff. {#qa#}).
{#aMSujAla#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-lam#}) <sup>1</sup> A collection or blaze of light. <sup>2</sup> A parcel or pencil of rays. E. {#aMSu#} and {#jAla#}.
{#aMSuDara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) The sun. E. {#aMSu#} and {#Dara#}.
{#aMSupawwa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-wwam#}) A peculiar kind of fine cloth made of bark. E. {#aMSu#} and {#pawwa#}.
{#aMSupati#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tiH#}) The sun. E. {#aMSu#} and {#pati#}.
{#aMSuBartf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rtA#}) The sun. E. {#aMSu#} and {#Bartf#}.

{#aMSumat#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-mAn-matI-mat#}) <sup>1</sup> Radiant, luminous. <sup>2</sup> Having small filaments. <sup>3</sup> Acuminated, pointed. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-mAn#}) <sup>1</sup> The sun. <sup>2</sup> A species of the Soma plant. <sup>3</sup> A prince of the solar race, son of Asamanjas, grandson of Sāgara and father of Dilīpa. <sup>4</sup> A descendant of Kratha. <sup>5</sup> A Ṛṣi.--f. ({#-matI#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of the celestial river Yamunā. <sup>2</sup> A plant (Hedysarum Gangeticum). E. {#aMSu#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#aMSumatPalA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-lA#}) The plantain (Musa paradisiaca). E. {#aMSumat#} and {#Pala#}.
{#aMSumAlA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-lA#}) A garland of light, a halo. E. {#aMSu#} and {#mAlA#}.
{#aMSumAlin#}¦ m. ({#-lI#}) The sun. E. {#aMSumAlA#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.
{#aMSula#}¦ m. ({#-laH#}) A name of the sage Chāṇakya. E. {#aMSu#}, taddh. aff. {#lac(?)#}; properly meaning, radiant, splendid.
{#aMSuvARa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-RaH#}) The sun. E. {#aMSu#} and {#vARa#}.
{#aMSuhasta#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-staH#}) The sun. E. {#aMSu#} and {#hasta#}.

{#aMs (aMsa-curAdi-parasmEpadin)#}¦ r. 10th cl. par. ({#aMsayati#} or {#aMsA-#} {#payati-#} p. p. {#aMsita#}) <sup>1</sup> To divide, to distribute. With {#vi#}, <sup>1</sup> To divide. <sup>2</sup> To make powerless, to ward off (as the force of a blow). See {#aMS#}.

{#aMsa#}¦ I. m. n. ({#-saH-sam#}) 1. The shoulder, the scapula; it is mentioned in medic. amongst those {#marman#} (q. v.) the wounding of which produces lameness or palsy. 2. (m.) One of the angles of the {#vedi#} (q. v.), compared to a shoulder. E. {#am#}, uṇ. aff. {#san#}. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-saH#}) 1. A part, a portion &c. See {#aMSa#}. (In this mean- ing the word is more correctly written {#aMSa#}.) 2. The name of a king, acc. to some, a son of Anu. E.(?).
{#aMsakUwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-waH#}) A bull's hump, the protuberance between the shoulders of the Indian ox. E. {#aMsa#} and {#kUwa#}.

{#aMsatra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-tram#}) (ved.) <sup>1</sup> Armour, mail. <sup>2</sup> A bow. E. {#aMsa#} and {#tra#}; also derived, though without probability, from {#aMhas#} (changed to {#aMsa#}) and {#tra#}, as preserving from evil.

{#aMsaPalaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) (In medic.) The upper part of the spinal column; it is mentioned amongst those {#marman#} (q. v.) the wound- ing of which produces lameness or palsy. E. {#aMsa#} and {#Palaka#}.
{#aMsaBAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A yoke on the shoulder for car- rying burthens with. Also {#aMseBAra#} q. v. E. {#aMsa#} and {#BAra#}.
{#aMsaBArika#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) One who carries burthens with a yoke on the shoulder. Also {#aMsoBArika#}. E. {#aMsaBAra#}, taddh. aff. {#zWan#}.
{#aMsala#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Strong, stout, lusty. E. {#aMsa#}, taddh. aff. {#lac#}, also written {#aMSala#}.
{#aMsavat#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-vAn-vatI-vat#}) Feeble, weak. E. {#aMsa#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#aMseBAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A yoke on the shoulder for carry- ing burthens with. Also {#aMsaBAra#} q. v. E. {#aMsa#} (loc.) and {#BAra#}.
{#aMseBArika#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) One who carries burthens with a yoke on the shoulder. Also {#aMsaBArika#}. E. {#aMseBAra#}, taddh. aff. {#zWan#}.
{#aMsya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-syaH-syA-syam#}) Belonging or referring to the shoulder. E. {#aMsa#}, taddh. aff. {#yat#}.

{#aMh#}¦ I. ({#ahi-BvAdi-udAtta-anudAttet#}) r. 1st cl. ātm. ({#aMhate-#} {#AnaMhe-aMhitA-aMhizyate-AMhizwa#}.--Caus. {#aMhayati-AYjihat#}. --Des. {#aYjihizate#}). To go. See {#aNG#}. [Page002-b+ 56] <div n="P">II. ({#ahi-curAdi-parasmEpadin#}) r. 10th cl. par. ({#aMhaya-#} {#ti#} p. p. {#aMhita#}) To shine, or according to some, to speak. <div n="P">The radical {#aMh#} is considered in some derivations as a substitute for {#han#}; see {#aMhati, aMhas, aMhu#} &c.

{#aMhati#}¦ f. I. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Pain, distress. <sup>2</sup> Sickness, disease. <div n="P">II. ({#-tiH#} and {#-tI#}) A gift, a donation. E. {#aMh#}, uṇ. aff. {#ati; aMh#} being considered here as a substitute for {#han#} . {#aMhatI#} with fem. aff. {#NIz#}.
{#aMhas#}¦ n. ({#-haH#}) Sin, evil. E. {#am#}, uṇ. aff. {#asun#} and āgama {#huk#} or according to others from {#aMh#} considered as a substitute for {#han#}. See {#aNGas#}.
{#aMhasaspati#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tiH#}) The intercalary month of the Hindu year. E. {#aMhas#} (gen.) and {#pati#}.
{#aMhasvat#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-svAn-svatI-svat#}) Sinful, wicked. E. {#aMhas#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#aMhiti#}¦ f. ({#-tiH#}) A gift or donation. E. See {#aMhati, iw#} being inserted.

{#aMhu#}¦ (ved.) I. m. ({#-huH#}) <sup>1</sup> Wicked, sinful, distressed. <sup>2</sup> The name of an Asura. II. n. ({#-hu#}) Distress. III. n. f. ({#-hu-huH#}) Puden- dum muliebre. E. ({#-aMh#},) uṇ. aff. {#u#}.
{#aMhuBedI#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-dI#}) (ved.) Whose female parts are broken (in coition; an ep. of a mare). E. {#aMhu#} and {#BedI#} inst. of {#BedyA#}.
{#aMhura#}¦ m. ({#-raH#}) (ved.) Wicked, sinful. E. {#aMh#}, uṇ. aff. {#urac#}.
{#aMhUraRa#}¦ (ved.) I. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) Sinful. II. n. ({#-Ram#}) Sin, evil. E. {#aMhUra#} ({#aMh#}, uṇ. aff. {#Ura#}), taddh. aff. {#na#}.
{#aMhomuc#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-k#}) (ved.) Freeing from sin, evil. E. {#aMhas#} and {#muc#}.
{#aMhoyu#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-yuH#}) (ved.) Freed from sin or evil; an ep. of {#tanU#} ‘body’. E. {#aMhas#} and {#yu#}.
{#aMhri#}¦ m. (according to some also n.) ({#-hriH-hri#}) <sup>1</sup> The foot. <sup>2</sup> The root of a tree. See {#aNGri#}. E. {#aMh#}, uṇ. aff. {#krin#}.
{#aMhripa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) A tree. E. {#aMhri#} and {#pa#}. See {#aNGripa#}.

{#aMhriskanDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nDaH#}) (In medic.) The same as {#kUrcaSiras#} i. e. the part under the ancle joint on either side of the foot; it is mentioned amongst those {#marman#} (q. v.) the wounding of which produces swelling and pain. Also {#aNGriskanDa#}. E. {#aMhri#} and {#skanDa#}.
{#ak (aka-BvAdi-GawAdi-udAtta-udAttet-mit)#}¦ r. 1st cl. par. ({#akati-Aka-akitA-AkIt#}.--Caus. {#akayati#}) To wind or move tortuously. See also {#ag#}.
{#aka#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> Pain, affliction. <sup>2</sup> Sin. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ka#}.

{#akaca#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-caH-cA-cam#}) Bald, destitute of hair. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-caH#}) A name of Ketu, the dragon's tail, or descending node. E. {#a#} priv. and {#kaca:#} this applies to Ketu, as the symbol of the asterism is a headless trunk.
{#akaRwaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Free from thorns, literally or metaphorically (as from enemies). E. {#a#} priv. and {#kaRwaka#}.
{#akanizWa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-zWaH-zWA-zWam#}) Not the youngest. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-zWaH#}) A deified saint according to the Bauddhas. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kanizWa#}.
{#akanizWaga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) A deified saint according to the Bauddhas. E. {#akanizWa#} and {#ga#}.
{#akapIvat#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vAn#}) The name of one of the seven Ṛṣis or Sages during the reign of Tāmasa or the fourth Manu. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kapIvata#}.

{#akampita#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unshaken, firm, not agitated or trembling. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-taH#}) The name of a Jaina saint, one of the pupils of the last Tīrthakara and one of the eleven chiefs of the Gaṇas or companies of the Jaina Ṛṣis. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kampita#}.

{#akara#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) One who does not act, inactive. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kara#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Handless, maimed. <sup>2</sup> Exempt from tax or duty, privileged. f. ({#-rA#}) Emblic myrobalan (Phyllanthus emblica). E. {#a#} priv. and {#kara#}.
{#akaraRi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-RiH#}) Failure, disappointment. (It is used only as an imprecation, as {#tasyAkaraRirevAstu#} ‘may he fail’.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#karaRi#}.
{#akaruRa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) Unfeeling, void of compassion or tenderness. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karuRA#}.
{#akarkaSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SA-Sam#}) Soft, not hard. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karkaSa#}.
{#akarRa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) <sup>1</sup> Earless. <sup>2</sup> Deaf. E. {#a#} priv. and {#karRa#}.

{#akarRya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rRyaH-rRyA-rRyam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not being in the ears. <sup>2</sup> Not fit for the ears. <sup>3</sup> Different from what is in or fit for the ears. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karRya#}.
{#akartana#}¦ Tatpur.(?) m. ({#-naH#}) A dwarf. E.(?). This word seems doubtful and may be perhaps a misreading of {#vartana#} q. v.
{#akarmaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-kaH#}) (In grammar.) Having no direct object, intransitive (as a verb). See {#akarman#}. E. {#akarman#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.

{#akarmakft#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kft#}) I. Free from action, neces- sary as vital or essential as religious. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karmakft#}. <div n="P">II. Committing improper acts. E. {#akarman#} and {#kft#}.
{#akarmaRya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RyaH-RyA-Ryam#}) Not to be done, improper. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karmaRya#}.

{#akarman#}¦ I. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rmA-rmA-rma#}) <sup>1</sup> Without work, idle, unoccupied. <sup>2</sup> Unfit to work, inefficient. <sup>3</sup> Degraded, no longer performing essential rites. <sup>4</sup> (In grammar.) Having no direct object, intransitive (as a verb). See {#akarmaka#}, E. {#a#} priv. and {#karman#}. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}) <sup>1</sup> Absence of occupation. <sup>2</sup> Loss or neglect of essential observances. <sup>3</sup> Improper act, crime, offence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karman#}.

{#akarmaBoga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) The renunciation of reward for virtuous actions, the liberation of the soul from the fruits of action, that is, its absorption into the divine essence which releases it from future transmigration and from the trammels of matter, bestowing the highest state of future bliss. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karmaBoga#}.

{#akarmAnvita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) I. <sup>1</sup> Without work, idle, unoccupied. <sup>2</sup> No longer performing essential rites, degraded. E. {#a#} neg. and {#karmAnvita#}. <div n="P">II. Committing improper acts. E. {#akarman#} and {#anvita#}.
{#akala#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Being without parts, whole, entire. E. {#a#} priv. and {#kalA#}.

{#akalka#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-lkaH-lkA-lkam#}) <sup>1</sup> Clear, clean. <sup>2</sup> Free from sediment. <sup>3</sup> Pure, sinless. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-lkA#}) Moonlight. E. {#a#} priv. and {#kalka#}.
{#akalkatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Purity, honesty. E. {#akalka#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#}.
{#akalkana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Humble, not proud. (This word is sometimes written {#akalkala#}.) E. {#a#} priv. and {#kalkana#}.
{#akalpa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-lpaH#}) Uncontrolled (lit. not subject to rules or precepts; a vaidik epithet of Indra). E. {#a#} priv. and {#kalpa#}.
{#akalmAza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) Name of a son of Tāmasa or the fourth Manu. E. {#a#} priv. and {#kalmAza#}.
{#akalyARa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RI-Ram#}) Unlucky, inauspicious. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-Ram#}) Bad luck. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kalyARa#}.
{#akava#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) (ved.) Not contemptible. not to be despised, superior. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kava#}.

{#akavAri#}¦ m. f. ({#-ri-rI#}) (ved.) Explained either as I. Tatpur. 1. Not having contemptible enemies--or--2. Having obtained superiority. E. 1. {#a#} neg. and {#kava-ari#} (enemy). 2. {#akava#} and {#ari#} (going to, obtaining); or as <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. Having enemies who are not to be despised. E. {#akava#} and {#ari#} (enemy).
{#akaSAya#}¦ Tatpur.(?) m. ({#-yaH#}) A proper name; cf. {#Aka-#} {#SAyeya#}. E. unknown.

{#akasmAt#}¦ Tatpur. ind. <sup>1</sup> Without a cause, without a where- fore. <sup>2</sup> Immediately, instantly, presently. <sup>3</sup> Suddenly, at once. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kasmAt#}, the fifth case of {#kim#}.
{#akARqa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-RqaH-RqA-Rqam#}) Sudden, un- expected. {#akARqe#} suddenly. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kARqa#}.
{#akARqapAtajAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Perishing suddenly after birth, dying as soon as born. E. {#akARqa#}, and {#pAta-jAta#}.

{#akAma#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) Want of desire, love, intention &c. (See {#kAma#}.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#kAma#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-maH-mA-mam#}) <sup>1</sup> One who has no desire, no love. (See {#kAma#}.) <sup>2</sup> Unwilling, reluctant. <sup>3</sup> Un- intentional. <sup>4</sup> (In vaid. grammar; m. sc. {#sanDi#}) The Sandhi which causes the {#visarjanIya#} (q. v.) to be dropped, after it has become {#r#} before a following {#r#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#kAma#}.
{#akAmakarSana#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-naH#}) (ved.) Not disappointing de- sires. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kAma-karSana#}.
{#akAmatas#}¦ Tatpur. ind. <sup>1</sup> Unwillingly, reluctantly. <sup>2</sup> Unin- tentionally. E. {#a#} neg. and {#kAmatas#}.

Unafflicted, one free from any calamity inflicted by God or the king. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-daH#}) <sup>1</sup> A medicament, a drug. <sup>2</sup> Alexipharmacy, one of the eight branches of medicine. E. {#a#} priv. and {#gada#}.
{#agadaNkAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A physician. E. {#agada#} and {#kAra#} with āgama {#mum#} (or better {#agada#} in the acc. and {#kAra#}).
{#agady#}¦ denom. par. ({#agadyati#}) <sup>1</sup> To be healthy. <sup>2</sup> To make heal- thy, to cure. E. {#agada#}, denom. aff. {#yak#}.
{#agantavya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vyaH-vyA-vyam#}) Not to be visited or approached, also {#agamanIya, agamya#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gantavya#}.
{#agama#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> A mountain. <sup>2</sup> A tree. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gama#}. See also {#agacCa, aga#} and {#naga#}.

{#agamya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-myaH-myA-myam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not to be visited or approached. <sup>2</sup> Difficult of acquirement, unattainable. <sup>3</sup> Unequalled, unsurpassable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gamya#}.
{#agamyarUpa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-paH-pA-pam#}) Of superior or un- equalled form or nature. E. {#agamya#} and {#rUpa#}.
{#agamyAgamana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Approaching a woman who is not to be approached, improper or illicit intercourse, in- cest. E. {#agamyA#} and {#Agamana#}.
{#agamyAgamanIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Referring to illicit or improper intercourse, to incest. E. {#agamyAgamana#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#agamyAgAmin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-mI-minI-mi#}) Having illicit intercourse, incestuous. E. {#agamyA#} and {#AgAmin#}.

{#agarI#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-rI#}) A kind of grass, vulg. Deotāḍ (An- dropogon serratus). See {#devatAqa#}, also {#garI, KarAgarI#} and {#garAgarI#}. E. {#a#} prohib. and {#gara#}, the plant being an antidote.
{#agaru#}¦ Tatpur. m. n. ({#-ruH-ru#}) Agallochum (Aquilaria agallocha, Rox.). See {#aguru#}.
{#agarba#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rbaH-rbA-rbam#}) Modest, humble, void of pride. E. {#a#} neg. and {#garba#}.

{#agasti#}¦ m. ({#-stiH#}) <sup>1</sup> The name of a saint and reputed author of several hymns of the Rigveda, celebrated in Hindu my- thology, more usually entitled Agastya, and considered as the son of both Mitra and Varuṇa, by Urvaśī; hence his names Maitrāvaruṇi and Aurvaśīya. He is represented of short stature, and is said by some to have been born in a water jar; hence his names Kumbhasambhava, Ghaṭod- bhava &c. He is famed for having swallowed the ocean, when it had given him offence, wherefore he is called Pī- tābdhi. At his command the Vindhya range of mountains prostrated itself, and so remains; hence his present appel- lation. He is also mentioned as one of the oldest medical authors, considered as the civilisor of the South and as the regent of the star Canopus. <sup>2</sup> The name of a tree (Sesbana grandiflora). <sup>3</sup> m. plur. {#agastayaH#} are the descendants of Agasti. See {#Agastya#}. E. {#aga#} (mountain) and {#as#} (to throw), uṇ. aff. {#ti--:#} Agastya having ordered the Vindhya mountain to prostrate itself before him; or according to others, a Tatpur. composed of {#aga#} (water jar) and {#stya#} (from {#styE#} to condense): from his being kept and born in a wa- ter jar. (Both etymologies are apparently artificial and with- out any grammatical evidence.) See also {#agastya#} and {#agastI#}.
{#agastidru#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-druH#}) A tree (Sesbana grandiflora). See {#agasti#}. E. {#agasti#} and {#dru#}.
{#agastI#}¦ f. ({#-stI#}) A female descendant of Agastya. q. v. E. {#agastya#}, fem. aff. {#NIp#}.
{#agastIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Referring to Agastya. E. {#agastya#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#agastya#}¦ m. ({#-styaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The name of a saint. <sup>2</sup> The star Canopus. <sup>3</sup> The name of a tree. <sup>4</sup> A name of Śiva. See {#agasti#} and the E. of this word.
{#agastyodaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) The seventh day in the second half of the month Bhādra in the lunar year of the Hindus. E. {#agastya#} and {#udaya#}.
{#agA#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. ({#-gAH-gAH#}) Not going. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gA#} (from {#gam#}, kṛt aff. {#viw#}).
{#agAtmajA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-jA#}) A name of Pārvatī, the daughter of the mountain Himālaya. E. {#aga#} and {#AtmajA#}.

{#agADa#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-DaH-DA-Dam#}) Bottomless, very deep. <div n="P">II. 1. m. n. ({#-DaH-Dam#}) A hole, a chasm. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-DaH#}) The name of one of the five fires at the Svāhākāra. E. {#a#} priv. and {#gADa#}.
{#agADajala#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Having very deep waters. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-laH#}) A deep lake. E. {#agADa#} and {#jala#}.
{#agAra#}¦ n. ({#-ram#}) A house. See {#AgAra#}.
{#agAvaha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) A proper name of <sup>1</sup> the son of Vasu- deva by Vṛkadevī, and <sup>2</sup> the son of Kṛṣṇa by Sudevā. E. {#aga#} and {#Avaha#}.
{#agira#}¦ m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> The sun. <sup>2</sup> Fire. <sup>3</sup> A demon, a Rākṣasa. E. {#ag#}, aff. {#ira#}.
{#agu#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-guH-guH-gu#}) <sup>1</sup> Having no cows. <sup>2</sup> Having no beams. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-guH#}) A name of Rāhu or the ascending node q. v. E. {#a#} and {#go#}.

{#aguRa#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-RaH#}) A defect, a fault. E. {#a#} neg. and {#guRa#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Void of attributes. <sup>2</sup> Void of good qualities, bad. E. {#a#} priv. and {#guRa#}.
{#aguRatA (-tA)#}¦ Absence of all good qualities; also {#aguRatva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aguRa#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#aguRavAdin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dI-dinI-di#}) Censorious, pointing out defects. E. {#aguRa#} and {#vAdin#}.
{#aguRaSIla#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Of a bad dispo- sition, worthless. E. {#aguRa#} and {#SIlA#}.

{#aguru#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-ruH-ruH#} or {#rU#} or {#rvI-ru#}) <sup>1</sup> Not heavy, light. <sup>2</sup> Short (as a syllable). <div n="P">II. m. n. ({#-ruH-ru#}) <sup>1</sup> A fragrant wood, aloe wood, or agallochum (Aquilaria agallocha, Rox.). <sup>2</sup> The balsam tree from which is produced Bdellium (Amyris agallocha). <sup>3</sup> A timber tree, commonly Sisū (Dalbergia sisu, Rox.). E. {#a#} neg. and {#guru#}.
{#agupta#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) I. Tatpur. Unhidden, uncon- cealed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gupta#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. One who cannot keep a secret. E. {#a#} priv. and {#gupta#}.
{#aguruSiMSapA#}¦ Karmadh.(?) f. ({#-pA#}) A timber tree (Dalbergia sisu). The best authorities consider this as formed of two distinct words. See {#aguru#} and {#SiMSapA#}.
{#agUQa#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-QaH-QA-Qam#}) I. Tatpur. Unhidden, uncon- cealed, manifest, evident. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gUQa#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. One who is not secret. E. {#a#} priv. and {#gUQa#}.
{#agUQaganDa#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-nDam#}) Asafoetida. E. {#agUQa#} and {#ganDa#}.
{#agUQaBAva#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Open, honest, candid; one whose purpose or inclinations are evident. E. {#agUQa#} and {#BAva#}.
{#agfBIta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not taken. (In the Vedas.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#gfBIta#} (see {#gfhIta#}).
{#agfha#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-haH#}) See {#agraha#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#gfha#}.

{#agocara#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Not coming under the perception of the senses, covert, unseen, unwitnessed. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Any act or event not the object of the senses. <sup>2</sup> The imperceptible, Brahma, or the invisible Supreme. E. {#a#} neg. and {#gocara#}.
{#agohya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-hyaH-hyA-hyam#}) Not concealable, clear, bright (espec. as attribute of the sun, in the Vedas). E. {#a#} neg. and {#gohya#}.
{#agOkas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-kAH#}) <sup>1</sup> A bird. <sup>2</sup> A lion. <sup>3</sup> The Śarabha, a fabulous animal with eight legs. E. {#aga#} (a tree or moun- tain) and {#okas#}.
{#agnAmarut#}¦ Dvandva. m. du. ({#-tO#}) Agni and Marut qq. vv. E. {#agni#} (changed to {#agnA#}) and {#marut#}.

{#agnAyI#}¦ f. ({#-yI#}) <sup>1</sup> A goddess, the wife of Agni, the deity of fire, and presiding over prayers accompanied with burnt offerings. <sup>2</sup> The Tretā or second age of the Hindus. E. {#agni#}, fem. aff. {#NIp#}, with {#E#} substituted for {#i#}.
{#agnAvizRu#}¦ Dvandva. m. du. ({#-zRU#}) Agni and Viṣṇu qq. vv. E. {#agni#} (changed to {#agnA#}) and {#vizRu#}.

{#agni#}¦ m. ({#-gniH#}) <sup>1</sup> Fire; the fire for common use (or {#lOkika#}) as well as the fire for sacrificial purposes (or {#vEdika#}) of which there are three kinds: the Gārhapatya, the Āhava- nīya and the Dakṣiṇāgni (qq. vv.). <sup>2</sup> The deity of fire, one of the most ancient and most sacred objects of Hindu wor- ship. As such Agni is considered as the mediator between men and gods, as protector of mankind and their home, and as witness of their actions; hence his invocation at all solemn occasions, at the nuptial ceremony &c. He is one of the eight Lokapālas or guardians of the world and especi- ally the Lord of the south-east quarter. He appears in the progress of mythological personification as a son of Angiras, as a king of the Pitṛs or Manes, as a Marut, as a grand- son of Śanḍila, as one of the seven Sages or Ṛṣis during the reign of Tāmasa or the fourth Manu, as a star and as a Ṛṣi or inspired author of several vaidic hymns. <sup>3</sup> The fire of the stomach, the digestive faculty. <sup>4</sup> Bile. <sup>5</sup> Gold. <sup>6</sup> A plant of which the fruit has escharotic properties (Seme- carpus anacardium). See {#BallAtaka#}. <sup>7</sup> Another plant (Plum- bago zeylanica). See {#citraka#}. <sup>8</sup> Another plant (Plumbago rosea). <sup>9</sup> (In arithmetic sometimes used as) a denomination of the numeral three (because there are three sacred fires; see above). E. {#aNg#}, uṇ. aff. {#ni#}, the nasal of the root being dropped.
{#agnika#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) An insect of a scarlet color, the lady-bird. E. {#agni#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#} (resembling fire).
{#agnikaRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RaH#}) A spark. E. {#agni#} and {#kaRa#}.
{#agnikarman#}¦ Tatpur. ({#-rma#}) <sup>1</sup> The action of Agni or fire. <sup>2</sup> (In medicine.) Application of fire for cure, cauterization. E. {#agni#} and {#karman#}.
{#agnikArikA#}¦ Tatpur. ({#-kA#}) Kindling or exciting the sacri- ficial fire, by throwing clarified butter &c. into it. E. {#agni#} and {#kArikA#}.
{#agnikArya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-ryam#}) The same as {#agnikArikA#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#kArya#}.
{#agnikAzWa#}¦ Tatp. n. ({#-zWam#}) Agallochum. See {#aguru#}. E. {#agni#} and {#kAzWa#}.
{#agnikukkuwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-waH#}) A firebrand, a lighted wisp of straw. E. {#agni#} and {#kukkuwa#}.
{#agnikuRqa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Rqam#}) A hole in the ground or an enclosed space on the surface for receiving and preserving consecrated fire. E. {#agni#} and {#kuRqa#}.
{#agnikumAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A particular preparation of medicaments. E. {#agni#} and {#kumAra#}.
{#agniketu#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tuH#}) The name of a Rakshas or demon. E. {#agni#} and {#ketu#}.
{#agnikoRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RaH#}) The south-east, the quarter ruled or protected by Agni. E. {#agni#} and {#koRa#}.
{#agnikriyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-yA#}) A religious act as obsequies &c. performed by the means of fire, particularly the burning of a corpse. E. {#agni#} and {#kriyA#}.
{#agnikrIqA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-qA#}) Illuminations, fireworks, &c. E. {#agni#} and {#krIqA#}.

{#agnigarBa#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-rBaH-rBA-rBam#}) Being pregnant with fire. <div n="P">II. 1. m. ({#-rBaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The sun-stone, crystal, or a fabulous gem; supposed to contain and impart solar heat. See {#sUryakAnta#}. <sup>2</sup> A plant, see {#agnijAra#}. 2. f. ({#-rBA#}) The name of another plant. See {#mahAjyotizmatI#}. E. {#agni#} and {#garBa#}.

{#agnicayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Arranging the fire-place, a sa- crificial ceremony, viz. arranging on a piece of ground of merely a fathom's length, which must have been previously ploughed, consecrated bricks (see {#izwakA#}), so as to make them to imitate the shape of a bird. There are five or in some case, six such chitis (q. v.) required for receiving the sacrificial fire. E. {#agni#} (in the sense of the dat.) and {#cayana#}.
{#agnicit#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#cit#}) One who has arranged a sa- crificial fire-place. See {#agnicayana#}. <div n="P">II. ind. (in the Vedas.) Like Agni. E. {#agni#} and {#cit#}.
{#agniciti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}). The same as {#agnicayana#}. E. {#agni#} and {#citi#}.
{#agnicityA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tyA#}). The same as {#agnicayana#}. E. {#agni#} and {#cityA#}.
{#agnicitvat#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-tvAn-tvatI-tvat#}) Having householders who have arranged and consecrated a sacrificial fire-place (as a village, a sacrifice &c.). E. {#agnicit#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.

{#agnija#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-jaH-jA-jam#}) <sup>1</sup> Produced by fire. <sup>2</sup> Digestive. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-jaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of Viṣṇu. <sup>2</sup> A plant used in me- dicine, of stimulant properties. See {#agnijAta, agnijAra#}, {#agnijAla#}. E. {#agni#} and {#ja#}.
{#agnijanman#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-nmA#}) A name of Skanda, the god of war. See also {#agniBU#}. E. {#agni#} and {#janman#}.
{#agnijAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) and m. ({#-taH#}) The same as {#agnija#}. E. {#agni#} and {#jAta#}.
{#agnijAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A medicinal plant. See {#agnija#}. E. {#agni#} and {#jAra#}.
{#agnijAla#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-laH#}) A medicinal plant. See {#agnija#}. E. {#agni#} and {#jAla#}.

{#agnijihvA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-hvA#}) <sup>1</sup> A tongue of Agni, a flame of fire. (There are seven tongues of Agni. See {#hiraRyA, kanakA#}, {#raktA, kfzRA, vasupraBA, atiraktA, bahurUpA#}). <sup>2</sup> A medicinal plant. See {#lANgalI#} and {#lANgalikI#}. E. {#agni#} and {#jihvA#}.

{#agnijvAlA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-lA#}) <sup>1</sup> A flame of fire. <sup>2</sup> A plant bear- ing red blossoms used by dyers (Grislea tomentosa, Rox.). <sup>3</sup> Another plant, commonly Jalapippalī. E. {#agni#} and {#jvAlA#}, from the fiery colour of its blossoms.

{#agnitejas#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-jAH-jAH-jaH#}) Having the power of Agni or fire. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-jAH#}) Name of a son of Pulaha, one of the seven Ṛṣis during the reign of the 11th (a future) Manu. E. {#agni#} and {#tejas#}.
{#agnitraya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-yam#}) The aggregate of the three fires &c. See {#agnitretA#}. E. {#agni#} and {#traya#}.
{#agnitretA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tA#}) The aggregate of the three fires maintained by the Brahman householder, viz. the Gārha- patya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇa, qq. vv. E. {#agni#} and {#tretA#}.
{#agnida#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-daH-dA-dam#}) <sup>1</sup> Setting on fire, in- cendiary. <sup>2</sup> Supplying with fire. <sup>3</sup> Stomachic, tonic, di- gestive. E. {#agni#} and {#da#}.

{#agnidagDa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-gDaH-gDA-gDam#}) Burnt with fire. <div n="P">II. m. pl. ({#-gDAH#}) The name of a particular class of Pitṛs or Manes, of such who when alive, kept up the household flame and presented oblations with fire. E. {#agni#} and {#dagDa#}. In the latter sense it would seem that the word has been taken as a Bahuvrīhi.
{#agnidatta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ttaH#}) The name of a prince. E. {#agni#} and {#datta#}.
{#agnidamanI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-nI#}) A medicinal plant of narcotic properties (Solanum jacquini). See {#kaRWakArikA#}. E. {#agni#} (bile) and {#damanI#} (what tames).
{#agnidiS#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dik#}) The south-east quarter, of which Agni is the regent. E. {#agni#} and {#diS#}.
{#agnidIpana#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nI-nam#}) Producing appetite, stomachic. E. {#agni#} and {#dIpana#}.

{#agnidIpta#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) <sup>1</sup> Blazing, on fire. <sup>2</sup> Digestive. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-ptA#}) The name of a plant. See {#mahAjyotizmatI#}. E. {#agni#} and {#dIpta#}.

{#agnideva#}¦ I. Karmadh. m. ({#-vaH#}) Agni, the god of fire. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. 1. m. ({#-vaH#}) A worshipper of fire. 2. f. ({#-vA#}) A name of the third lunar mansion, identified with the Ple- iades: Agni being the ruling deity of the constellation. Also {#agnidevatA#}. E. {#agni#} and {#deva#}.

{#agnidevatya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-tyaH-tyA-tyam#}) Belonging or referring to the divinity of Agni or fire. (This word occurs also, but less correctly, in the form of {#agnidEvatya#}). E. {#agnidevatA#}, taddh. aff. {#yat#}.
{#agnidEvata#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Belonging to Agni as divinity, referring to the divinity of Agni. E. {#agni#} and {#dEvata#}.
{#agnidEvatya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-tyaH-tyA-tyam#}) See {#agnidevatya#}.
{#agninakzatra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-tram#}) The third lunar mansion. E. {#agni#} and {#nakzatra#}.
{#agninayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) See {#agnipraRayana#}. E. {#agni#} and {#nayana#}.
{#agniniryAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) The name of a plant, also {#agnijAra#}. E. {#agni#} and {#niryAsa#}.
{#agnipakva#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kvaH-kvA-kvam#}) Cooked or dressed with fire. E. {#agni#} and {#pakva#}.
{#agnipada#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-dam#}) The name of a plant. (?) E. {#agni#} and {#pada#}.
{#agniparicCada#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-daH#}) The implements and apparatus used in oblations to fire. E. {#agni#} and {#paricCada#}.
{#agnipariDAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Surrounding the sacrificial fire with the paridhis (see {#pariDi#}) or wooden frames covered with skin. E. {#agni#} and {#pariDAna#}.

{#agniparIkzA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kzA#}) Ordeal by fire, as formerly practised by walking through it, or as subsequently prac- tised, by dipping the hand into boiling oil, holding a heated iron &c. E. {#agni#} and {#parIkzA#}.
{#agniparvata#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) A volcano. E. {#agni#} and {#parvata#}.

{#agnipraRayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Carrying forth the sacrificial fire, a ceremony occurring in several sacrifices, as in the Jyotiṣṭoma, the Darśapūrṇamāsa, the Chāturmāsya. It consists in taking the fire from the Prāchīnavanśa (q. v.) Manḍapa, a building erected in the centre of the Dārśikī Vedi (q. v.) and carrying it to the Āgnīdhra (q. v.) Man- ḍapa, which stands in the Saumikī Vedi (q. v.). E. {#agni#} and {#praRayana#}.
{#agnipraveSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}) Entering the fire, esp. self im- molation by a widow upon the pyre of her deceased hus- band. E. {#agni#} and {#praveSa#}. Also {#agnipraveSana#} n. ({#-nam#}).
{#agniprastara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Fire-stone, flint, or any stone producing fire. E. {#agni#} and {#prastara#}.
{#agnibAhu#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-huH#}) See {#agnivAhu#}.
{#agniBa#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-Bam#}) Gold. E. {#agni#} and {#BA#} (having the lustre of fire, brilliant as fire).
{#agniBu#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Bu#}) See the following.

{#agniBU#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-BUH#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of Skanda, the Hindu deity of war. See {#kArttikeya, skanda, agnijanman#}. (Śiva hav- ing cast his seed into flame, for the purpose of generating a warrior, able to subdue Tāraka, a demon, Skanda was produced.) <sup>2</sup> (In arithmetic sometimes used to denote) the numeral six (Skanda having six faces). <div n="P">II. n. ({#-Bu#}) Water (rain being generated, according to the Hindu belief from the clouds which are produced by the smoke of fire). E. {#agni#} and {#BU#} (generating from).

{#agniBUti#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-tiH#}) A proper name, viz. one of the pupils of the last Tīrthakara, belonging to the family of Gotama and being one of the eleven chiefs of the gaṇas or companies of the Jaina Ṛṣis. E. {#agni#} and {#BUti#} (super- human power): equal to Agni.
{#agnimaRi#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RiH#}) The sun-stone. E. {#agni#} and {#maRiH#} brilliant as fire. See {#agnigarBa#} and {#sUryakAnta#}.

{#agnimat#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-mAn-matI-mat#}) <sup>1</sup> Having fire in general. <sup>2</sup> Having and maintaining a consecrated fire. <sup>3</sup> Having a good digestion. E. {#agni#} taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#agnimanTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nTaH#}) A small tree (Premna integrifolia). See {#maRikArikA#}. E. {#agni#} and {#manTa#} (churning), because fire is produced by friction of two pieces of its wood.
{#agnimanTana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Producing fire by friction of two pieces of wood. See the preceding. E. {#agni#} and {#manTana#}.
{#agnimanTanIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Referring to {#agnimanTana#} q. v. E. The preceding, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#agnimAWara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) The name of an expounder of the Rigveda. E. {#agni#} and {#mAWara#}.
{#agnimAndya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-ndyam#}) Languor of the digestive organs, the want of appetite or digestion. E. {#agni#} and {#mAndya#}.

{#agnimAruti#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-tiH#}) A name of the saint Agastya. E. {#agni#} fire, i. e. the fire of the stomach, the digestive fa- culty, and {#mAruti#} a name of Hanumat; because the saint could digest as well as the monkey: the epithet alludes to a story of his devouring and digesting Vātāpi, a demon, who had assumed the form of a sheep.
{#agnimitra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-traH#}) The name of a prince of the Sunga dynasty. E. {#agni#} and {#mitra#}.
{#agniminDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nDaH#}) The priest who kindles or at- tends the fire. See {#agnID#}. E. {#agni#} and {#inDa#}, with āgama {#mum#} (or better {#agni#} in the acc. and {#inDa#}).

{#agnimuKa#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. ({#-KaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A deity. <sup>2</sup> A Brāhmaṇa. <sup>3</sup> A plant (Plumbago zeylanica). <sup>4</sup> Marking nut (Semecarpus anacardium). <sup>5</sup> A particular medicinal preparation promo- tive of digestion and appetite. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-KI#}) <sup>1</sup> Marking nut (Semecarpus anacardium). <sup>2</sup> Another plant, see {#lANgalikI#}. E. {#agni#} and {#muKa#}.
{#agniyuta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) Name of a Ṛṣi or sage, author of a hymn of the Rigveda. E. {#agni#} and {#yuta#}.
{#agniyojana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) A sacrificial act, viz. making the fire to join or to light up with a powerful blaze, by throw- ing ājya or clarified butter into it. E. {#agni#} and {#yojana#}.
{#agnirakzaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) Maintenance of a sacred fire; preserving a fire in a family for perpetuity, which supplies that lighted on occasions of worship. E. {#agni#} and {#rakzaRa#}.
{#agnirajas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-jAH#}) An insect of a scarlet colour. E. {#agni#} and {#rajas#}. Also {#agniraja#} m. ({#-jaH#}).
{#agniruhA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-hA#}) The name of a plant, called Mān- sarohiṇī. E. {#agni#} and {#ruha#}, fem. aff. {#wAp#}.
{#agnirohiRI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-RI#}) Hard, inflammatory swelling in the axilla, one of the minor diseases or {#kzudraroga#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#rohin#}, fem. aff. {#NIp#}.
{#agniloka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) The world of Agni. E. {#agni#} and {#loka#}.
{#agnivat#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-vAn-vatI-vat#}). See {#agnimat#}. E. {#agni#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}. <div n="P">II. ind. Like Agni or fire. E. {#agni#}, taddh. aff. {#vati#}.
{#agnivarcas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-rcAH#}) The name of a pupil of Sūta, a teacher of the Purāṇas. E. {#agni#} and {#varcas#}.

{#agnivarRa#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) <sup>1</sup> Having the colour of fire. <sup>2</sup> Having the property of fire, hot, scalding, scorching. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-rRaH#}) The name of a prince, the son of Sudarśana. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-rRA#}) A kind of strong liquor. E. {#agni#} and {#varRa#}.
{#agnivarDaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA#} or {#-kI-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> Tonic, stomachic. <sup>2</sup> Feeding or exciting fire. E. {#agni#} and {#varDaka#}.

{#agnivarDana#}¦ Tatpur. I. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Exciting fire. <sup>2</sup> Improving the appetite. II. m. ({#-naH#}) A stomachic or any thing im- proving the appetite. E. {#agni#} and {#varDana#}.

{#agnivallaBa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-BaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A plant (Shorea robusta). <sup>2</sup> Resin, pitch, the resinous and fragrant exudation of the Shorea robusta. E. {#agni#} and {#vallaBa#}, from its exciting or befriend- ing fire.
{#agnivARa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RaH#}) A fiery arrow, a rocket. E. {#agni#} and {#vARa#}.
{#agnivAha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) Smoke. E. {#agni#} and {#vAha#}.

{#agnivAhu#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-huH#}) Smoke. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. ({#-huH#}) A proper name of <sup>1</sup> the son of Pri- yavrata by Kāmyā, and <sup>2</sup> one of the ten sons of Svāyam- bhuva or the first Manu. E. {#agni#} and {#vAhu#}. Also {#agnibAhu#}.

{#agnivimocana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) A sacrificial act, viz. with- drawing the fuel so as to diminish the fire after its having been made to rise in a large blaze. See {#agniyojana#}. E. {#agni#} and {#vimocana#}.
{#agnivisarpa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rpaH#}) Pain occasioned by the inflam- mation of a tumour. E. {#agni#} and {#visarpa#}.

{#agniviharaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) Removing the sacrificial fire, a ceremony in the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice which consists in taking the fire from the Āgnīdhra Manḍapa (q. v.) and placing it in the Sadas (q. v.), another Manḍapa in the Saumikī Vedi (q. v.). E. {#agni#} and {#viharaRa#}.
{#agnivIja#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-jam#}) Gold. E. {#agni#} and {#vIja#}.
{#agnivIrya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-ryam#}) Gold. E. {#agni#} and {#vIrya#}.
{#agnivfdDi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dDiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Improved digestion or appetite. <sup>2</sup> Increase of fire. E. {#agni#} and {#vfdDi#}.
{#agniveSa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-SaH#}) Name of one of the oldest medi- cal authorities in India. He is called also Hutāśaveśa and Bhadrakāpya. E. {#agni#} and {#veSa#}.
{#agniSaraRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) The house or place where the sacred fire is kept. E. {#agni#} and {#SaraRa#}.
{#agniSAla#}¦ Tatpur. f. n. ({#-lA-lam#}) The house where the sa- cred fire is kept. E. {#agni#} and {#SAlA#}, the latter part of the compound remaining fem. or becoming neuter.

{#agniSiKa#}¦ I. Bahuvr. 1. m. f. n. ({#-KaH-KA-Kam#}) Having the splendour or the heat of fire. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-KaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A lamp. <sup>2</sup> An arrow. <sup>3</sup> A fiery arrow, a rocket. <sup>4</sup> The safflower plant (Carthamus tinctorius). <sup>5</sup> The name of the father of Vararuchi. <div n="P">3. m. n. ({#-KaH-Kam#}) Saffron, the plant and die. <div n="P">4. n. ({#-Kam#}) Gold. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. f. ({#-KA#}) <sup>1</sup> Flame. <sup>2</sup> A plant (Gloriosa su- perba). <sup>3</sup> A medicinal plant (Menispermum cordifolium). E. {#agni#} and {#SiKA#}.
{#agniSeKara#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-ram#}) Saffron. E. {#agni#} and {#SeKara#}.
{#agnizwut#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zwut#}) <sup>1</sup> The name of the first day of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice (q. v.). <sup>2</sup> The name of a day of the Sattra Pañchadaśarātra. E. {#agni#} and {#stut#}.
{#agnizwuB#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zwup#}) A proper name, the son of the sixth Manu, Chākṣuṣa, by Naḍvalā, also called Agni- ṣṭoma. E. {#agni#} and {#stuB#}.

{#agnizwoma#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> The name of a sacrifice or rather a series of offerings to fire for five days, to be celebrated in the spring. It is the first and principal part of the Jyo- tiṣṭoma, one of the great sacrifices in which especially the juice of the Soma plant is offered for the purpose of ob- [Page013-a+ 56] taining Swarga or heaven. It is nitya or obligatory for the complete performance of the Jyotiṣṭoma and so far considered sometimes identical with it, while the other six parts or Somasansthās of this sacrifice are considered as kāmya and anitya, voluntary and supererogatory. (See {#atyagnizwoma, ukTya, zoqaSin, atirAtra, aptoryAma#} and {#vAjapeya#}.) The Agniṣṭoma consists of three distinct parts or savanas, the prātaḥsavana with five, the mādhyandina- savana with five and the tṛtīya-savana with two stotras. <sup>2</sup> The name of the Sāman or Sāmaveda verse called Yajnā- yajnīya (which begins with the words {#yajYAyajYA vo agnaye#} &c. see Sāmaveda I. 1. 4. 1.), because it closes the ceremonies of the Agniṣṭoma in the tṛtīya-savana. <sup>3</sup> The name of the first day in the Sattra Pañchadaśarātra. <sup>5</sup> A proper name, the son of the sixth Manu, Chākṣuṣa, by Naḍvalā, also Agniṣṭubh. <sup>6</sup> A species of the Soma plant. E. {#agni#} and {#stoma#}.
{#agnizwomayAjin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jI#}) One who has performed the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice. E. {#agnizwoma#} and {#yAjin#}.

{#agnizWa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-zWaH-zWA-zWam#}) Placed in, on or by the fire. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-zWaH#}) <sup>1</sup> An iron frying pan. <sup>2</sup> The eleventh yūpa or sacrificial post of the 21 posts in the Aśvamedha sacri- fice, that post to which the seventeen animals are tied. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-zWA#}) That corner of the eight corners of the yūpa or sacrificial post which is near the fire. E. {#agni#} and {#sTa#}.

{#agnizvAtta#}¦ Tatpur. m. pl. ({#-ttAH#}) Demigods or manes to whom funeral oblations are presented; a sort of manes who when alive did not maintain their domestic fires nor offer burnt sacrifices. According to some they live in the Somaloka and are sons of Marīchi and progenitors especially of the gods; according to others they are residents of the Virāja- loka, sons of Pulastya, the manes of the demigods and demons, and parents of Pīvarī. Also written {#agnisvAtta#}. E. {#agnisva#} ({#agni#} and {#sva#}) and {#Atta#} (who are obtained by what belongs or is given to Agni) or {#agnizu#} (in or by obla- tions to fire) and {#Atta#} (obtained viz. invoked).

{#agnisaMskAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Consecration of fire, making the three fires (see {#agni#}) fit for sacrificial purposes by the Agnyādhāna, the Pavamāneṣṭi (q. v.) and other prepara- tory rites which, themselves, are performed with non-con- secrated fire. <sup>2</sup> The completion of any essential rite by worship with fire, especially the burning of the dead body as an essential rite of the Hindu religion. E. {#agni#} and {#saMskAra#}.
{#agnisaYcaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) The same as {#agnicayana#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#saYcaya#}.
{#agnisaKa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-KaH#}) The wind. E. {#agni#} and {#saKi#}, sa- māsta aff. {#wac#}.

{#agnisamBava#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Originating from fire. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-vaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Wild safflower. <sup>2</sup> The juice or essence of the body, lymph. E. {#agni#} and {#samBava#}.
{#agnisahAya#}¦ m. ({#-yaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The wind. <sup>2</sup> A wild pigeon. E. {#agni#} and {#sahAya#}.

{#agnisAkzikamaryAda#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-daH#}) One who binds himself [Page013-b+ 56] with a vow in taking fire as a witness, esp. one who takes the vow of conjugal fidelity. E. {#agnisAkzika#} and {#maryAdA#}.
{#agnisAt#}¦ ind. Completely to fire. Only in composition with {#as, BU#} or {#kf#}, i. e. to be reduced or to reduce ‘(completely to fire). E. {#agni#}, taddh. aff. {#sAti#}.
{#agnisAra#}¦ n. ({#-ram#}) A medicinal application to the eyes, a collyrium from the calx of brass. E. {#agni#} and {#sAra#}.
{#agnisAvarRi#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rRiH#}) A proper name, one of the fourteen Manus who preside successively over the fourteen Manvantaras of the Kalpa. E. {#agni#} and {#sAvarRi#}.
{#agnisiMha#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-haH#}) A proper name, the father of the seventh black Vāsudeva (q. v.). E. {#agni#} and {#siMha#}.
{#agnisiMhanandana#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-naH#}) A proper name, the son of Agnisinha and the seventh black Vāsudeva (q. v.). E. {#agni-#} {#siMha#} and {#nandana#}.
{#agnistoka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) A spark. E. {#agni#} and {#stoka#}.
{#agnisvAtta#}¦ See {#agnizvAtta#}.
{#agnihotf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tA#}). See {#agnihotrin#}. E. {#agni#} and {#hotf#}.

{#agnihotra#}¦ I. Bahuvr. n. ({#-tram#}) <sup>1</sup> A sacrificial ceremony which consists in making oblations to fire, of milk (payas), curds (dadhi), sour gruel (yavāgū), clarified butter (ghṛta), boiled rice (odana), grain (tanḍula), the juice of the Soma plant, flesh, sesamum oil (taila) and kidney beans (māṣa), or as is practised at present, merely of milk, sesamum oil and sour gruel. There are two kinds, 1. the nitya, perpetual, ‘during the whole life’ or that Agnihotra which is addressed to Agni every evening at sunset and to Sūrya every morning at sunrise; and 2. the kāmya, voluntary or the Agnihotra which occurs only occasionally and which is performed for the attainment of some specific object, as the Mṛtāgnihotra or the Māsāgnihotra in the beginning of the Sattra Kun- ḍapāyināmayana. <sup>2</sup> The same as {#agnyADAna#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#hotra#}, sc. {#karman#} ‘an act in which oblations are made to Agni’. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. m. ({#-traH#}) <sup>1</sup> Fire. <sup>2</sup> Havis or clarified butter. E. {#agni#} and {#hotra#}.
{#agnihotrahavaRI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-RI#}) A wooden vessel used in sa- crifices for making libations with clarified butter. E. {#agni-#} {#hotra#} (clarified butter) and {#havanI#}.

{#agnihotrin#}¦ m. ({#-trI#}) <sup>1</sup> One who has performed the Agni- hotra q. v. <sup>2</sup> The same as {#agnyAhita#}. <sup>3</sup> The same as {#agni-#} {#cit#}. <sup>4</sup> One who possesses or keeps a sacrificial fire. Some- times read {#agnihotf#}. E. {#agnihotra#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#agnID#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gnIt#}) The priest who kindles the fire; he is one of the three priests who are subordinate to the Brahman or the Ṛtvij performing the ceremonial of the Ṛg-, Yajur- and Sāmaveda, (see {#brahman, brAhmaRAcCaMsin#} and {#potf#}) and one of the four priests who receive the third division of the Dakṣiṇā. (See {#nezwf, pratihartf#} and {#acCA-#} {#vAka#}.) E. {#agni#} and {#iD#} (instead of {#inD#}).

{#agnIDra#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-DraH#}) <sup>1</sup> A proper name: the son of Priyavrata and Kāmyā, a king of Jambudvīpa; one of the ten sons of the first Manu, Svāyambhuva. <sup>2</sup> The same as {#agnID#} q. v. In this meaning the word seems to be a misspelling of {#AgnIDra#}. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-DrI#}) Kindling or exciting the sacrificial fire by [Page014-a+ 56] throwing clarified butter &c. into it. See {#AgnIDrI#} which seems to be the more correct form of this word. E. {#agni#} and {#iDra#} (from {#inD#}, uṇ. aff. {#kran#}).
{#agnInDana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Kindling or exciting a sacrificial fire. E. {#agni#} and {#inDana#}. See {#agnikArikA#}.
{#agnIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Fiery, relating to Agni (in the different meanings of this word). E. {#agni#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#agnIzoma#}¦ Dvandva. m. du. ({#-mO#}) Agni and Soma. E. {#agni#} and {#soma#}.

{#agnIzomapraRayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Carrying forth the fire and the Soma; a ceremony in the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice which takes place after the Vaisarjana homa (q. v.) and consists in taking the fire from the Prāchīnavaṇśa (q. v.) Manḍapa and carrying it to the Āgnīdhra (q. v.) Manḍapa, and in the same time taking the Soma from the Prāchīnavaṇśa and carrying it to the Havirdhāna Manḍapa, a building erected in the Saumikī Vedi (q. v.). See also {#agnipraRayana#}. E. {#agnIzoma#} and {#praRayana#}.
{#agnIzomIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Belonging or sacred to Agni and Soma. E. {#agnIzoma#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.

{#agnIzomIyanirvApa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) A ceremony in the Dar- śapūrṇamāsa sacrifice which is performed on the day of the full moon and consists in making libations with the Puroḍāśa (q. v.) or cake sacred to Agni and Soma and previously fried in eleven kapālas or bowls. See {#agnI-#} {#zomIyEkAdaSakapAla#}. E. {#agnIzomIya#} and {#nirvApa#}.

{#agnIzomIyapaSu#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-SuH#}) One of the three prin- cipal paśus or sacrificial animals in the Jyotiṣṭoma sacri- fice. (See also {#savanIyapaSu#} and {#anubanDyapaSu#}.) It is a goat or according to one school, a sheep, sacred to Agni and Soma, the procedings with which take place on the day called Aupavasathya or the fourth of the Agniṣṭoma (q. v.). E. {#agnIzomIya#} and {#paSu#}.
{#agnIzomIyapaSvanuzWAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The procedings with the Agnīṣomīyapaśu. See {#agnIzomIyapaSu#}. E. {#agnIzomI-#} {#yapaSu#} and {#anuzWAna#}.

{#agnIzomIyapuroqASa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-SaH#}) The Puroḍāśa (q. v.) with which libations are made during the Agnīṣomīyayāga (q. v.) after having been baked in eleven kapālas or bowls. E. {#agnIzomIya#} and {#puroqASa#}.

{#agnIzomIyayAga#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-gaH#}) One of the three yāgas or sacrificial acts of which consists the Pūrṇamāsa or the latter part of the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifice. (See also {#AgneyayAga#} and {#upAMSuyAjayAga#}.)

{#agnIzomIyEkAdaSakapAla#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-laH#}) The Puroḍāśa (q. v.) or cake which is offered to Agni and Soma in the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifice after having been baked in eleven kapālas or bowls. See also {#agnIzomIyapuroqASa#}. E. {#agnI-#} {#zomIya#} and {#ekAdaSakapAla#}.
{#agnIzomya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}). The same as {#agnIzomIya#}. E. {#agnIzoma#}, taddh. aff. {#yat#}.
{#agnyaBAva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Loss or extinction of the sa- cred fire. <sup>2</sup> Loss of appetite. E. {#agni#} and {#aBAva#}.

{#agnyastra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-stram#}) Fire-arms; in poetry, it is usually applied to a superhuman power over the element of fire, but occasionally indicates, apparently, a rocket. E. {#agni#} and {#astra#}.
{#agnyAgAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) A fire-temple; a chamber or build- ing where the sacred fire is kept. E. {#agni#} and {#AgAra#}.

{#agnyADAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The placing of the fire on the ground previously prepared for it (see {#agnicayana#}); a cere- mony which is necessary to make the Āhavanīya and the other sacred fires (see {#agni#}) fit for sacrificial use and is fol- lowed by the Pavamāneṣtis (q. v.). See {#agnisaMskAra#}. The act takes place in the spring, if the person belongs to the cast of the Brāhmaṇas, in the hot season or grīṣma if he is a Kshatriya, in the autumn or śarad if he is a Vaiśya and is performed once for all, to serve all future purposes. E. {#agni#} and {#ADAna#}.
{#agnyADeya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-yam#}) The same as {#agnyADAna#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#ADeya#}.

{#agnyAlaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A place in which consecrated fire is kept. <sup>2</sup> A hole, with compartments of prescribed di- mensions and shape, for the several sacred fires. E. {#agni#} and {#Alaya#}.
{#agnyAhita#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-taH#}) A householder who has per- formed the ceremony of the {#agnyADAna#} q. v. Also {#Ahi-#} {#tAgni#}. E. {#agni#} and {#Ahita#}.
{#agnyAhiti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) The same as {#agnyADAna#} q. v. E. {#agni#} and {#Ahiti#}.
{#agnyutpAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) A fiery meteor, a falling star, a comet. E. {#agni#} and {#utpAta#}.

{#aNga#}¦ I. Ind. (see {#nipAta#}.) <sup>1</sup> A vocative particle implying <sup>a.</sup> solicitation, equivalent to the English ‘do’, in phrases as ‘do give’ &c. <sup>b.</sup> abuse, <sup>c.</sup> joy. <sup>2</sup> A particle implying con- firmation, as ‘indeed, certainly’, or putting stress on the word with which it is connected. <sup>3</sup> Again, further, the rather. <sup>4</sup> Quick. <sup>5</sup> A particle of assent used in composition with {#kf#} and its derivatives, {#I#} being substituted for the ter- minating vowel as in {#aNgIkaraRa#} &c. (See {#gati#}.) <div n="P">II. n. ({#-Ngam#}) <sup>1</sup> A limb or member. <sup>2</sup> The body. <sup>3</sup> A part or division of a whole. <sup>4</sup> A division of Hindu learning, com- prehending especially such science as is considered depend- ant upon the Vedas, hence also called Vedāṅga; works on six subjects come under this description, viz. {#SikzA#} or pronunciation, {#vyAkaraRa#} or grammar, {#Candas#} or prosody, {#nirukta#} or explanation of obscure terms, {#kalpa#} or description of religious rites and {#jyotiza#} or astronomy. Also the Jainas call the twelve divisions of their holy work Gaṇipiṭaka, Angas. <sup>5</sup> An inferior or secondary part of a whole. <sup>6</sup> (In rhetoric.) An incidental passion or figure, illustrative of, but subordinate to the main subject of the description. <sup>7</sup> All the dramatis personae of a play, except the hero and he- roine, the body of the characters. <sup>8</sup> (In grammar.) The theme or that part of a word in general, to which the affix [Page018-a+ 56] is attached, whether the affix be one of inflexion or deri- vation. <sup>9</sup> An expedient, a means of success. <sup>10</sup> Mind, un- derstanding. <sup>11</sup> A denomination of the numeral six (this being the number of the Vedāṅgas). (In this sense the word is mostly used as a plural.) <sup>2</sup> A proper name: the son of Ūru by Āgneyī and grandson to Chākṣuṣa or the sixth Manu, a descendant of Atri; the eldest son of the king Bali. E. {#aNg#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">IV. m. f. n. ({#-NgaH-NgA-Ngam#}) <sup>1</sup> Having limbs, a body &c. <sup>2</sup> Near, proximate. E. {#aNga#} (see II.), taddh. aff. {#ac#}.

{#aNgiras#}¦ I. m. sing. ({#-rAH#}) The proper name of a Maharshi, a great Ṛṣi or saint who is the reputed author of many vaidik hymns, but who is mentioned also in a subse- [Page020-a+ 56] quent period as one of the inspired legislators of India and as the author of an astronomical work. The various legends connected with his life seem to have been occasioned by the word {#aNgiras#} coming from the same radical as, and its sound recalling that of, {#agni#}, fire (q. v.). Hence we find Angiras sometimes either as an epithet or as the father of Agni, and the Saint himself connected chiefly with such hymns as are addressed to Agni, to Indra or to dei- ties of a kindred description: a portion of the fourth Veda, the Atharvan, reports him also as an expounder of the Brahmavidyā (q. v.) or the sacred knowledge, that had been imparted to him by Satyavāha, a descendant of Bharadvāja. (See {#aNgir#}.) Though Angiras, as may be concluded from his name being connected with the authorship of a great por- tion of the sacred Hindu literature, appears to have been one of the oldest civilizers of India, no historical date is to be obtained from the epic or pauranik literature where the vaidik legends of his life are merely amplified; there he is named as one of the Prajāpatis or progenitors of mankind engendered, according to some by Manu, accord- ing to others by Brahmā himself, either with the female half of his body or from his mouth or from the space between his eye-brows. As such he is considered also as one of the seven Ṛṣis who preside over the reign of the first Manu or Svāyambhuva. He is called, besides, the priest of the Gods, the Lord of the sacrifice &c. Sometimes he is considered as a son of Uru by Āgneyī, the daughter of Agni. His daughters are the Ṛchas (or vaidik hymns) and also, Śaśvatī, Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, Anumati; his sons are Samvarta, the manes called Havishmats, Utathya, Bṛhaspati, Mārkanḍeya; his wives, Smṛti (traditional science), two daughters of Daksha, Svadhā and Satī, and Śraddhā, the daughter of the sage Kardama. As an astro- nomical personification he is Bṛhaspati himself or the regent of the planet Jupiter and presides over the sixth year of the cycle of sixty years. See also {#aTarvan#}. <div n="P">II. m. pl. ({#-rasaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The descendants of the former. In this capacity they share also in the nature of the legends attri- buted to Angiras. Angiras being the father of Agni, they are considered as descendants of Agni himself, who is also called the first of the Angirasas. Like Angiras, they occur in hymns addressed to the luminous deities and, at a later period, they become for the most part personifications of light, of luminous bodies, of divisions of time, of celestial phenomena and fires adapted to peculiar occasions as the full and change of the moon, or to particular rites as the Aśvamedha, Rājasūya, the Pākayajnas or sacrifices with food, obsequial and funeral fires, expiatory fires, and the like. Most of the authors of the hymns of the Rigveda are connected with them and in the Purāṇas mention is made of two tribes of the Angirasas which were Brāhmaṇas as well as Kshatriyas. <sup>2</sup> The hymns of the Atharvaveda. See also {#aTarvan#} pl. and {#aTarvANgiras#} pl. E. {#aNg#}, uṇ. aff. {#asi#} with āgama {#iruw#}, or, according to another authority, a Tatpur. composed of {#an#} (meaning {#anna#} food, from {#an#} kṛt aff. {#kvip#}) and {#giras#} (from {#gF#} to swallow) ‘devouring food’. The latter [Page020-b+ 56] etymology, apparently without any grammatical authority, would refer especially to {#aNgiras#} as epithet of Agni. See also {#aNgirastama#}. The plural {#aNgirasaH#} is considered, though without any etymological necessity, as the plural of the deriv. form {#ANgirasa#} with luk or elision of the affix.

{#aRuBA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-BA#}) Lightning. E. {#aRu#} and {#BA#}.

{#aRureRu#}¦ Karmadh. m. f. ({#-RuH-RuH#}) Small particles of dust, a mote in a sunbeam &c. E. {#aRu#} and {#reRu#}.

{#aRuSas#}¦ ind. In small pieces. E. {#aRu#}, taddh. aff. {#Sas#}.

{#aRW (aWi-BvAdi-udAtta-anudAttet)#}¦ r. 1st cl. ātm. ({#aRWate-#} {#AnaRWe-aRWitA#}.--p. p. {#aRWita#}) To go, to go to or towards. See {#aW#}.

E. {#am#}, uṇ. aff. {#qa#}.

{#aRqakowarapuzpI#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-zpI#}) A plant (perhaps Convol- vulus argenteus). See {#ajAntrI#}. Another reading of this word is {#antaHkoWarapuzpI#}. E. {#aRqa, kowara#} and {#puzpa#}.
{#aRqakoSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}). See the next.
{#aRqakoza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) The scrotum. E. {#aRqa#} and {#koSa#} or {#koza#}.
{#aRqakozaka#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) The scrotum. E. taddh. aff. {#kan#} added to the last.

{#aRqaja#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-jaH-jA-jam#}) Oviparous. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-jaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A bird. <sup>2</sup> A fish. <sup>3</sup> A serpent. <sup>4</sup> A lizard. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-jA#}) Musk. E. {#aRqa#} and {#ja#}.

{#aRqAlu#}¦ m. ({#-luH#}) A fish. E. {#aRqa#}, taddh. aff. {#Alu#}.

{#aRva#}¦ n. ({#-Rvam#}) The small hole of a filtre or sieve (in the Vedas; esp. in the plural). E. {#aRu#}, taddh. aff. {#a(?)#}.
{#aRvanta#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-ntaH#}) A question the object of which is the solution of some subtle or difficult point. E. {#aRu#} and {#anta#}.
{#aRvI#}¦ f. ({#-RvI#}) (ved.) A finger. See {#aRu#}.

{#ataTA#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-TAH#}) Different, not so as before. (ved.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#taTA#}.

{#ataTya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-TyaH-TyA-Tyam#}) Untrue, false, un- real. E. {#a#} neg. and {#taTya#}.

{#atandra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ndraH-ndrA-ndram#}) Unwearied, active, alert. E. {#a#} priv. and {#tandrA#}.
{#atandrita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unwearied, active, energetic. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tandrita#}.
{#atandrin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ndrI-ndriRI-ndri#}) Unwearied, ac- tive, alert. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tandrin#}.

{#atapta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) Cool, not heated. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tapta#}.

{#atarkita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unconsidered. <sup>2</sup> Un- expected, unweighed. {#atarkitam#} used as adv., unexpected- ly, suddenly. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tarkita#}.
{#atarkya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rkyaH-rkyA-rkyam#}) Unsearchable, in- comprehensible, inscrutable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tarkya#}.
{#atala#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-lam#}) A particular hell or division of the infernal regions, the portion immediately below the earth. E. {#a#} priv. and {#tala#}; ‘bottomless’.

{#atalaspfS#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-spfk#}). See the preceding. E. {#a#} neg. and {#tala-spfS#}.
{#atavyas#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vyAn-vyasI-vyaH#}) Not stronger, not very strong. (ved.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#tavyas#}.

If {#ati#}, in com- position with a nominal theme, constitutes a Tatpur. com- pound, it must either express a higher degree (f. i. in {#atirAjan#}, a superior or excellent king) or the sense of the word {#krAnta#} must be supplied after it and the latter part of the compound understood in the sense of the accu- [Page032-b+ 56] sative (f. i. in {#atiKawvaH#} which is explained as meaning {#atikrAntaH KawvAm#}). E. {#at#}, kṛt aff. {#in(?)#}.

({#-TaH-TA-Tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Incredible, unworthy of be- lief or trust. <sup>2</sup> Erring, deviating from the duties of a pro- fession or cast. E. {#ati#} and {#kaTA#}. {#atikAya#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Gigantic. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-yaH#}) The name of a Rākṣasa. E. {#ati#} and {#kAya#}.
{#atikutsita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Very low, much despised. E. {#ati#} and {#kutsita#}.

{#atikeSara#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-raH#}) The name of an aquatic plant (Trapa bispinosa). See {#kubjaka#}. E. {#ati#} and {#keSara#}.

{#atikrama#}¦ m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> Going over or beyond, lit. or fig. <sup>2</sup> Sur- passing, excelling, overcoming. <sup>3</sup> Transgressing. <sup>4</sup> Neglect, disregard, impropriety. <sup>5</sup> Contrariety, opposition. <sup>6</sup> A ground- less demand, an imposition. <sup>7</sup> A gallant attack, advance of an army in front of an enemy. {#atikramin#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-mI-miRI-mi#}) <sup>1</sup> Transgressing. <sup>2</sup> Ex- ceeding, surpassing. E. {#atikrama#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}, or {#kram#} with {#ati#}, kṛt aff. {#ini#}.

{#atikzipta#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) Thrown beyond, thrown outside &c. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-ptam#}) (In medicine.) ({#-nDaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A fragrant grass, lemon-grass (Andropo- gon schœnanthus). <sup>2</sup> Champac (Michelia champaca). <sup>3</sup> A kind of Jasmin. See {#mudgara#}. <sup>4</sup> Sulphur. E. {#ati#} and {#ganDa#}.
{#atiganDAlu#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-luH#}) The name of a creeper. See {#putradAtrI#}. E. {#ati#} and {#ganDAlu#}.
{#atigarbita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Very arrogant, very proud. E. {#ati#} and {#garbita#}.

{#aticCanda#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ndaH-ndA-ndam#}) Without desire, free from worldly desire. Also {#aticCandas#}. E. {#ati#} (sc. {#krAnta#}) and {#Canda#} (in the sense of the accusative), ‘having gone beyond desires’.

({#-ndAH-ndaH#}) The name of two classes of metres regulated by number and quantity, the first of which com- prises the classes {#atijagatI, SakvarI, atiSakvarI, azwi#}, {#atyazwi, Dfti, atiDfti#} (qq. vv.) and the second the classes {#kfti, prakfti, Akfti, vikfti, saNkfti, atikfti#} (or {#aBi-#} {#kfti#}), {#utkfti#} (qq. vv.). <div n="P">III. f. E. {#ati#} (sc. {#krAntA#}) and {#jagatI#} (in the sense of the accusative) ‘going beyond the metre {#jagatI#} q. v.’.

{#atijava#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-vaH#}) Extreme speed. <div n="P">II. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Marching fast or fleet. E. {#ati#} and {#java#}.
{#atijAgara#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Very wakeful, restless. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-raH#}) The black curlew. E. {#ati#} and {#jAgara#}.
{#atijAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Superior by birth (to the parents). E. {#ati#} and {#jAta#}.
{#atijIrRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) Very old. E. {#ati#} and {#jIrRa#}.
{#atiqIna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Very lofty or very rapid flight of birds. E. {#ati#} and {#qIna#}.

{#atitarAm#}¦ ind. <sup>1</sup> Far more, far better (with a word follow- ing in the ablative or fifth case). <sup>2</sup> Very much, excessively, exceedingly. <sup>3</sup> Far beyond, far above (with a word follow- ing in the accusative or second case). {#atitIkzRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kzRaH-kzRA-kzRam#}) Very pungent, sharp, hot or acrid. E. {#ati#} and {#tIkzRa#}.

{#atitfRRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RRaH-RRA-RRam#}) Very much hurt or injured. E. {#ati#} and {#tfRRa#}.
{#atitfpti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ptiH#}) Oversatisfaction, satisfying one's appetite too much. E. {#ati#} and {#tfpti#}.

(instead of {#atisyaH#}, {#atityO#} &c.).

{#atitvAn#}¦ Tatpur. The accus. in the plural of the preceding.
{#atitvAm#}¦ Tatpur. The accusative in the singular and dual of {#atitvam#}.

({#-TiH#}) <sup>1</sup> A proper name of a king of Ayodhyā, the son of Kuśa and grandson of Rāma. <sup>2</sup> The vaidik name of an attendant of Soma. (This latter meaning is more likely to be taken in a figurative sense, Soma being mentioned as the name of a king and Agni, Atithi, Śyena as those of his attendants). E. {#at#}, uṇ. aff. {#iTin#}. ({#atiTi#} in the mean- ing of ‘guest’ is also explained as a Bahuvr. ‘one who has no kind of {#tiTi#} or holy day, who may arrive any day’ or ‘one who does not sojourn a whole tithi, but only one single night’, or ‘one who is not steady (when {#tiTi#} is supposed to be a mutilated form of {#sTiti#})’; all these ex- planations are artificial.) <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. ({#-TiH#}) Wrath, anger. E. {#a#} priv. and {#tiTi#} ‘not restricted to a tithi, what may come at any time’.
{#atiTikriyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-yA#}) Hospitality considered as a religious duty. E. {#atiTi#} and {#kriyA#}.

{#atiTigva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gvaH#}) A proper name or a vaidik epithet of Divodāsa. (Properly meaning: ‘worthy to be approached by guests, hospitable’. E. {#atiTi#} and {#gva#} (from {#gam#}, uṇ. aff. {#qva#}).
{#atiTitva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) Hospitality. E. {#atiTi#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#atiTidveza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) Inhospitality. E. {#atiTi#} and {#dveza#}.

{#atiTisatkAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) The rite of hospitality, the hospitable treatment of a guest. E. {#atiTi#} and {#satkAra#}.
{#atiTisevA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-vA#}) Service of a guest, hospitality. E. {#atiTi#} and {#sevA#}.

E. {#ati#} and {#dagDa#}.

{#atidarSin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rSI-rSinI-rSi#}) Seeing very far. E. {#ati#} and {#darSin#}.
{#atidAtf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tA#}) A liberal man. E. {#ati#} and {#dAtf#}.
{#atidAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Munificence, giving largely. E. {#ati#} and {#dAna#}.

{#atidIrGa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rGaH-rGA-rGam#}) Too or very long (in time and space). E. {#ati#} and {#dIrGa#}.

{#atiduzkara#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA#} or {#-rI-ram#}) Very ar- duous, very difficult. E. {#ati#} and {#duzkara#}.

{#atidUra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-ram#}) Excessive distance. ({#atidUram#}, {#atidUrAt, atidUreRa#} and {#atidUre#}, especially in conjunc- tion with {#na#} are used adverbially ‘not very far off’.) E. {#ati#} and {#dUra#}.
{#atideva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) A superior god, one who surpasses the Gods. E. {#ati#} and {#deva#} (or according to others {#ati#}, sc. {#krAnta#}, and {#deva#}, in the sense of the accusative).

{#atideSa#}¦ m. ({#-SaH#}) A rule providing for something more than the ordinary or established rules (see {#pradeSa, upadeSa#}) pro- vide for and not comprehended by them; it may be either enjoined specially or derived from inference; if such a rule, in grammar, affects the form, gender &c. of a word, it is called {#rUpAtideSa, liNgAtideSa#} &c.; in philosophy atideśas of a general or comprehensive nature are called {#sAmAnyAtideSa#} and those restricted to a special case {#viSe-#} {#zAtideSa#}. {#atidoza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) A great fault. E. {#ati#} and {#doza#}.
{#atiDanvan#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-nvA#}) The proper name of a descen- dant of Śunaka. E. {#ati#} and {#Danvan#}.

(See <sup>1</sup> {#SArdUla#} or {#SArdUlavikrIqita#}, <sup>2</sup> {#meGavisPurjita#} or {#vismita#}, <sup>3</sup> {#paYcacAmara#}, <sup>4</sup> {#puzpadAman#}, <sup>5</sup> {#bimbA#}, <sup>6</sup> {#CAyA#}, <sup>7</sup> {#maka-#} {#randikA#}, <sup>8</sup> {#samudratawA#}, <sup>9</sup> {#surasA#}, <sup>10</sup> {#maRimaYjarI#}, <sup>11</sup> {#candramAlA#} or {#candra#}, <sup>12</sup> {#DavalANka#} or {#Davala#}, <sup>13</sup> {#samBu#}.) <sup>2</sup> (In arithmetic sometimes used to denote) the number nineteen. {#atiDenu#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-nuH-nuH-nu#}) Having excellent or a great many cows. E. {#ati#} and {#Denu#}.
{#atinAman#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-mA#}) A proper name, one of the seven Ṛṣis or Sages who preside over the reign of Chā- kshusha, the sixth Manu. E. {#ati#} and {#nAman#}.

{#atinidra#}¦ I. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-draH-drA-dram#}) One who sleeps inordinately. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. f. ({#-drA#}) Excessive sleep (also considered as a morbid symptom). <div n="P">III. Avyayībh. ({#-dram#}) After sleeping. E. {#ati#} and {#nidrA#}.
{#atinivft#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-vft#}). See {#atinicft#}.

{#atipAdanivft#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-t#}). See the preceding.

E. {#ati#} (sc. {#krAntaH#}) and {#rAtri#} (in the sense of the accusative), samāsānta aff. {#ac#}; properly meaning ‘last- ing beyond a night’.

{#atri#}¦ m. ({#-triH#}) <sup>1</sup> Eater, devourer (in the Vedas especially as an epithet of Agni, the divinity of fire). <sup>2</sup> The name of a Maharshi or a great Saint, who in the Vedas occurs especi- ally in hymns composed for the praise of Agni, Indra, the Aśvins and the Viśvadevas; and who in the epic period is considered as one of the ten Prajāpatis or lords of crea- tion engendered by Manu for the purpose of creating the universe; at a later period he appears as a mindborn son of Brahmā and as one of the seven Ṛṣis who preside over the reign of Svāyambhuva, the first, or according to others of Svārochiṣa, the second, or of Vaivaswata, the seventh Manu; he is married to Anasūyā, the daughter of Daksha and their son is Durvāsas. Produced by a flash of light from his eye which was received by Space, the via lactea personified, or according to a more recent legend, by his penitence, is Soma or the moon. See {#atrijAta#}, {#atridfgja, atrinetraja#} &c. As sons of his are also named the Manes Barhishads and Udamaya; a daughter of his is Apālā. The name of Atri occurs also as that of the author of several vaidik hymns, as that of an inspired legislator, of the author of an astronomical and medical work and, in astronomy, as one of the seven Ṛṣis in the constel- lation of the great bear.--An Atri, son of Sāṅkhya, but probably a different personage, is the author of a hymn in the Ṛgveda.--Amongst the authors of vaidik hymns we find as sons or descendants of Atri the following: Archa- nāna, Avasyu, Bāhuvṛkta, Bhauma, Budha, Dvita, Ga- viṣṭhira, Gaya, Gopavana, Isha, Paura, Pratibhānu, Pra- tiprabha, the Prayaswats, Purīṣa, Ratahavya, Sadāpṛṇa, Saptavadhri, Śaśa, Satyaśravas, Śrutavid, Sutambhara, Śyāvāśva, Vasuśruta, the Vasūyus, Viśvasāman, Yajata; and as daughters of Atri, Apālā, Gātu, Viśvavārā. <sup>3</sup> m. pl. ({#atrayaH#}) The descendants (see {#gotra#}) of Atri collectively. (The masc. plur. {#atrayaH#} is considered as the plur. of the patronymic {#Atreya#} (q. v.) with luk of the taddh. aff. {#Qak#}; the plural of the fem., however, remaining regular, viz. {#AtreyyaH#}; but there is no necessity to adopt this artificial etymology which is given to connect the sense of the pa- tronymic with that of the plur. of the original form.) E. See {#attri#}.

{#aTa#}¦ ind. An inceptive and auspicious particle. It serves to introduce the beginning of a work, a chapter, a sentence and with respect to the latter may imply doubt or inter- rogation or may serve as a conjunctive or disjunctive par- ticle. It may be accompanied by those particles or words which themselves are used in the same sense, giving them greater emphasis, especially by {#u, atas, anantaram, kim#}, {#tu, punar, vA, kimu, api#}. Without or with these particles {#aTa#} corresponds therefore with: <sup>1</sup> Now (inceptive or pre- mising); in the same sense but with greater emphasis {#aTo#} ({#aTa#} and {#u#}), {#aTAtas, aTAnantaram#}. <sup>2</sup> Why? what? (in- terrogatively and doubtingly); (likewise {#aTavA#}.) <sup>3</sup> How else? certainly; (in the same sense {#aTakim#}.) <sup>4</sup> But, on the contrary; (in the same sense {#aTa tu, aTa punar#}.) <sup>5</sup> Or, or rather; (likewise {#aTavA, aTavApi, aTApi vA#} &c.) <sup>6</sup> More- over, so much the more, therefore, thus; (likewise {#aTaca#}, {#aTApi, aTo api, aTa kimu#}.) In the Vedas there occurs also the protracted form {#aTA#} which seems to be the more original one; (cf. {#taTA#} and {#yaTA#}). E. According to the native authorities from {#arT#}, kṛt aff. {#qa#} with {#r#} being dropped; but it is more probably derived from {#a#}, the pron. theme which is considered as a substitute for {#idam#} (pointing to what follows), taddh. aff. {#Ta#}.
{#aTakim#}¦ ind. A particle of assent, how else, what else, as- suredly. (Better to be considered as two words. See {#aTa#}.) E. {#aTa#} and {#kim#}.
{#aTakimu#}¦ ind. So much the more. (Better to be considered as two separate words and also written {#aTa kimu#}. See {#aTa#}.) E. {#aTa#} and {#kimu#}.
{#aTaca#}¦ ind. Also, moreover. (Better to be considered as two words. See {#aTa#}.) E. {#aTa#} and {#ca#}.

{#aTarI#}¦ f. (occurs only as a plural in the Vedas; {#-ryaH#}) The finger. E. This word is given as an irregular derivation from {#at#} ‘to go constantly’; but it is more probable that it is derived, with aff. {#ari#}, from an obsolete rad. {#aT#} which seems to have had the same meaning as {#at#} (cf. {#aw#} and {#aW#}), but is found only in {#aTarI, aTarvan#} and their derivatives, implying quickness or agility. The same etymo- logical connexion between words meaning ‘finger’ and ‘fire’ may be perceived in other derivations from a radical in the sense of ‘to go’ f. i. in {#aNguli#} or {#aNguri, agrU#} and {#agni, aNgiras#}, from {#aNg#}. A commentary explains, that {#aTarya#} is an epithet of {#dakzi-#} {#RAgni#}, because the sacred fire ‘goes always’ from the Gār- hapatya (q. v.) to his proper place; the epithet may be con- sidered, however, as one of a more general bearing.
{#aTaryu#}¦ m. ({#-yuH#}) Moving constantly; an epithet of Agni in the Vedas. See the preceding. E. {#aTary#}, kṛt aff. {#u#}.

{#aTarva#}¦ m. ({#-rvaH#}) A proper name of the eldest son of Brahmā, to whom Brahmā revealed the Brahmavidyā (q. v.) or know- ledge of God. See {#aTarvan#}. E. See {#aTarvan#} of which it is an abbreviated form.
