{#aTarvaRi#}¦ m. ({#-RiH#}) <sup>1</sup> A Brahman versed in the Atharvaveda. <sup>2</sup> A family priest. E. See {#ATarvaRi#} which is the better reading of this word.

{#aTarvan#}¦ 1. m. ({#-rvA#}) <sup>1</sup> A Brāhmaṇa, a priest (probably one connected with offerings to fire or the attendance on the holy fire). <sup>2</sup> The proper name of a priest who is considered to have obtained the fire from heaven and who in the course of mythological personification appears as a Prajāpati or father of all beings, as the inspired author of the fourth or Atharvaveda, as the eldest son of Brahmā to whom Brahmā revealed the Brahmavidyā (q. v.) or knowledge of God (see also {#aTarva#}) and, at a later period, as the same as Angiras (q. v.). Sons of his are Agni (see also {#aNgiras#}), Dadhyanch, Bhishaj, Bṛhaddiva, Kabandha. <sup>3</sup> An epithet of <sup>a.</sup> Vasiṣṭha q. v., <sup>b.</sup> Soma q. v., <sup>c.</sup> {#prARa#} q. v., <sup>d.</sup> Śiva (the god being supposed to carry into effect the charms of the Atharvaveda). <div n="P">2. m. n. ({#-rvA-rva#}) The fourth or Atharvaveda q. v. (see also m. pl. {#aTarvARaH#}). <div n="P">3. m. pl. ({#-rvARaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The descendants of Atharvan; they appear sometimes coupled with the descendants of Bhṛgu and of Angiras (see {#aTarvANgirasaH#}). <sup>2</sup> The hymns of the fourth or Atharvaveda collectively (considered as the descen- dants of Atharvan); the Atharvaveda (see also {#aTarvANgi-#} {#rasaH#}). E. From an obsolete theme {#aTar#}, fire, with taddh. aff. {#vanip#}. See the E. of {#aTarI#}. The oldest etym. which derives {#aTarvan#} from {#a#} neg. and {#Tarvan#} (from {#Tarv#} ‘to go’), is without any probability. A similar etym. is given of {#aTarvI#} q. v.

{#aTarvaBUta#}¦ Tatpur. m. pl. ({#-tAH#}) An epithet of the twelve Maharshis: [Page045-b+ 56] {#Darma, dakza, marIci, atri, pulastya, pulaha, kratu, vasizWa, gO-#} {#tama, Bfgu, aNgiras, manu#} and (according to a commentary) of ‘Rudra, the Lord of the Universe’. {#aTarvaSiKA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-KA#}) The name of one of the Upani- shads of the Atharvaveda. E. {#aTarvan#} and {#SiKA#} ‘the crest’ i. e. (according to the comm.) the essence of the Atharvaveda.

{#aTarvANgiras#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-rAH#}) The Angiras of the Athar- vaveda. Dwandwa. m. pl. ({#-rasaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The descendants of Athar- van and of Angiras. <sup>2</sup> The Atharvaveda hymns of both collectively; the Atharvaveda (q. v.), one part (or parvan) of which is considered to have been revealed by the descen- dants of Atharvan and another by the descendants of An- giras. E. {#aTarvan#} and {#aNgiras#}.

({#-sam#}) The religious observances ({#karman#}) connected with the ritual of the Atharvaveda. <div n="P">III. m. pl. ({#-sAH#}) The mantras or hymns of the Athar- vaveda. {#adakziRa#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) I. Tatpur. <sup>1</sup> Not right, left. <sup>2</sup> Not clever, unskilful. E. {#a#} neg. and {#dakziRa#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. Being or being performed without the presents usually given to Brahmans (see {#dakziRA#}), as a sacrifice &c. The celebration of a sacrifice without the Dakṣiṇā oc- curs for instance under the following circumstances: at the Prātaḥsavana of the Jyotiṣṭoma, when about to sing the Vahiṣpavamāna stotra, the priests step out from the house where the sacred fire is kept, one going after the other and holding the one who precedes by the hem of his garment: if it so happens, at this procession, that the Udgātṛ inadvertently drops the hem, the sacrifice goes on without the Dakṣiṇā; once accomplished, however, it is to be repeated and then the Udgātṛ has to pay the Dakṣiṇā which should have been given at the first performance; if the Pratihartṛ meets with a similar accident, he has to pay his whole property at the renewal of the ceremony, which then is called {#sarvasvadakziRa#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#dakziRA#}.

{#advayAvin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vI#}) (ved.) The same as {#advayat#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#dvayAvin#}.

(q. v.), but in the abl. and loc. sing. of the masc. and neuter and in the nom. plur. of the masc. it forms optionally {#aDarasmAt#} or {#aDarAt, aDarasmin#} or {#aDare, aDare#} or {#a-#} {#DarAH#}; it may form Tatpur. compositions with nouns having the sense of the singular and considered then as depending upon {#aDara#}, which is the former part of the compound, in the genitive; for instance {#aDarakAyaH#} is explained, {#aDaraM#} {#kAyasya#}.) Adverbially used are {#aDarAt, aDarasmAt, aDareRa#}; qq. vv. <sup>2</sup> Low, vile. <sup>3</sup> Speechless, refuted, overcome in abuse or controversy. <sup>4</sup> Prior, preceding in time. See {#aDaredyus#}. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-raH#}) The lower lip, the lip. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-rA#}) <sup>1</sup> The lower region. <sup>2</sup> The nadir (?). <div n="P">IV. m. n. ({#-ram#} or {#-re#}) <sup>1</sup> The lower and higher, inferior and better, prior and posterior. <sup>2</sup> A state of con- fusion, when things are tupsy-turvy. <sup>3</sup> Address and answer. {#aDarozWa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-zWaH#}) The lower lip. Also {#aDarOzWa#}. E. {#aDara#} and {#ozWa#}.

{#aDarma#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. ({#-rmaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Unrighteousness, injustice, all behaviour contrary to the Śruti and Smṛti, or religious and legal institutions. <sup>2</sup> (In philosophy.) According to the Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika: moral demerit, the result of doing what is forbidden, the peculiar cause of pain, one of the twenty-four qualities united with substance.--According to the Sāṅkhya, one of the changeable ({#vEkftika#}) dispo- sitions ({#BAva#}) of the mind, which being the efficient cause, makes the soul migrate into an animal, a deer, a bird, a reptile, a vegetable, a mineral.--According to the Bud- dhistic doctrine it is the consequence of upādāna or exertion of body or speech.--According to the Jainas it is that which causes the soul in general to continue embarrassed with body notwithstanding its capacity for ascent and na- tural tendency to soar. <sup>3</sup> As a personification Adharma oc- curs in the Purāṇas as one of the Prajāpatis or mind-born sons of Brahmā; his wife is Hinsā (mischief) on whom he begot Anṛta (falsehood) and Nikṛti (immorality) or ac- cording to others, Mṛṣā (falsehood) and his children Dam- bha (hypocrisy) and Māyā (deceit) who were adopted by Nirṛti (misfortune).--Adharma is also mentioned as one of the eighteen servants of the sun. <div n="P">2. f. ({#-rmA#}) According to the Śāktas a kalā or part of the original or Mūla-prakṛti and personified as the bride of Mṛtyu or Death. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Darma#}.

{#aDavA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-vA#}) A widow. See {#viDavA#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#Dava#}.

{#aDastAddiS#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-k#}) The lower region, the nadir. E. {#aDastAt#} and {#diS#}.
{#aDaspada#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-dam#}) The place under the feet. E. {#a-#} {#Das#} and {#pada#}.
{#aDA#}¦ ind. See {#aDa#}.
{#aDAmArgava#}¦ m. ({#-vaH#}) A plant (Achyranthes aspera). Also {#DAmArgava#}; and see {#apAmArga#}. E. unknown.
{#aDAraRaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Not supporting, not giving or not allowing to gain a livelihood, unpro- fitable. E. {#a#} priv. and {#DAraRa#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#aDArmika#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) Unjust, unrighteous, wicked. See also {#ADArmika#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#DArmika#}.

{#aDi#}¦ ind. (see {#nipAta, upasarga, gati, karmapravacanIya#}) A par- ticle implying superiority in place, power, rank, quality and quantity and generally used as a separable prepo- sition or as a prefix to verbs, but in the Vedas also as an adverb. With nouns it may form Tatpur., Bahuvr. and Avyayībhāva compounds. It means. <div n="P">1. (as adverb, in the Vedas) very much, excessively. <div n="P">2. (as a separable preposition) <sup>1</sup> with a noun following or preceding in the locative, <sup>a.</sup> above (in place), <sup>b.</sup> over (in the sense of mastership, power &c.), <sup>c.</sup> under (see {#aDIna#} and {#aDika#} 4, cf. {#aDas#}); <sup>2</sup> with a noun following or pre- ceding in the accusative, <sup>a.</sup> on, above (in place), <sup>b.</sup> concerning, with respect to, <sup>c.</sup> repeated it implies also proximity; f. i. {#aDyaDi grAmam#} above the village but in its neighbourhood; <sup>3</sup> with a noun following or preceding in the ablative (in the Vedas), <sup>a.</sup> on, above, <sup>b.</sup> from above, <sup>c.</sup> from (in this meaning it occurs also in the classical language, when it is supposed to be merely an expletive, the preceding ablative implying already the notion ‘from’), <sup>d.</sup> in consequence of, on behalf of, <sup>e.</sup> in presence of, before, in front of; <sup>4</sup> with a noun following or preceding in the genitive (in the Vedas), amidst, amongst. <div n="P">3. (as a prefix to verbs) Over, esp. in the sense of taking possession of, mastering &c. literally or metapho- rically; but used also as an expletive esp. when followed by another preposition: f. i. with {#kf#} to superintend, with {#i#} to obtain, to study &c.; but it does not alter the meaning of {#Agam#}, when forming with the latter {#aDyAgam#}. <div n="P">4. (in composition) <sup>1</sup> (with Tatpur. or Bahuvr.) it implies superiority in place, rank, quantity &c., <sup>2</sup> (with Avyayībh.) <sup>a.</sup> concerning, with respect to, <sup>b.</sup> over. E. unknown.

{#aDi#}¦ 1. m. ({#-DiH#}) Anxiety, mental pain; more usually {#ADi#} q. v. of which it seems to be an incorrect reading. E. see {#ADi#}. <div n="P">2. f. ({#-DiH#}) A woman in her courses. See also {#avi#}. E. {#ad#}, kṛt aff. {#i#} and {#D#} substituted for {#d#} or a Tatpur. {#a#} neg. and {#Di#} (from {#DA#}). (The first etym. doubtful.)

{#aDika#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> Exceeding, in addition to (the reverse of {#nyUna#}; between both {#sADAraRa#}). <sup>2</sup> More, more than, superior (in place, power, rank, quality or quantity). <sup>3</sup> Very much, excessive, excellent. <sup>4</sup> Less, smaller, inferior (cf. {#aDi#} 2. 1. c.). {#aDikam#} used as adverb. (If {#aDika#} has the first of these meanings, that by which the excess is caused, stands in the instrumental or (but seldom) in the locative or forms the first part of a Tatpur. compound of which {#aDika#} is the latter; if it has the second meaning, the object compared with, stands in the instrumental, the ablative or in the genitive; if it has the last meaning, the object compared with stands in the abla- tive. Cf. {#aDyArUQa#}. With numerals {#aDika#} may form Bahuvr. compounds, usually in the plural, if it is the former part of the compound; for instance {#aDikacatvAriMSAH#} (sc. {#saMKyAH#}) i. e. more than {{fourty->forty|||Dr. Sampada Savardekar|https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/50|}}. It is considered as dropped in Dwandwa compounds of numerals f. i. in {#paYcaviMSati#}, equal to {#paYcADi-#} {#kaviMSati#}.) <sup>5</sup> Embolismic, intercalary (only in composition with and prefixed to the name or numeral of a luni-solar year, to the name of a month and to the name of a day; [Page054-a+ 56] f. i. {#aDikASvina#}. See also {#aDikatiTi, aDikadina, aDi-#} {#kamAsa, aDikasaMvatsara#}, and compare {#kzaya#}). <sup>5</sup> Subsequent, following (as a day, a chapter or a passage in a book &c.; used very much in the same manner as {#UrDva#}). <div n="P">II. n. ({#-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> The surplus, that which is exceeding. <sup>2</sup> (In Nyāya.) Superfluity in reasons or instances, giving more reasons or instances than are required or relevant in a syllogism. <sup>3</sup> (In rhetoric.) Hyperbole (of which two kinds are enumerated: hyperbole concerning the recipient (substance, subject &c.) and hyperbole concerning that which is to be received (accidents, predicate &c.). E. {#aDi#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.
{#aDikatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Excess, addition; also {#aDikatva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aDika#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#aDikakzayakArin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rI-riRI-ri#}) Causing excessive loss, wasting too much. E. {#aDika-kzaya#} and {#kArin#}.

{#aDikatiTi#}¦ Karmadh. m. f. ({#-TiH-TiH#}) An intercalary lunar day. When no tithi (q. v.) begins or ends in a solar day, the numeral of the preceding is repeated in the calendar, the first tithi being accounted the intercalated and the second the proper one. Compare {#kzayatiTi#}. E. {#aDika#} and {#tiTi#}.
{#aDikadanta#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-ntaH#}) A tooth growing over an- other. See {#aDidanta#} and {#varDana#}. E. {#aDika#} and {#danta#}.
{#aDikadina#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-nam#}) An intercalated day. See {#aDikatiTi#}. Also {#aDidina#}. E. {#aDika#} and {#dina#}.
{#aDikamAMsArman#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}). See {#aDimAMsArman#}. E. {#a-#} {#Dika-mAMsa#} and {#arman#}.
{#aDikamAsa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-saH#}) An intercalated month. Also {#aDimAsa#}. Compare {#kzayamAsa#}. E. {#aDika#} and {#mAsa#}.

{#aDikaraRa#}¦ I. Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Superiority, supremacy, govern- ment. <sup>2</sup> Title, right. <sup>3</sup> Town meeting, court of justice. <sup>4</sup> Sup- port, receptacle. <sup>5</sup> Substance ({#dravya#}, as the recipient of quali- ties &c.). <sup>6</sup> (In grammar.) Comprehension, location, gener- ally the sense of the seventh or locative case, but occa- sionally also that of the third or instrumental and of the sixth or genitive case. <sup>7</sup> (In grammar.) Government, re- gimen; see {#ekADikaraRa, yugapadaDikaraRa, samAnADikaraRa#}. <sup>8</sup> (In philosophy.) A case or topic; esp. in the Mīmānsā and Vedānta; in the former it comprehends usually five parts or members, the subject ({#vizaya#}), the doubt ({#saMSaya#}), the first side (or objectionable) argument ({#pUrvapakza#}), the fol- lowing (or right) argument ({#uttarapakza#}) and the conclusion ({#sidDAnta#} or {#rAdDAnta#}). Sometimes, however, the second part is inherent in the third and the fifth in the fourth. In both philosophies an adhikaraṇa is a subdivision of a pāda, which is the division of an adhyāya. E. {#kf#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. ({#-RaH-RI#}). See {#aDikAra#} II. E. {#aDi#} and {#karaRa#}; in the fem. with aff. {#NIp#}.
{#aDikaraRamaRqapa#}¦ Tatpur. m. n. ({#-paH-pam#}) A hall of the town council, a hall of justice(?). E. {#aDikaraRa#} and {#maRqapa#}.

{#aDikaraRasidDAnta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ntaH#}) (In the Nyāya philoso- phy.) A truth or conclusion which implies another truth or conclusion; one of the four kinds of {#sidDAnta#}. See also {#sarva-#} {#tantrasidDAnta, pratitantrasidDAnta#} and {#aByupagamasidDAnta#}. E. {#a-#} {#DikaraRa#} and {#sidDAnta#}, a paramount truth.
{#aDikaraRika#}.¦ See {#ADikaraRika#}.
{#aDikaraREtAvattva#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-ttvam#}) Quantity. E. {#aDikaraRa#} (substance) and {#etAvattva#} ‘the fixed measure of a substance’.
{#aDikardDi#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rdDiH-rdDiH-rdDi#}) Prosperous, every way happy. E. {#aDika#} and {#fdDi#}.
{#aDikarmakara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) The same as the following. E. {#aDi#} and {#karmakara#}.

{#aDikarmakft#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-t#}) A servant who is set over or superintends the working men; one of the four kinds of servants called {#karmakAra#} or {#karmakara#} qq. vv. See also {#SuSrUzaka#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#karmakft#}.
{#aDikarmakfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) The master or chief of a fa- mily, one who superintends all family affairs. E. {#aDi-#} {#karman#} and {#kfta#}.
{#aDikarman#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}) Superintendence, supervision. E. {#kf#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#manin#}.
{#aDikarmika#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) Clerk or prefect of the market or fair. E. {#aDikarman#}, taddh. aff. {#Wan#}.

{#aDikalpin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-lpI#}) (ved.) An exceedingly {{shrewed->shrewd|||Dr. Sampada Savardekar|https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/50|}} gambler, one skilled in superior tricks or combinations(?). E. {#aDi#} and {#kalpin#}.
{#aDikavAkyokti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ktiH#}) Exaggeration, hyperbole. E. {#aDika-vAkya#} and {#ukti#}.
{#aDikazAzwika#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) Bought with, made of &c. more than sixty. E. {#aDika-zazwi#}, taddh. aff. {#WaY#}.
{#aDikasaMvatsara#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-raH#}) An intercalated year. E. {#aDika#} and {#saMvatsara#}.
{#aDikasAptatika#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) Bought with, made of &c. more than seventy. E. {#aDika-saptati#}, taddh. aff. {#WaY#}.

{#aDikANga#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-NgaH-NgI#} or {#-NgA-Ngam#}) Having more members than natural or common. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-Ngam#}) The girdle over the coat of mail, worn as a kind of scarf. E. {#aDika#} and {#aNga#}; in the fem. with aff. {#NIz#} or {#wAp#}.

{#aDikAra#}¦ I. Tatp. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Superintendence, supremacy, autho- rity. <sup>2</sup> Rule, government. <sup>3</sup> Duty, office. <sup>4</sup> Right, title, owner- ship. <sup>5</sup> The use of royal insignia. <sup>6</sup> (In the Mīmānsā philo- sophy.) The right of action, i. e. the right to institute a sacrifice and to claim the results which are derived from it; it is subject to different regulations and restrictions and forms the subject of the sixth adhyāya of the Mīmānsā. See also {#karmADikAra#}. <sup>7</sup> A topic in a book; especially in grammatical works where it means a precept, rule or word, heading and applying to a number of particular rules which follow. Also written {#aDIkAra#}. E. {#kf#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. ({#-raH-rI#}) One who has many duties to per- form, very busy. E. {#aDi#} and {#kAra#}; in the fem. with aff. {#NIz#}.
{#aDikArasTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-sTaH-sTA-sTam#}) Established in an office or charge. E. {#aDikAra#} and {#sTa#}.

{#aDikAritA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) <sup>1</sup> Ownership, lordship. <sup>2</sup> Right, title &c. See {#aDikArin#}. Also {#aDikAritva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aDi-#} {#kArin#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.

{#aDikArin#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-rI-riRI-ri#}) (In law.) Possessing a right or title. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-rI#}) <sup>1</sup> A superintendent, a ruler, a director. [Page055-a+ 56] <sup>2</sup> One holding an office. <sup>3</sup> A master, an owner. <sup>4</sup> (In the Mī- mānsā.) One entitled to institute a sacrifice; see {#aDikAra#}. <sup>5</sup> (In the Vedānta.) A person who is perfect in the principles and practice of the Vedānta. <sup>6</sup> Man (in general). E. {#aDi-#} {#kAra#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.
{#aDikArTavacana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Exaggeration, hyperbole. E. {#aDika-arTa#} and {#vacana#}.
{#aDikArma#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rmam#}). Perhaps the name of a place or country. E. {#aDika#} and {#arma#}.

{#aDikfta#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Superintended, governed. <sup>2</sup> Claimed or held as a right. <sup>3</sup> Set as a rule or authority. <sup>4</sup> Set over, superintendent. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-taH#}) <sup>1</sup> A superintendent in general. <sup>2</sup> Inspector of receipts and disbursements, an auditor of public ac- compts. E. {#kf#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDikfti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) A possession, a right, a privilege. See {#aDikaraRa#}. E. {#kf#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#ktin#}.
{#aDikrama#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) Invasion, assailing. E. {#kram#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}.
{#aDikzit#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-t#}) (ved.) Lord, ruler. E. {#kzi#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kvip#}.

{#aDikzipta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) <sup>1</sup> Censured, reviled, detracted from. <sup>2</sup> Thrown or cast down. <sup>3</sup> Dismissed, sent, dispatched. <sup>4</sup> Placed, fixed. E. {#kzip#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDikzepa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) <sup>1</sup> Detraction, censure. <sup>2</sup> Dismissal, dispatch. E. {#kzip#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}.
{#aDigata#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Obtained. <sup>2</sup> Gone through or over, lit. or fig. as read, studied. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDigantavya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vyaH-vyA-vyam#}) To be reached, attain- able, acquirable, lit. or fig. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#tavya#}.
{#aDigantf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ntA#}) One who obtains or acquires. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#tfc#}.

{#aDigama#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> Obtaining, attaining, acquiring. <sup>2</sup> Attainment, apprehension, going through or over, lit. or fig. <sup>3</sup> Profit, gain, interest on capital or risk. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}.

{#aDigamana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Obtaining, attaining, acquiring. <sup>2</sup> Attainment, apprehension, going through or over, lit. or fig. as reading, studying. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDigamanIya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) To be reached, attainable, acquirable, lit. or fig. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#anIyar#}.
{#aDigamya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-myaH-myA-myam#}) Attainable, to be reached or acquired, lit. or fig. E. {#gam#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#yat#}.
{#aDigava#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vI-vam#}) (ved.) On the cow, coming from the cow (as milk &c.). E. {#aDi#} and {#go#}, samāsānta aff. {#wac#}.
{#aDiguRa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) Of superior quali- ties. E. {#aDi#} and {#guRa#}.
{#aDija#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-jaH-jA-jam#}) <sup>1</sup> Superior by birth. <sup>2</sup> Born from, produced on(?). E. {#jan#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#qa#}.
{#aDijanana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Birth. E. {#jan#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#aDijihva#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-hvaH#}) One of the diseases of the throat, described as ‘a swelling at the root of the tongue like a second tongue’ (probably a swelling of the epiglottis)--therefore [Page055-b+ 56] called also {#dvijihva#}--and produced by the phlegm and blood; when it suppurates, considered as incurable. Also {#aDi-#} {#jihvikA#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#jihvA#}.
{#aDijihvikA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-kA#}) The same as the preceding. E. {#aDijihva#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#aDijya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-jyaH-jyA-jyam#}) Strung (as a bow). E. {#aDi#} and {#jyA#}.

{#aDijyotizam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning or relating to the lu- minous part of creation; a chapter in the Upanishads treat- ing thereon, comprises the following subjects: fire, sun, water and the substance of lightning. E. {#aDi#} and {#jyotiza#}.
{#aDityakA#}¦ f. ({#-kA#}) Land on the upper part of a mountain. E. {#aDi#}, taddh. aff. {#tyakan#}.
{#aDidanta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ntaH#}) A tooth growing over another. See {#aDikadanta#} and {#varDana#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#danta#}.
{#aDidina#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The same as {#aDikadina#}. E. {#a-#} {#Di#} and {#dina#}.

{#aDideva#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A supreme or tutelary deity. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-vam#}) Concerning the gods. (In derivatives with a taddh. aff. which has an anubandha {#Y, R#} or {#k#}, both parts of this word have vṛddhi, f. i. {#ADidEvika#} q. v.) E. {#aDi#} and {#deva#}.
{#aDidevatam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning the divinities or the gods. E. {#aDi#} and {#devatA#}.
{#aDidevatA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tA#}) A tutelary or presiding divinity. E. {#aDi#} and {#devatA#}.
{#aDidevana#}¦ n. ({#-nam#}) The ground in a hall, on which gambling with dice takes place. E. {#div#}, with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDidEva#}¦ I. Tatpur. n. ({#-vam#}) and <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-vam#}). See the following. E. {#aDi#} and {#dEva#}.

{#aDidEvata#}¦ I. Tatpur. n. ({#-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> The supreme or tutelary deity. <sup>2</sup> The active principle in creation, the regulating power which resides in water, fire, sky, air, the regions &c. See also {#aDiBUta, aDyAtma#}. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-tam#}) Concerning <sup>1</sup> the deity or <sup>2</sup> the active principle in creation. E. {#aDi#} and {#dEvata#}.

{#aDipa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) <sup>1</sup> An owner, a lord or master. <sup>2</sup> A king. <sup>3</sup> (In astrology.) The regent of a sign of the zodiac. E. {#pA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#ka#}.

{#aDipati#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> A master, an owner, a ruler. <sup>2</sup> A king. (A noun depending upon it in these meanings stands in the gen. or loc., f. i. {#gavAmaDipati#} or {#gozvaDipati#}.) <sup>3</sup> (In me- dicine.) ‘That part of the trunk which is inside of the upper part of the head, at the passage of the vessel along the lateral sinus; wounds inflicted there produce instan- taneous death’. E. {#pA#} with {#aDi#}, uṇ. aff. {#qati#}.

{#aDipativatI#}¦ f. ({#-tI#}) The name of certain female divinities (in the Vedas). See {#patnI#}. E. {#aDipati#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}, the change of {#m#} in the affix to {#v#} being restricted, in this word, to the vaidik meaning of it.
{#aDipatnI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tnI#}) A mistress, a protectress. E. {#aDipati#}, fem. aff. {#NIp#}, and {#n#} ādeśa for the final {#i#}.
{#aDipaTam#}¦ Avyayībh. Over or across a road. E. {#aDi#} and {#paTin#}, samāsānta aff. {#a#}.
{#aDipA#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-pAH#}) (ved.) A master, a lord, a pro- tector. E. {#pA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#vic#}.
{#aDipAMSula#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Where dust is lying on or has risen from, dusty. Also written {#aDipAMsula#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#pAMsula#}.
{#aDipuruza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) The supreme or presiding spirit. E. {#aDi#} and {#puruza#}.

{#aDiprajam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning or relating to the continua- tion of the world by procreation; a chapter in the Upa- nishads treating thereon comprises the subjects: mother, father, posterity and generation. E. {#aDi#} and {#prajA#}.
{#aDiprazwi#}¦ Avyayībh. (ved.) Over the Praṣṭi (q. v.). See the following. E. {#aDi#} and {#prazwi#}.

{#aDiprazwiyuga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) (ved.) The yoke over the Praṣṭi horse, to which a fourth horse was put (in a cere- mony connected with the Vājapeya sacrifice; two horses being put before a cart and a third in front of the two, so as to form with them a kind of triangle or tripod ({#prazwi#} q. v.), wherefore the third horse was called meta- phorically the Praṣṭi). E. {#aDiprazwi#} and {#yuga#}.
{#aDiBU#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-BUH#}) A master, a ruler. E. {#BU#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kvip#}.

{#aDiBUta#}¦ I. Tatpur. n. ({#-tam#}) A subtile or invisible element, one which is the cause of the gross or visible elements (also as an attribute of the supreme soul that pervades and regulates all elements or existence). <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-tam#}) Concerning or relating to the bhūta or elements; a chapter in the Upanishads includes under this topic, earth, atmosphere, material heaven, regions, intermediate regions, fire, air, sun, moon, lunar mansions, water, annual plants, trees, ether, soul. (In derivatives with a taddh. aff. which has an anubandha {#Y, R#} or {#k#}, both parts of this word assume vṛddhi, f. i. {#ADiBOtika#}.) E. {#aDi#} and {#BUta#}.

{#aDimanTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nTaH#}) (In medicine.) Severe ophthal- mia which is described as having the following symptoms: ‘acute pains as if the eyes were torn; throbbing which ex- tends to half of the head’; it consists of four varieties ac- cording to its being produced by derangement of the air, bile, phlegm or blood. Also {#aDImanTa#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#manTa#}.

{#aDimanTana#}¦ Tatpur. m. n. ({#-naH-nam#}) (ved.) A piece of wood from the paring of the sacrificial post, placed over the araṇi (q. v.) to kindle a fire by attrition. E. {#manT#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}; {{seil->scil|||Dr. Sampada Savardekar|https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/50|}}. {#Sakala#}.
{#aDimanTita#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Affected with the disease called {#aDimanTa#} q. v. E. {#aDimanTay#} ({#aDimanTa#}, denom. aff. {#Ric#}), kṛt aff. {#kta#}.

{#aDimAMsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) (In medicine.) A disease of the gums, described as ‘a great and painful swelling round the wisdom-tooth with the discharge of saliva; produced by diseased phlegm’. Also {#aDimAMsaka#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#mAMsa#}.
{#aDimAMsaka#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}). The same as the preceding. E. {#aDi-#} {#mAMsa#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.

{#aDimAMsArman#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}) (In medicine.) A disease of the white part on the conjunctiva of the eye; it is described as ‘a large, soft (fleshy growth), either liver-coloured or brown’. Also {#aDikamAMsArman#}. E. {#aDimAMsa#} (scil. {#ja#}) and {#arman#}; ‘the disease {#arman#} produced by the fleshy excrescence’.

{#aDimAtra#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-traH-trA-tram#}) Excessive, above measure. Cf. {#atimAtra#}. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-tram#}) Above syllabic measurement. (In the doctrine of the Upanishads the mysterious syllable {#om#} is said to be exempt from the general rules of prosody. See also {#aDyakzara#}.) E. {#aDi#} and {#mAtrA#}.

{#aDimAtrakAruRika#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) The name of a Mahā- brahman (q. v.) according to the mythology of the Buddhists. E. {#aDimAtra#} and {#kAruRika#}, lit. ‘excessively kind or com- passionate’.

{#aDimAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) An intercalary month, formed of the aggregate days omitted in reckoning the lunar year, in com- parison with the solar. See also {#aDikamAsa#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#mAsa#}.
{#aDimukti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kti#}) (In Buddhistic literature.) Com- prehension, intelligence, natural disposition (of the soul). E. {#muc#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#ktin#}.
{#aDimuktika#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) A name of Mahākāla (q. v.), according to the mythology of the Buddhists. E. {#aDimukti#}, taddh. aff. {#kan(?)#}.
{#aDimuktisAra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) (In Buddhistic literature.) Being quite comprehension, being thoroughly addicted to comprehending. E. {#aDimukti#} and {#sAra#}.
{#aDimuhya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-hyaH#}) A name of Śākyamuni in one of his thirty-four anterior births. E. {#muh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#yat(?)#} or {#aDi#} and {#muhya#}. The word is doubtful.

{#aDiyajYa#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-jYaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The supreme sacrifice, the sacrifice <lang n="greek">ϰατ᾽ἐξοχήν</lang>. <sup>2</sup> An influence superior to or pre- siding over sacrifice. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-jYam#}) Concerning or with respect to sa- crifice. E. {#aDi#} and {#yajYa#}.

{#aDiyANga#}¦ Tatpur.(?) n. ({#-Ngam#}). The same as {#aDikANga#} of which it is given as a various reading. E. doubtful, per- haps instead of {#aDyANga#} ({#aDi#} and {#ANga#}), or of {#aDikANga#}, with {#y#} in the place of {#k#}.

{#aDiraTa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-TaH-TA-Tam#}) Being on or above a car. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-TaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A charioteer. <sup>2</sup> The proper name of a charioteer who was a prince and descendant of Anu and of Anga, a son of Satyakarman and foster father of Karṇa. E. {#aDi#} and {#raTa#}.
{#aDiraTi#}¦ m. ({#-TiH#}). See {#udaraTi#} of which it occurs as a various reading.
{#aDirAj#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rAw#}) A supreme king or ruler. E. {#aDi#} and {#rAj#}.
{#aDirAja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}). The same as the preceding. E. {#aDi#} and {#rAjan#}, samāsānta aff. {#wac#}.
{#aDirAjan#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jA#}). The same as {#aDirAj#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#rAjan#}.
{#aDirAjya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-jyam#}) <sup>1</sup> Supreme sway. <sup>2</sup> Empire. <sup>3</sup> The name of a country, also read {#aDirAzwra#} and {#aDi-#} {#vAjya#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#rAjya#}.
{#aDirAjyaBAj#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-k#}) An emperor, a paramount sovereign. E. {#aDirAjya#} and {#BAj#}.
{#aDirAzwra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-zwram#}). See {#aDirAjya#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#rAzwra#}.
{#aDirukma#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kmaH-kmA-kmam#}) Wearing gold. E. {#aDi#} and {#rukma#}.
{#aDirUQa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-QaH-QA-Qam#}) Ascended or gone over, lit. or fig., act. or pass., person. or impersonally. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDiropaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) Causing to ascend, placing over. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, in the caus., kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDiropita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Placed over, lit. or fig. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, in the caus., kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDiroha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) Surmounting, ascending, over- topping. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}.
{#aDirohaRa#}¦ Tatpur. I. n. ({#-Ram#}) Ascending, surmounting, over- topping. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-RI#}) A ladder, a staircase. See also {#aDirohiRI#}. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDirohin#}¦ Tatp. I. m. f. n. ({#-hI-hiRI-hi#}) Who rises on or above. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-RI#}) A ladder, a staircase. See {#aDirohaRI#}. E. {#ruh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini(?)#}.
{#aDilokam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning or relating to the world. A chapter in the Upanishads treating thereon comprises the subjects: earth, sky, æther, wind. E. {#aDi#} and {#loka#}.
{#aDivaktf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ktA#}) I. A partisan, an advocate. E. {#vac#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#tfc#}. <div n="P">II. One who speaks in a superior manner, very eloquent. E. {#aDi#} and {#vaktf#}.
{#aDivacana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) I. Advocating, speaking in favour of another. E. {#vac#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}. <div n="P">II. A name, an appellation. E. {#aDi#} and {#vacana#}.
{#aDivastra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-straH-strA-stram#}) Wearing cloth or raiment. E. {#aDi#} and {#vastra#}.
{#aDivAjya#}¦ n. ({#-jyam#}) The name of a country; see {#aDirAjya#} which seems to be the more correct reading of this word.

{#aDivAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) I. <sup>1</sup> One who dwells above others. <sup>2</sup> One who dwells near others, a neighbour. <sup>3</sup> An in- habitant. <sup>4</sup> An abode, a place or situation. E. {#vas#} (to dwell &c.) with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">II. A cover, an upper garment. Also {#aDIvAsa#}. E. {#vas#} (to cover with dress) with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">III. Continuance, perseverance, esp. fig.: fixing one's self at a person's door in order to enforce compliance with some demand. E. {#vas (vasu)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">IV. <sup>1</sup> Perfuming or dressing the person &c.; (as materials and objects of toilet by which this is done, are enumerated the fol- lowing: {#mfttikA, ganDaH, SilA, DAnyam, dUrvA, puzpam, Palam#}, {#daDi, Gftam, svastikam, sindUram, SaNKaH, kajjalam, rocanA, Sve-#} {#tasarzapaH, svarRam, rOpyam, tAmram, cAmaram, darpaRam, dIpaH, praSa-#} {#stapAtram#}). <sup>2</sup> See {#aDivAsana#}. E. {#vAs#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#ac#}.

{#aDivAsana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) I. <sup>1</sup> Perfuming or dressing the per- son &c. (see {#aDivAsa#} IV. 1.). <sup>2</sup> A religious ceremony, pre- liminary to any great Hindu festival: touching a vessel containing perfumes, flowers and other things previously presented to an idol, or offering perfumes &c. to it. E. {#vAs#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}. <div n="P">II. <sup>1</sup> A summoning and fixing of the presence of a divinity upon an image &c., when he is wanted for any solemnity. <sup>2</sup> The placing of a new image in water &c. the day before the divinity is to be summoned to inhabit it. <sup>3</sup> The same as {#aDivAsa#} III. E. {#vas (vasu)#} with {#aDi#}, in the caus., kṛt aff. {#yuc(?)#}.
{#aDivAsaBUmi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-miH#}) A dwelling place. E. {#aDivAsa#} and {#BUmi#}.

{#aDivAsita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) I. Invested with. E. {#vas#} (to cover with dress) with {#aDi#}, in the caus., kṛt aff. {#kta#}. <div n="P">II. Perfumed, scented. E. {#vAs#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDivAsitA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Residence, staying or abiding in one place. Also {#aDivAsitva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aDivAsin#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#aDivAsin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-sI-sinI-si#}) Staying or abiding in one place. E. {#vas#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini(?)#}.
{#aDivAhana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-naH#}) A proper name; acc. to some, a son of Anga. E. {#aDi#} and {#vAhana#}.
{#aDividyam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning or relating to knowledge. A chapter in the Upanishads treating thereon comprises the sub- jects: teacher, pupil, science and expounding. E. {#aDi#} and {#vidyA#}.

{#aDivinnA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-nnA#}) (In law.) A wife whose husband has subsequently married others; a superseded wife. E. {#vid (vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}, or according to another etym. a Bahuvr. of {#aDi#} and {#vinna#}, taken either in the sense of {#vinnA#} or {#vinnam#}.

{#aDivettavyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-vyA#}) A wife deserving or proper to be superseded by her husband marrying another. Also {#aDivedyA#} or {#aDivedanIyA#}. E. {#vid (vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#tavya#}.
{#aDivettf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ttA#}) A man marrying another than his first wife. E. {#vid (vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#tfc#}.
{#aDivedana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Marrying again, whilst a former wife is living. E. {#vid (vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDivedanIyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-yA#}). The same as {#aDivettavyA#}. E. {#vid (vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#anIyar#}.
{#aDivedam#}¦ Avyayībh. Concerning or with respect to the Veda. E. {#aDi#} and {#veda#}.
{#aDivedyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dyA#}). The same as {#aDivettavyA#}. E. {#vid#} {#(vidx)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#yat#}.
{#aDiSayita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Lain or slept over or upon; used either in an active or passive sense, personally or impersonally. E. {#SI#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.

{#aDiSrayaRa#}¦ Tatpur. I. n. ({#-Ram#}) Placing over the fire a pot &c. (the reverse of {#avaSrayaRa#} q. v.); also as a sacrificial act which occurs in several sacrifices, the Darśapūrṇamāsa, Vājapeya &c. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-RI#}) A furnace or fire-place. E. {#Sri#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}, in the fem. with {#NIp#}.
{#aDiSrayaRIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Relating to the {#aDi-#} {#SrayaRa#} q. v. E. {#aDiSrayaRa#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#aDiSrita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Placed over the fire. E. {#Sri#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.

{#aDizavaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) (ved.) The name of two wooden boards, on which the juice of the Soma plant was expressed and where the Somābhiṣava (q. v.) was placed, in sacrifices as the Jyotiṣṭoma or those sharing in the principal rites of it. E. {#sU#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#aDizWAtf#}¦ Tatp. I. m. f. n. ({#-tA-trI-tf#}) Governing, directing, ruling. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-tA#}) <sup>1</sup> A ruler, a governor, a superintendent. <sup>2</sup> (According to the doctrine of the Pāśupatas) Īśvara, the superintending or ruling providence. (In the feminine esp. in conjunction with {#devatA#}, a ruling or tutelary divinity.) E. {#sTA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#tfc#}.

{#aDizWAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Abiding, resting upon. <sup>2</sup> Site, [Page058-a+ 56] situation. <sup>3</sup> A town. <sup>4</sup> (In architecture.) Base, basement. <sup>5</sup> Power, dignity, superintendence. <sup>6</sup> Prescribed rule, fixed practice. <sup>7</sup> A wheel. <sup>8</sup> Approaching. <sup>9</sup> (In Buddhistic litera- ture.) Benediction. E. {#sTA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#aDizWAnaSarIra#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-ram#}) (In Sāṅkhya phil.) According to some, an intermediate body between the {#liNgaSarIra#} and {#sTUla-#} {#SarIra#} (qq. vv.), one that is supposed to enable the subtle body to assume the corporeity of gross body. E. {#aDizWAna#} and {#SarIra#}.
{#aDizWAyaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yakaH-yikA-yakam#}) Superintending, governing. E. {#sTA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Rvul#} and āgama {#yuk#}.

{#aDizWita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Fixed, determined, estab- lished; literally or figuratively, as a house or a practice. <sup>2</sup> Inha- bited, occupied. <sup>3</sup> Supervised, superintended, guarded. <sup>4</sup> Ap- pointed. <sup>5</sup> Superintending, inhabiting, occupying. Used act. or pass., person. or impersonally. E. {#sTA#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDistrI#}¦ I. Tatpur. f. ({#-strI#}) A superior or excellent woman. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-stri#}) Used in the same sense as the lo- cative of {#strI#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#strI#}.
{#aDihari#}¦ Avyayībh. Used in the same sense as the locative of {#hari#}. E. {#aDi#} and {#hari#}.
{#aDIkAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}). See {#aDikAra#}.

{#aDIgarTa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-rTaH#}) (In grammatical terminology.) A radical having the sense of remembering. E. {#ik#} (the technical form of {#i#} in the sense of remembering) with {#aDi#}, and {#arTa#}; scil. {#DAtu#}.
{#aDIta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Read, obtained &c. E. {#i#} ({#iN#} or {#ik#}) with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDItaveda#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-daH#}) A Brahman, who has read the Vedas; a student who has finished his course of study. E. {#aDIta#} and {#veda#}.
{#aDIti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Study, perusal. <sup>2</sup> (ved.) Recollec- tion, desire. E. {#i#} (<sup>1</sup> {#iN#}, <sup>2</sup> {#ik#}) with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#ktin#}.
{#aDItin#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-tI-tinI-ti#}) Well read in, conversant with, versed in (with a noun in the locative; f. i. {#aDItI#} {#vyAkaraRe#}, versed in grammar). E. {#aDIta#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#aDIna#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Dependant. <sup>2</sup> Docile. E. {#aDi#} and {#ina#} ‘having a master over one's self’. This word and the etymology as mentioned, are given by the native lexicographers; but according to the best grammatical autho- rities {#aDIna#} would not exist as a real word. Words as {#rA-#} {#jADIna, brAhmaRADIna#} and the like, are explained by them as coming from {#rAjADi#} ({#rAjan#} and {#aDi#}), {#brAhmaRADi#} ({#brAhmaRa#} and {#aDi#}) with taddh. aff. {#Ka#}, or by others as derived from {#rA-#} {#jan, brAhmaRa#} with taddh. aff. {#saDInan#}; it would seem therefore that the use of {#aDIna#} as an independant word is grammatically not correct. But see {#aDyaDIna#} and {#anaDInaka#}.

{#aDInatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Subjection, dependance, slavery: so {#aDI-#} {#natva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aDIna#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}. The gram- matical correctness of this word is questionable; see the E. of the preceding.
{#aDImanTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nTaH#}). The same as {#aDimanTa#} q. v.; the vowel in {#aDi#} being lengthened.

{#aDIyat#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-yan#}) A student who reads the Veda &c. with facility or ease. See {#aDIyAna#}. E. {#i (iN)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Satf#}. <div n="P">II. m. f. n. ({#-yan-yatI-yat#}) Remembering. E. {#i (ik)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Satf#}.
{#aDIyAna#}¦ m. ({#-naH#}) A student, one going over or reading the Vedas &c. E. {#i (iN)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#SAnac#}.

{#aDIra#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Unsteady, unstable (lit. or met.). <sup>2</sup> Perplexed, confused, not possessed of self- command. <sup>3</sup> Unwise. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-rA#}) <sup>1</sup> Lightning. <sup>2</sup> (In rhetoric.) A cross or ca- pricious mistress, one not possessed of self-command; with two varieties, the {#maDyA#} or adolescent dame who will ‘as- sail her lover with harsh speeches’ and the {#pragalBA#} or {#prOQA#} or mature dame who will ‘scold and beat him’. See also {#DIrA#} and {#DIrADIrA#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#DIra#}.
{#aDIratA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Fickleness, unsteadiness; also {#aDIratva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#aDIra#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#aDIvAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}). The same as {#aDivAsa#} II., the {#i#} in {#aDi#} being made long.
{#aDISa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}) A master, a lord. E. {#aDi#} and {#ISa#}.
{#aDISvara#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> An emperor, a king paramount over all the neighbouring princes. <sup>2</sup> An Arhat, according to the Jainas. E. {#aDi#} and {#ISvara#}.

{#aDunA#}¦ ind. Now, at present. E. {#aS#} (i. e. {#a#}, considered as a substitute of {#idam#}), taddh. aff. {#aDunA#}.
{#aDunAtana#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-naH-nI-nam#}) Of or belonging to the present. E. {#aDunA#}, taddh. aff. {#wyu#} and āgama {#tuw#}.
{#aDura#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Having no load (as a cart). E. {#a#} priv. and {#Dur#}, samāsānta aff. {#a#}.
{#aDfta#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unheld, undetained. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-taH#}) A name of Viṣṇu. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Dfta#}.

{#aDfti#}¦ I. Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Laxity, want of firm hold. <sup>2</sup> Want of steadiness or firmness. (In rhetoric described as one of the conditions connected with the Rasa Śṛṅgāra q. v.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#Dfti#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tiH-tiH-ti#}) Having no steadiness or firmness. E. {#a#} priv. and {#Dfti#}.
{#aDfzwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) <sup>1</sup> Ashamed, modest, humble. <sup>2</sup> Not overcome, invincible. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Dfzwa#}.

{#aDyAtmavid#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-t#}) One who knows the supreme spirit or the nature of ātman or soul. E. {#aDyAtma#} (I. or II.) and {#vid#}.
{#aDyAtmavidyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dyA#}). The same as {#aDyAtmajYAna#}. E. {#aDyAtma#} and {#vidyA#}.
{#aDyAtmika#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}). See {#ADyAtmika#} which is the more correct form of this word.

{#aDyApaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A teacher, esp. one who instructs in the sacred books. <sup>2</sup> (According to a legend in the Calcutta edition of the Harivanśa.) E. {#i (iN)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}. <div n="P">II. {#aDyAyin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yI-yinI-yi#}) Reading, studying. E. {#i (iN)#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini#}.

({#-paH#}) Fixing in or upon, transferring; but more especially used in philosophy, in the sense of transferring or attributing erroneously the predicates, nature &c. of one object to another, as those of a serpent to those of a rope &c. {#aDyAsana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Sitting on or upon. <sup>2</sup> Presiding over, ruling, inhabiting as chief. E. {#As#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#aDyAsayoga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) In Buddhistic doctrine, one of the 108 {#DarmAlokamuKa#} (q. v.), perhaps: excessive or profound meditation. E. {#aDyAsa#} and {#yoga#}.
{#aDyAsita#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Seated in or on. <sup>2</sup> Presiding over. <sup>3</sup> Inhabited. E. {#As#}, in the caus., with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDyAsin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-sI-sinI-si#}) Sitting on or upon. E. {#As#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini#}.
{#aDyAharaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}). The same as {#aDyAhAra#}. E. {#hf#} with {#A#} and {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#aDyAhartavya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vyaH-vyA-vyam#}). The same as {#aDyAhArya#} q. v. E. {#hf#} with {#A#} and {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#tavya#}.

{#aDyAhAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Adding a word or words to com- plete a sentence, supplying an ellipsis. <sup>2</sup> Reasoning, discuss- ing. See {#aDyAharaRa#}. E. {#hf#} with {#A#} and {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}.

{#aDyAhArya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ryaH-ryA-ryam#}) <sup>1</sup> To be discussed or argued. <sup>2</sup> To be added in order to complete a sentence, to [Page062-b+ 56] supply an ellipsis, as a word or words. E. {#hf#} with {#A#} and {#aDi#}, kṛtya aff. {#Ryat#}.

{#aDyAhfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Discussed, argued. <sup>2</sup> Added to complete a sentence, to supply an ellipsis, as a word or words. E. {#hf#} with {#A#} and {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#aDyuzita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Inhabited. <sup>2</sup> Arrived at, obtained. (See {#samayADyuzita#}.) E. {#vas#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#} and āgama {#iw#}.
{#aDyuzwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) Bound or tied over, coiled up. See the following. E. {#ucC#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.

E. {#aDyuzwa#} and {#valaya#}.
{#aDyuzwra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-zwraH#}) A litter drawn or carried by a camel. E. {#aDi#} and {#uzwra#}.

({#-QaH#}) A name of Śiva. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-QA#}) A superseded wife, one whose husband has married others. E. {#vah#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}. {#aDyUzivas#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zivAn-zuzI-zivas#}) Having in- habited (in the sense of {#luN, laN#} and {#liw#} qq. vv.). E. {#vas#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#kvasu#}.
{#aDyUhana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Covering over, esp. with ashes and coals. (Used principally in ritual works.) E. {#Uh#} with {#aDi#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#aDriyamARa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Not held &c. See {#Df#}. <sup>2</sup> (In law.) Not alive, not surviving. E. {#a#} neg. and {#DriyamARa#}.

{#aDvara#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Not crooked, honest proper (ved.) <sup>2</sup> Not perishable, lasting (in its con- sequences, as a sacrifice; ved.). <sup>3</sup> Intent, attentive. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Sacrifice in general, but in the ritual works mostly used as the denomination of the greater sacrifices or those performed with the juice of the Soma plant; see also {#sOmyADvara#} and {#aDvarakARqa#}. <sup>2</sup> The name of a Vasu (q. v.). <sup>3</sup> The proper name of the chief of a renowned fa- mily. {#aDvaryu#}¦ m. ({#-ryuH#}) <sup>1</sup> One desirous of having a sacrifice insti- tuted for one's self (used in this sense in the Rigveda). <sup>2</sup> A priest in general (ved.) <sup>3</sup> (In the ritual and the epic litera- ture.) A special priest, one conversant with and performing the ritual observances connected with the Yajurveda; he is one of the sixteen Ṛtvijs required for the performing of the great Soma sacrifices (see {#ftvij#}) and, amongst them, one of the four leading priests (see besides {#brahman, udgAtf#} and {#hotf#}) who receive the whole dakṣiṇā (q. v.); his pu- rushas or assistant priests are the {#pratiprasTAtf, nezwwa#} and {#unnetf#} who are called, like himself, the {#dIkzayitf#} (q. v.) because they initiate, viz. the {#aDvaryu#} the three other leading priests, the {#pratiprasTAtf#} the {#arDin-#} (q. v.), the {#nezwf#} the {#tftIyin-#} (q. v.) and the {#unnetf#} the {#pAdin-#} (q. v.) priests. The Mi- mānsā decides in doubtful cases, viz. whenever a sacrifice mentioned in and making part of the ritual of the Yajur- veda, is mentioned also and forms part of another Veda, whether the Adhwaryu has another priest to share in his functions or whether he has to abstain from the pro- ceedings altogether. The ten {#camasADvaryu#} (q. v.), who, are also assistants or purushas of the Adhwaryu, are dis- tinct from and do not bear the name of Ṛtvij.--According to a legend in the Harivanśa, Nārāyaṇa created the first Adhwaryu from his arms. The dual {#aDvaryu#} is the collective denomination of the {#aDvaryu#} and {#pratiprasTAtf#}, his principal assistant; the plur. {#aDvaryavaH#} of the {#aDvaryu#} and his three assistants, and in general of those devoted to the study or the practice of the Yajurveda. <sup>4</sup> The Yajurveda (also in the plur. {#aDvaryavaH#}). E. {#aDvary#}, kṛt aff. {#u#}.

{#anadDA#}¦ Tatpur. ind. (ved.) Not clearly, not truly, perhaps. Also with the particles {#u#} and {#iva, anadDo#} and {#anadDeva#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#adDA#}.
{#anadDApuruza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) (ved.) No man in the true sense of the word, ‘one who does not serve the ends of the gods, of the pitṛs, or of men’. E. {#anadDA#} and {#puruza#}.

{#anadya#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-dyaH-dyA-dyam#}) Not fit to be eaten. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-dyaH#}) White mustard. See {#anaGa#} which is the more correct reading of this word. E. {#a#} neg. and {#adya#}.

{#anadyatana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-naH#}) (In grammar.) The time which does not belong to the current day. See {#adyatana#}. It is either {#BUtAnadyatanaH#} the past or {#BavizyadanadyatanaH#} the future time, if such a period does not include the current day. E. {#a#} priv. and {#adyatana#}, sc. {#kAla#}.
{#anaDikAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Absence of right, claim, in- terest or concern. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDikAra#}.
{#anaDikAracarcA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-rcA#}) Officiousness, meddling with other people's business. E. {#anaDikAra#} and {#carcA#}.
{#anaDikArin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rI#}) One who has no right or claim &c. See the meanings of {#aDikArin#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDikArin#}.
{#anaDikfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not set over, or appointed &c. See the meanings of {#aDikfta#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDikfta#}.
{#anaDigata#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not acquired. <sup>2</sup> Not learnt or studied. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDigata#}.
{#anaDInaka#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-nakaH-nikA-nakam#}) Independant. E. {#a-#} {#aDIna#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.

{#anaDyakza#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-kzaH-kzA-kzam#}) I. Tatpur. Imperceptible, unperceived, absent. See {#apratyakza#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDyakza#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. Having no superintendent. E. {#a#} priv. and {#aDyakza#}.
{#anaDyayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Want or intermission of reading or study, especially of the Vedas. E. {#a#} neg. and {#aDyayana#}.

{#anaDyAya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-yaH#}) Time on which it is improper and forbidden to read or to study the Vedas; also used in the sense of ‘a holy-day’ or ‘vacation’. E. {#a#} priv. and {#aDyAya#}, sc. {#kAla#}.
{#anaDyAyadivasa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-saH#}) A day on which it is improper to study. See the preceding. E. {#anaDyAya#} and {#divasa#}.
{#anana#}¦ n. ({#-nam#}) Breathing, living. E. {#an#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
{#ananaNgamejaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Not allowing the body to remain unshaken or quiet. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anaNgamejaya#}.

{#ananuBAzaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) (In the Nyāya philosophy.) Not repeating the argument for discussion, i. e. a tacit agreement with it or assent to the assertion of the person [Page067-b+ 56] who has proposed it; viz. if, after the argument for dis- cussion has been announced, it has not been repeated by any one--the sign of taking it up--the proposer has to proclaim it three times; if then it does not meet with the anubhāṣana, it is considered as proved or as accepted as such. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anuBAzaRa#}.
{#ananuzaNgin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-NgI-NgiRI-Ngi#}) Not attached to, indifferent (as to pleasure &c.). E. {#a#} neg. and {#anu-#} {#zaNgin#}.
{#ananuzWAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Non-observance (of duties &c.), neglect, want of propriety. See the meanings of {#anuzWAna#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anuzWAna#}.
{#ananUkta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not spoken-after or accordingly. <sup>2</sup> Not read or studied (as the Veda). E. {#a#} neg. and {#anUkta#}.

{#ananta#}¦ Bahuvr. I. m. f. n. ({#-ntaH-ntA-ntam#}) Endless in time and space: eternal, unbounded, innumerable &c. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-ntaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa. <sup>2</sup> A name of Baladeva, the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa. <sup>3</sup> A name of Śiva. <sup>4</sup> A name of Rudra, in an Upanishad of the Athar- vaveda. <sup>5</sup> A name of Śeṣa, the chief of the Nāgas or ser- pent race that inhabit the infernal regions: the couch and constant attendant of Viṣṇu. <sup>6</sup> A name of Vāsuki, another king of the serpents, the brother of the former. <sup>7</sup> A name of one of the Viśvadevas. <sup>8</sup> The name of the fourteenth of the twenty-four Arhats or Jaina deified saints of the present Avasarpiṇī; see also {#anantajit#}. <sup>9</sup> The name of a king of Kashmir; see also {#anantadeva#}. <sup>10</sup> A proper name common to several authors &c. <sup>11</sup> The name of a plant, Vitex trifolia (Lin.); see {#sindavAra#}. <sup>12</sup> Talc (see {#aBraka#}; in this sense the word is given by some as a neuter). <sup>13</sup> (In arithmetic.) Infinite quantity: a fraction having a cypher for its deno- minator; see also {#anantarASi#} and {#Kahara#}. <sup>14</sup> The name of the twenty-third of the lunar asterisms; see {#SravaRa#}. <sup>15</sup> A silken cord with fourteen knots which the Hindus tie round the right arm at the festival of Anantachaturdaśī. <div n="P">III. f. ({#-ntA#}) <sup>1</sup> The earth. <sup>2</sup> (In arithmetic sometimes used to denominate) the numeral one. <sup>3</sup> A name of Pār- vatī, the wife of Śiva. <sup>4</sup> A name of Tārā, a Buddhist deity. <sup>5</sup> The proper name of the wife of Janamejaya. <sup>6</sup> The name of the following plants: <sup>a.</sup> Hedysarum alhagi; see {#yavAsa#} or {#rodanI#}. <sup>b.</sup> Echytes frutescens; see {#SyAmA#} or {#go-#} {#pI#}. <sup>c.</sup> A sort of potherb; see {#viSalyA#} or {#SakrapuzpI#}. <sup>d.</sup> Agrostis linearis (Koen.) or Panicum dactylon; see {#dUrvA#} or {#BArgavI#}, {#SvetadUrvA#} and {#nIladUrvA#}. <sup>e.</sup> Phyllanthus emblica (emblic my- robolan); see {#AmalakI#}. <sup>f.</sup> Menispermum glabrum or cordi- folium; see {#guqUcI#}. <sup>g.</sup> Gloriosa superba; see {#lANgalI#}. <sup>h.</sup> See {#hemamAnI#}. <sup>i.</sup> Premna spinosa; see {#asimanTa#}. <sup>k.</sup> Piper longum (Long pepper); see {#pippalI#} or {#kaRA#}. <sup>l.</sup> Terminalia chebula (yellow myrobolan); see {#harItakI#}. <sup>m.</sup> Asclepias pseudosar- sa; see {#SArivA#}. <sup>n.</sup> Justicia adhatoda(?). <sup>o.</sup> Bromelia Ana- nas(?). <sup>p.</sup> Echytes dichotoma(?). <sup>q.</sup> According to some also the same as {#anantamUla#} q. v. <div n="P">IV. n. ({#-ntam#}) <sup>1</sup> Sky, atmosphere, æther. <sup>2</sup> Talc; (also given in the latter sense as a masculine). E. {#a#} priv. and {#anta#}.

{#anantaka#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Endless, eternal, unlimited. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-kam#}) (In the Jaina doctrine.) The collective ex- pression for what is eternal viz. matter and soul; but in- cluding also, according to a commentary, planets or accord- ing to another, æther, regions &c. E. {#ananta#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}, or rather a Bahuvr. composed of {#a#} neg. and {#anta#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#anantakara#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rI-ram#}) Making endless or unlimited. E. {#ananta#} and {#kara#}.
{#anantaga#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-gaH-gA-gam#}) Going continually, moving perpetually. E. {#ananta#} and {#ga#}.

{#anantacaturdaSI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-SI#}) The fourteenth lunation of the light half i. e. the day of the full moon of the month Bhādra (August-September), when Viṣṇu under the form of the serpent Ananta is worshipped. E. {#ananta#} and {#caturdaSI#}.
{#anantacAritra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-traH#}) The proper name of a Bo- dhisattva, Mahāsattva, or a superior Bauddha saint. E. {#ananta#} and {#cAritra#}.

{#anantajit#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jit#}) The name of the fourteenth of the twenty-four Arhats or Jaina deified saints of the present Avasarpiṇī; also called {#ananta#}. E. {#ananta#} and {#jit#} ‘who conquers, who gains eternity’.
{#anantatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Eternity: also {#anantatva#} n. ({#-tvam#}). E. {#ananta#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#anantadfzwi#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-zwiH#}) A name of Śiva. E. {#ananta#} and {#dfzwi#}.

{#anantadeva#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-vaH#}) The proper name of a king of Kashmir, the son of Harirāja; also a proper name be- longing to several authors &c. See also {#ananta#}. E. {#ananta#} and {#deva#}.
{#anantanemi#}¦ Bahuvr.(?) m. ({#-miH#}) The proper name of a king of Mālava, a contemporary of Śākyamuni. E. {#ananta#} and {#nemi#}.
{#anantapAla#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-laH#}) The proper name of a warrior chief serving under Harsha, king of Kashmir. E. {#ananta#} and {#pAla#}.
{#anantamati#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-tiH#}) The proper name of a Bodhi- sattva or Bauddha saint, the son of the Tathāgata Chan- drasūryapradīpa. E. {#ananta#} and {#mati#}.
{#anantamUla#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-laH#}) The name of a plant (Periploca Indica or Asclepias pseudosarsa or Asclepias asthmatica); see also {#anantA#} and {#SArivA#}. E. {#ananta#} and {#mUla#}.

{#anantara#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Having nothing in- termediate, having no interval or defect, uninterrupted, entire; in the Upanishads also as an epithet of Brahman (n.) or the supreme soul, of which it is said that it has nothing before it nor after it, nor between ‘before’ and ‘after’ it nor besides it, or that it exists without interruption or defect, entire. <sup>2</sup> Next, immediately following or pre- ceding. <sup>3</sup> Next of kin, in succession, in caste. <sup>4</sup> Close, compact.--{#anantaram#} immediately, afterwards; it is fol- lowed or preceded sometimes by a noun depending upon it in the ablative or genitive. E. {#a#} priv. and {#anantara#}.

{#anantaraja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}) The son of a man of the three first castes, married to a woman of a caste inferior in order [Page068-b+ 56] to his own, but not to a Sūdra woman viz. of a Brāhmaṇa by a Kṣatriyā or Vaiśyā and of a Kṣatriyā by a Vaiśyā. The three kinds of sons got by parents of the same caste are called {#sajAtija#} and both, comprising six kinds, have the privileges of a Dvija or twice-born man. (This is the explanation given by a commentator of Manu and, according to him, {#anantaraja#} would have a different mean- ing than {#anantarajAta#}, though both words appear to be synonymes.) E. {#anantara#} and {#ja#}.

{#anantarajAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) The son of a father married to a woman of a caste next in order to his own, viz. of a Brāhmaṇa by a Kṣatriyā, of a Kshatriya by a Vaiśyā, of a Vaiśya by a Sūdrā. E. {#anantara#} and {#jAta#}.
{#anantarAyam#}¦ Bahuvr. ind. Without interruption. E. {#a#} priv. and {#antarAya#}.
{#anantarASi#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-SiH#}) (In arithmetic.) Infinite quantity: a fraction having a cypher for its denominator. See also {#ananta#} II. 13. and {#Kahara#}. E. {#ananta#} and {#rASi#}.
{#anantarita#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Uninterrupted, not separated by. E. Denom. of {#anantara#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.
{#anantarIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Belonging to what is next, next in succession, caste &c. See the meanings of {#anantara#}. E. {#anantara#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#anantarUpa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-paH-pA-pam#}) Having innumerable forms or shapes, multiform. E. {#ananta#} and {#rUpa#}.
{#anantarhita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not separated, not interposed. <sup>2</sup> Not concealed, not hidden. E. {#a#} neg. and {#antarhita#}.

{#anantavat#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-vAn-vatI-vat#}) Endowed with infinity, eternal. <div n="P">II. m. ({#-vAn#}) A name or epithet of one of the four pā- das or feet of Brahman (in the symbolical language of the Upanishads), consisting of four Kalās or parts, viz. earth, intermediate space, heaven and ocean. The other three feet are called {#prakASavat, jyotizmat#} and {#Ayatanavat#} (qq. vv.).
{#anantavarman#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-rmA#}) The proper name of a king. E. {#ananta#} and {#varman#}.

{#anantavAta#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-taH#}) (In medicine.) One of the diseases of the head (see {#Siroroga#}). It is described in the following manner: ‘when the three humours (air, bile and phlegm) are deranged in the vessels of the back of the neck they make it very feverish and painful and it sup- presses the humours particularly in the region of the eyes, eyebrows and temples; it then produces shaking in the sides of the cheeks, cramp of the jaws and morbid affec- tions of the eyes’. E. {#ananta#} and {#vAta#}.
{#anantavikramin#}¦ m. ({#-mI#}) The proper name of a Bodhisattva or Bauddha saint. E. {#ananta-vikrama#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.
{#anantavijaya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-yaH#}) The name of the shell of Yu- dhiṣṭhira. E. {#ananta#} and {#vijaya#}.
{#anantavIrya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-ryaH#}) The proper name of the twenty- third Jaina Arhat or deified saint of a future age or Utsar- piṇī. E. {#ananta#} and {#vIrya#}.

{#anantavrata#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-tam#}) The name of a festival ob- served on the day of the full moon in Bhādra (August- [Page069-a+ 56] September) in honour of Viṣṇu under the form of the serpent Ananta (q. v.). See {#anantacaturdaSI#}. E. {#ananta#} and {#vrata#}.
{#anantaSakti#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-ktiH#}) The proper name of a son of the king Amaraśakti. E. {#ananta#} and {#Sakti#}.
{#anantaSayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The name of Travancore. E. {#ananta#} and {#Sayana#}.
{#anantaSIrzA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-rzA#}) The proper name of the wife of Vāsuki, a king of the serpents. E. {#ananta#} and {#SIrza#}; literally: ‘having innumerous heads’.
{#anantaSuzma#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-zmaH#}) (ved.) Of infinite power or strength; an epithet of the Maruts. E. {#ananta#} and {#Suzma#}.
{#anantya#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-ntyaH-ntyA-ntyam#}) Infinite, eternal, unbounded. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-ntyam#}) Infinity, eternity, immortality. cf. {#Anantya#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#antya#}.

{#ananda#}¦ Bahuvr. m. pl. ({#-ndAH#}) (In the Upanishads) the name of a world where those are doomed to reside after their death, who have not acquired spiritual knowledge or who have made to a priest a sacrificial gift of an old or de- fective cow &c. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nanda#}; literally: ‘having or giving no pleasure or joy’.
{#ananna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nnam#}) No-food, no-corn, bad food, bad corn &c. See the meanings of {#anna#}. E. {#a#} deter. and {#anna#}.

{#ananya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-nyaH-nyA-nyam#}) I. Tatpur. Not different, same, identical. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. <sup>1</sup> Without another, one, sole. <sup>2</sup> Fixed on one object, having no other object or occupation. E. {#a#} priv. and {#anya#}.

{#ananyagati#}¦ I. Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) No other refuge, asylum or hope, one only refuge &c. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya-gati#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tiH-tiH-ti#}) Having but one refuge, asylum or hope. E. {#a#} priv. and {#anya-gati#}.
{#ananyagatika#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Having but one refuge, asylum or hope. E. {#ananyagati#} II, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#ananyacinta#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ntaH-ntA-ntam#}) Having the thoughts fixed on one only object. E. {#ananya#} and {#cintA#}.
{#ananyaja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}) A name of Kāma or Love. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya-ja#} ‘produced by nothing else than the manas or heart’.
{#ananyatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) or {#ananyatva#} n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> Sameness, identity. <sup>2</sup> Singleness. E. {#ananya#} I. and II., taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#ananyadeva#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Having no other gods. E. {#a#} priv. and {#anya-deva#}.
{#ananyanizpAdya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dyaH-dyA-dyam#}) What cannot be done or accomplished by any one else. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya-nizpAdya#}.

{#ananyapUrva#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-rvaH-rvA-rvam#}) Intact, never in the prior possession of another. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-rvA#}) A girl not previously wedded, a virgin. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya-pUrva#}. Also with taddh. aff. {#kan, ananya-#} {#pUrvaka#} m. f. n. ({#-rvakaH-rvikA-rvakam#}).
{#ananyapratikriya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Having no other remedy. E. {#a#} priv. and {#anya-pratikriyA#}.
{#ananyaBava#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Produced or effected [Page069-b+ 56] by no one or nothing else, by one particular person or thing. E. {#ananya#} and {#Bava#}.
{#ananyamanas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-nAH-nAH-naH#}) Intent, attentive, having the mind fixed on one subject, not absent. E. {#ananya#} and {#manas#}.
{#ananyamanaska#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-skaH-skA-skam#}). The same as the preceding. E. {#ananyamanas#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#ananyamAnasa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-saH-sI-sam#}). The same as {#ananyamanas#}. E. {#ananya#} and {#mAnasa#}.
{#ananyavftti#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ttiH-ttiH-tti#}) Having the mind fixed on one object, intent, attentive. E. {#ananya#} and {#vftti#}.
{#ananyahfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not stolen or taken, safe. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anya-hfta#}.
{#ananyAdfSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SI-Sam#}) Not like another, unusual, extraordinary. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anyAdfSa#}.

{#ananyArTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rTaH-rTA-rTam#}) What exists or is done &c. not for any one or any thing else, what exists &c. on its own behalf, principal, absolute (e. g. a sacrifice). The reverse of {#anyArTa#}. E. {#a#} and {#anyArTa#}.

{#ananyASrita#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not supported by or dependant upon another, independant. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-tam#}) (In law.) Unencumbered property. E. {#a#} and {#anya-ASrita#}.

{#ananvaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) (In rhetoric.) One of the Ālaṅkā- ras or figures of speech: comparing an object to itself, with respect to its being the only one of its class as to the qua- lities expressed and therefore not liable to comparison with any thing else; e. g. the moon shines like a moon i. e. like a very moon, a moon indeed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anvaya#}, literally: ‘want of connexion sc. with other objects’.
{#ananvita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unconnected with, inconsistent, incoherent. <sup>2</sup> Devoid of, not possessing. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anvita#}.
{#anapa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-paH-pA-pam#}) Destitute of water. E. {#a#} priv. and {#ap#}, samāsānta aff. {#a#}.
{#anapakaraRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}). The same as the following. E. {#a#} neg. and {#apakaraRa#}.

{#anapakarman#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}) 1. Not doing ill, evil &c. (The re- verse of {#apakarman#} q. v.) 2. (In law.) <sup>1</sup> Not delivering (a gift). <sup>2</sup> Not paying or acquitting (debts, wages). See also {#anapakaraRa, anapakriyA, anapAkaraRa, anapAkarman#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#apakarman#}.
{#anapakAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Harmlessness, freedom from hatred &c. (The reverse of {#apakAra#} q. v.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#apakAra#}.
{#anapakArin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rI-riRI-ri#}) Innocuous &c. (The reverse of {#apakArin#}.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#apakArin#}.
{#anapakriyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-yA#}). The same as {#anapakarman#} q. v. E. {#a#} neg. and {#apakriyA#}.
{#anapaga#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-gaH-gA-gam#}) Not departing, not being separated from. E. {#a#} neg. and {#apaga#}.
{#anapacyuta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) (ved.) Not fallen off, not diminished in power &c., irresistible; as an epithet of Soma, Indra &c. E. {#a#} neg. and {#apacyuta#}.

{#anapajayya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-yyaH-yyA-yyam#}) (ved.) What has no possibility of being made un-conquered or un-victorious [Page070-a+ 56] (as a victory). {#anapajayyam#} used also adverbially: so as not to become un-victorious (e. g. to conquer so as not to have a barren victory, as not to have the ennemy rising again). E. {#a#} priv. and {#apajayya#}.

{#anapatya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tyaH-tyA-tyam#}) <sup>1</sup> Childless, having no progeny. <sup>2</sup> (ved.) Prejudicial to progeny. <sup>3</sup> (ved. Tatpur.) What causes to fall, unpropitious(?). E. {#a#} priv. and {#apatya#}.
{#anapatyaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}). The same as {#ana-#} {#patya#}. E. {#anapatya#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.
{#anapatyatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) Childlessness, want of progency. E. {#ana-#} {#patya#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#}.

{#anAdizwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not assigned, not appointed, not fixed. <sup>2</sup> Not commanded, not directed. <sup>3</sup> Not allowed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Adizwa#}.
{#anAdfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not respected. <sup>2</sup> Dis- respected, disregarded, despised. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Adfta#}.

{#anADfzwi#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-zwiH#}) <sup>1</sup> The proper name of <sup>a.</sup> a prince, the son of Śura by Bhojyā, or according to others by Māriṣā, and brother of Vasudeva; his wife is Aśmakī and his son Ninartaśatru or according to another reading, Nirvṛttiśatru; <sup>b.</sup> a son of Ugrasena and chief of the Yā- davas. <sup>2</sup> A name or epithet of Ṛcheyu, the son of Rau- drāśva. {#anAraBya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ByaH-ByA-Byam#}) What cannot or aught not to be begun or attempted. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AraBya#}.

{#anAraByavAda#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-daH#}) An injunction (concerning sa- crifices or vaidik rites) not connected with the books or chapters which treat authoritatively on sacrifices &c. in the regular order. See {#AraByavAda#} and the following. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AraByavAda#}.

{#anAraByADIta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not read in con- nexion with chapters or books treating authoritatively on vaidik rites or sacrifices; said of passages, esp. in the Brāhmaṇas, which treat on rites, sacrifices &c. not to be connected with other passages with which they may happen [Page078-a+ 56] to be found together, the injunctions of the latter not be- ing applicable to those of the former. {#anAyatikta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ktaH#}) A medicinal plant, a kind of gentian (Gentiana cherayta, Rox.) See also {#kirAtatikta#}. E. {#anArya#} I. 2. and {#tikta#}.

{#anArza#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rzaH-rzI-rzam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not relating or be- longing to a Ṛṣi (to his name &c.). <sup>2</sup> Not relating to the vaidik hymns (considered as the inspirations of the Ṛṣis). E. {#a#} neg. and {#Arza#}.
{#anArzeya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yI-yam#}) Not relating or be- longing to a Ṛṣi. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Arzeya#}.

{#anAlamba#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-mbaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Want of support. <sup>2</sup> Despon- dency, heart-brokenness. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Alamba#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-mbaH-mbA-mbam#}) Without support or stay, unsupported. E. {#a#} priv. and {#Alamba#}.
{#anAlambana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Without stay or support, unsupported. <sup>2</sup> Despondent, heart-broken. E. {#a#} priv. and {#Alambana#}.
{#anAlambanatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) <sup>1</sup> Unsupportedness. <sup>2</sup> Despondency, heart-brokenness. E. {#anAlambana#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#}.
{#anAlambI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-mbI#}) The Vīṇā or lute of Śiva. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AlambI#}.
{#anAlambukA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kA#}). See the following.
{#anAlamBukA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kA#}) A woman during menstruation. This word occurs only in ritual works and is sometimes, though less correctly written {#anAlambukA#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AlamBukA#}.
{#anAlApa#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) Taciturnity, silence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AlApa#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-paH-pA-pam#}) Silent, taciturn. E. {#a#} priv. and {#AlApa#}.
{#anAlocita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unseen, unbe- held. <sup>2</sup> Unweighed, unconsidered, rash, imprudent. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Alocita#}.
{#anAvidDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dDaH-dDA-dDam#}) Not pierced, not wounded, not hurt. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AvidDa#}.
{#anAvila#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Clear, clean, pure. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Avila#}.
{#anAvfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Uncovered, unhidden. <sup>2</sup> Open, uninclosed (as a field &c.). E. {#a#} neg. and {#Avfta#}.
{#anAvftta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ttaH-ttA-ttam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not turned round. <sup>2</sup> Not retreating. <sup>3</sup> Not approached, not visited. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Avftta#}.
{#anAvftti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ttiH#}) Not-returning, literally and me- taphorically (as after death into this world). E. {#a#} neg. and {#Avftti#}.
{#anAvfzwi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-zwiH#}) Drought. E. {#a#} neg. and {#A-vfzwi#} (explained with {#samantAdvfzwi#}). See also under {#anA#}.
{#anAvedita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not made known, not announced. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Avedita#}.
{#anASa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SA-Sam#}) I. Without hope, hope- less. E. {#a#} priv. and {#ASA#}. <div n="P">II. Not dead, living. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nASa#}. The latter meaning is artificial.
{#anASaka#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-kam#}) Fasting. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASaka#}.
{#anASakanivftta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ttaH#}) One who desists from fast- ing (as a Sannyāsin who returns to his home &c.). E. {#anASaka#} and {#nivftta#}.
{#anASakAyana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The penitence of fasting. E. {#anASaka#} and {#ayana#}.
{#anASasta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-staH-stA-stam#}) Not excellent, not praiseworthy; (according to a vaidik commentary). E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASasta#}.
{#anASin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SI-SinI-Si#}) Not perishing, not being lost. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nASin#}.

{#anASu#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-SuH-SuH-Su#}) I. Tatpur. Not quick, slow. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASu#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. (ved.) Without destruction, indestructible, unchecked (as horses going extremely fast). This meaning seems doubtful. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nASu(?)#}.
{#anASya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SyaH-SyA-Syam#}) Indestructible. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nASya#}.
{#anASramavAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}). See {#anASramevAsa#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASramavAsa#}.
{#anASramin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-mI#}) One not belonging to one of the āśramas (q. v.) or religious orders. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASramin#}.

{#anASraya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Without an asylum or refuge, unprotected. E. {#a#} priv. and {#ASraya#}.

{#anASrita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not connected with, not resorting to, esp. not belonging to one of the āśramas (q. v.) or religious orders. <sup>2</sup> (In philosophy.)
