E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASrita#}.
{#anASvas#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SvAn-SuzI-SvaH#}) Not having eaten, fasting. E. {#a#} neg. and {#ASvas#} (from {#aS#} to eat).
{#anAzwra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-zwraH-zwrA-zwram#}) (ved.) Free from ene- mies, free from mischievous beings. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nAzwra#}.
{#anAsika#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Noseless. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nAsikA#}.
{#anAsTA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-sTA#}) <sup>1</sup> Want of fixity or condition. <sup>2</sup> Disregard, want of consideration. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AsTA#}.
{#anAsTAna#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Without a fixed site, without a basis or foundation. E. {#a#} priv. and {#AsTAna#}.

{#anAhata#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unhurt, unbeaten, unwounded. <sup>2</sup> Unwashed, new (as cloth). <sup>3</sup> (In music.) Not beat or struck, not produced in the ordinary way (as a sound). See {#anAhatanAda#}. <div n="P">II. n. ({#-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> A new garment (see {#Ahata#}). <sup>2</sup> The fourth of the six mystical Chakras or circles of the body. E. {#a#} neg. and {#Ahata#}.

{#anAhatanAda#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-taH#}) A sound not produced in the ordinary manner; the mysterious sound (om) which is heard in consequence of religious meditation and which is said ‘not to give pleasure, but eternal bliss’; unlike the {#Ahata-#} {#nAda#} (q. v.) or the real musical sound. E. {#anAhata#} and {#nAda#}.

{#anAhAra#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Abstinence, starvation. <sup>2</sup> Non- seizure. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AhAra#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Not taking food. E. {#a#} priv. and {#AhAra#}.
{#anAhitAgni#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gniH#}) A householder who has not performed the ceremony of the {#agnyADAna#} q. v. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AhitAgni#}.
{#anAhitAgnitA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) or {#anAhitAgnitva#} n. ({#-tvam#}) The con- dition of an {#anAhitAgni#} q. v. E. The preceding, taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.
{#anAhuti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Not-sacrificing. <sup>2</sup> A bad or im- proper sacrificing. E. {#a#} neg. or deter. and {#Ahuti#}.
{#anAhUta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Uncalled, unbidden. E. {#a#} neg. and {#AhUta#}.
{#aniketa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Without a house. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niketa#}.
{#aniketana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Without a house. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niketana#}.
{#anikziptaDUra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) The proper name of a Bodhi- sattva or Bauddha deified saint. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nikziptaDUra(?)#}.
{#anikzu#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kzuH#}) A sort of long grass or reed (Saccharum spontaneum). E. {#a#} comp. and {#ikzu#} sugar-cane. Cf. {#ikzutulyA#}.
{#anigIrRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not swallowed. <sup>2</sup> (In rhetoric.) Not to be supplied, not being the object of an ellipsis. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nigIrRa#}.

{#anigraha#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) <sup>1</sup> Want of restraint &c. See {#nigraha#}. <sup>2</sup> (In Nyāya phil.) No-failure in argument, not perceiving one's self having failed in argument. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nigraha#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-haH-hA-ham#}) Unrestrained, uncon- fined. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nigraha#}.
{#anigrahasTAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) (In Nyāya phil.) No-failure in argument. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nigrahasTAna#}.
{#aniGAtezu#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-zuH#}) Probably a proper name or sur- name implying blame; lit. one whose arrows do no harm. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niGAta-izu#}.
{#anici#}.¦ See {#Aniceya#}.

{#anicCa#}¦ I. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-cCaH-cCA-cCam#}) Undesirous, in- different, disliking. E. {#a#} priv. and {#icCA#}. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. f. ({#-cCA#}) Absence of wish or desire, indif- ference, dislike. E. {#a#} neg. and {#icCA#}.

{#anitya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-tyaH-tyA-tyam#}) <sup>1</sup> Transient, not ever- lasting (as the body, or in the Sāṅkhya philosophy the discrete principles mahat, ahaṅkāra &c. or in the Nyāya the sound &c. <sup>2</sup> Occasional, not peremptory, not obligatory as a rule &c. (see also {#kAmya#}; as in the Jyotiṣṭoma the six samsthās: {#atyagnizwoma, ukTya, zoqaSin, atirAtra, aptoryAma#} and {#vAjapeya#} &c.). <sup>3</sup> Not necessary, not immutable. See {#anityasamAsa#}. <sup>4</sup> Unstable, inconstant. <sup>5</sup> Unusual, irregular. ({#anityam#} not always.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#nitya#}.
{#anityakarman#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-rma#}) An act of worship which is not peremptory, but voluntary and occasional. See {#kAmya-#} {#karman#}. E. {#anitya#} and {#karman#}.
{#anityakriyA#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-yA#}). The same as the preceding. E. {#anitya#} and {#kriyA#}.

{#anityatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) or {#anityatva#} n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> Impermanence, transient existence. <sup>2</sup> The being occasional, not peremptory. <sup>3</sup> The being not necessary. <sup>4</sup> Unstableness, inconstance. <sup>5</sup> Unusual occurrence. See the meanings of {#anitya#}. E. {#anitya#}. taddh. aff. {#tal#} or {#tva#}.

{#anityadatta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-ttaH#}) (In law.) A son given away by his natural parents temporarily or for a term. The adoption of such a son is performed without the homas or burnt offerings re- quired at the adoption of a nityadatta (q. v.). Also {#anityadattaka#} and {#anityadatrima#}. E. {#anitya#} and {#datta#}, temporarily given, scil. {#putra#}.
{#anityadattaka#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) (In law.) The same as {#anityadatta#} q. v. E. The preceding, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.
{#anityadatrima#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) (In law.) The same as {#ani-#} {#tyadatta#} q. v. E. {#anitya#} and {#datrima#}.
{#anityapratyavekzA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kzA#}) In Buddhist doctrine, one of the 108 {#DarmAlokamuKa#} (q. v.): the reflection that (every thing) is transitory. E. {#anitya#} and {#pratyavekzA#}.
{#anityaBAva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) The state or condition of what is transient or perishable, perishableness. E. {#anitya#} (in the sense of the genitive) and {#BAva#}.

{#anityasama#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. ({#-maH-mA#}) (In the Nyāya philosophy.) Wrongly generalizing the predicament of perishableness i. e. a sophism on perishableness; viz. arguing perishableness from the reason that every thing is perishable because it shares in some qualities with other things which are pe- rishable. E. {#anitya#} and {#sama#} (in the sense of {#jAti#}, sophism); the masc. form of this word is explained according to some, by the ellipsis of {#pratizeDa#} or contradiction, as a Sūtra in the Nyāya treating on a sophism is always followed by another containing the refutation; or, according to others, by the ellipsis of {#vikalpa#} (in the sense of {#viviDaH kalpaH#} i. e. {#prakAraH#} or variousness), there being various sophisms, viz. twenty-four; or according to others, by the ellipsis of {#prayoga#} i. e. a (logical) proceeding which likens or produces the plausibility of perishableness; or the word is taken as a Bahuvr. with the ellipsis of {#prayoga#} i. e. a logical proceeding in which perishableness is likened (viz. made plausible).-- As a feminine, {#˚samA#} is taken in the sense of {#jAti#}, sophism.
{#anityasamaprakaraRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) The chapter in the Nyāya philosophy which treats on the sophism {#anityasama#} q. v. E. {#anityasama#} and {#prakaraRa#}.

{#anityasamAsa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-saH#}) (In grammar.) A compound which may be dissolved into its constituent parts without under- going a material change of sense; e. g. {#rAjapuruzaH#}, which may be dissolved into {#rAjYaH puruzaH#}. The converse of {#nityasamAsa#} q. v.
{#anidra#}¦ I. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-draH-drA-dram#}) Sleepless, awake. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nidrA#}. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. f. ({#-drA#}) Want of sleep. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nidrA#}.
{#aniDi#}¦ Bahuvr. See {#AniDeya#}.
{#aniDfzwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) Not defeated, not overcome. Cf. {#aniBfzwa#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niDfzwa#}.
{#aniDma#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-DmaH-DmA-Dmam#}) Without fuel. E. {#a#} priv. and {#iDma#}.
{#anina#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Without a master, in- dependent. E. {#a#} priv. and {#ina#}.
{#anindita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Irreproachable, blame- less, virtuous, good. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nindita#}.
{#anindya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ndyaH-ndyA-ndyam#}) Irreproachable, blameless. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nindya#}.
{#anindra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ndraH-ndrA-ndram#}) <sup>1</sup> Deprived of Indra. <sup>2</sup> (ved.) Not paying regard to Indra, not holding Indra in esteem. E. {#a#} priv. and {#indra#}.
{#anindriya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-yam#}). The same as {#antaHkaraRa#} q. v. E. {#a#} neg. and {#indriya#}, ‘no-indriya (q. v.), different from the indriyas’.
{#anipadyamAna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Not falling down, not dejected, untiring. (ved.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#nipadyamAna#}.
{#anipAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) Not dying, remaining alive. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nipAta#}.

{#anibadDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dDaH-dDA-dDam#}) Not attached, not bound, not connected, incoherent. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nibadDa#}.

{#anibADa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-DaH-DA-Dam#}) Unconfined, un- restricted, extended. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nibADa#}.
{#aniBfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not modest, bold. <sup>2</sup> Not lonely, not private. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niBfta#}.
{#aniBfzwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) (ved.) Not defeated, not overcome, unhurt. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niBfzwa#}.
{#aniBfzwatavizi#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-ziH#}) (ved.) Of unhurt power, of unabated strength. E. {#aniBfzwa#} and {#tavizI#}.
{#aniBya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ByaH-ByA-Byam#}) Not wealthy, not opulent. E. {#a#} neg. and {#iBya#}.
{#animantrita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Uninvited, uncalled. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nimantrita#}.
{#animantritaBojin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-jI-jinI-ji#}) Eating without having being invited. E. {#animantrita#} and {#Bojin#}.
{#animAna#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Measureless, im- mense, boundless. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nimAna#}.

{#animiz#}¦ Tatpur. f. (only in the acc. {#-zam#} and instrum. {#-zA#}) (ved.) <sup>1</sup> The not twinkling. <sup>2</sup> Attentiveness, watchfulness. <sup>3</sup> Uninterruptedness. {#animizam#} and {#animizA#} <sup>1</sup> Attentively, watchfully. <sup>2</sup> Uninterruptedly, continually. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nimiz#}.

({#-zaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A god. <sup>2</sup> A fish. See also {#animeza#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nimiza#}. <div n="P">III. Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}). The same as {#animiz#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nimiz#}.

{#animizA#}¦ Tatpur. (ved.) See {#animiz#}.

({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not restrained, not fastened. <sup>2</sup> Not necessarily connected. <sup>3</sup> Not inevitable, not certain, not always occurring. <sup>4</sup> Not positive, not de- finite, undefined, undetermined. (The {#aniyatA DarmAH#} or ‘undetermined rules’ of the Buddhists, are the topic of one of the chapters of their Phātimokkha, and treat on transgressions that involve exclusion, suspension and pe- nance, but not permanent exclusion, of a Bauddha priest.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#niyata#}.
{#aniyatapuMskA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-skA#}) An unsteady or unchaste woman. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niyata-pum#} (Bahuvr. samāsānta aff. {#kap#}).
{#aniyatavftti#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ttiH-ttiH-tti#}) One who has no fixed profession or livelihood. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niyata-vftti#}.
{#aniyatANka#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-NkaH#}) (In Arithmetic.) An inde- terminate digit. E. {#aniyata#} and {#aNka#}.
{#aniyatAtman#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tmA#}) Not exercising self-control, not subduing one's mind. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niyata-Atman#}.

{#aniyama#}¦ 1. Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> Absence of a restriction or fixed rule. <sup>2</sup> Absence of moral or religious obligation. <sup>3</sup> In- decorous or improper conduct. E. {#a#} neg. and {#niyama#}. <div n="P">2. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-maH-mA-mam#}) Without restriction, undertermined, undefined, unprovided for, by any rule or law. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niyama#}.

{#aniyukta#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) Not authorised, not called, not appointed &c. See {#niyukta#}. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-ktaH#}) (In Law.) A Brāhmaṇa who attends a court without having been appointed a member of it, whose vote is therefore not binding, and who is at liberty to attend the court meetings and to debate in them, or not. (See, on the contrary, {#saBAsad#}.)

{#anira#}¦ (ved.) I. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Without food, without an offering (of clarified butter). E. {#a#} priv. and {#irA#}. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. f. ({#-rA#}) Want of food, famine, calamity, distress. E. {#a#} neg. and {#irA#}.

{#anirAkarizRu#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zRuH-zRuH-zRu#}) <sup>1</sup> Not disposed to or in the habit of throwing obstacles in the way, of being obstructive. <sup>2</sup> Not in the habit of disdaining, of dis- pising. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirAkarizRu#}.
{#anirAkfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unchecked, unob- structed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirAkfta#}.

{#anirukta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not spoken out, not declared. <sup>2</sup> Not explained, not defined (e. g. the di- vinity, if spoken of in general terms, or Brahma (n.) that is without qualities, or an invocation, not containing the special name of the god addressed, one addressed to the gods in general &c.). <sup>3</sup> Obscure, incomprehensible, literally and metaphorically; e. g. Prajāpati, Brahman (n.) or a hymn uttered inaudibly, so as not being comprehensible to the by-standers. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirukta#}.
{#aniruktagAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) One of the modes of chanting the hymns of the Sāmaveda. See {#gAna#}. E. {#anirukta#} and {#gAna#}.

{#anirudDa#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-dDaH-dDA-dDam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unobstructed, unrestrained. <sup>2</sup> Self-willed, ungovernable, headstrong. <sup>3</sup> Move- able, unsteady(?). <div n="P">2. m. ({#-dDaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The name of the son of Pradyumna or Kāmadeva by Śubhāṅgī or, according to others, Kaku- dvatī, the daughter of Rukmin; his wife is Uṣā, the daughter of Vāna, or, according to others, Subhadrā, the granddaughter of Rukmin, and his son Vajra.--The Vaiṣṇava sect, called Pāñcharātra or Bhāgavatas, con- sider him as an incarnation or part of Viṣṇu and identify him with Ahaṅkāra, self-consciousness.--<sup>2</sup> A name of Śiva. <sup>3</sup> The name of a celebrated Bauddha Arhat and con- temporary of Śākyamuni. <sup>4</sup> The name of a member of the Vṛṣṇi tribe, the descendants of Vṛṣṇi. See also {#AnirudDa#} and {#AnirudDAyani#}. <sup>5</sup> A spy(?). <div n="P">3. n. ({#-dDam#}) A rope for fastening cattle. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirudDa#}. (It is doubtful whether the meaning 1. 3. (move- able) or the meaning 2. 4. (spy) is the correct one, the translation being founded on the word {#cara#}, given as one of the meanings of {#anirudDa#}, but without any further in- dication as to the gender. From the place, however, {#cara#} occupies in the explanation of some of the native dictio- naries, the meaning ‘spy’ is likely to be preferable to the meaning ‘moveable’.)
{#anirudDapaTa#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-Tam#}) Atmosphere, æther. E. {#anirudDa#} and {#paTin#}, samāsānta aff. {#a#}; lit. having an unobstructed path.
{#anirudDaBAvinI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-nI#}) The wife of Aniruddha, Uṣā (q. v.). E. {#anirudDa#} and {#BAvinI#}.
{#anirjita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unsubdued, uncon- quered. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirjita#}.
{#anirRaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) Uncertainty. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirRaya#}.
{#anirRIta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unascertained, un- determined. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirRIta#}.

{#anirdaSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SA-Sam#}) Not out of, i. e. within, the ten days of impurity which follow after a case of birth or death. {#anirdaSam#} also used adverbially. See the following. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirdaSa#}; scil. {#ahan#}.
{#anirdaSAha#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-haH-hA-ham#}). The same as the preceding. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirdaSAha#}.
{#anirdizwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) Not defined or de- termined by a rule. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirdizwa#}.

{#anirdeSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Absence of rule or direction. <sup>2</sup> A bad or imperfect direction, a rule not conveying exactly the bearing or sense it is intended to have. E. {#a#} neg. or deter. and {#nirdeSa#}.
{#anirDArita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unascertained, un- determined, undefined. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirDArita#}.
{#anirmala#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-laH-lA-lam#}) Unclean, dirty. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirmala#}.

{#anirmAlyA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-lyA#}) A plant (Trigonella corniculata or Medicago esculenta, Rox.). Also {#nirmAlyA, laNka, pikA#}, {#pfkkA, piSunA#}, and ranging amongst the {#mahOzaDa#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirmAlya#}, according to a commentary ‘because no garland can be made of it’.
{#anirlocita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not considered, not reflected. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirlocita#}.
{#anirvacanIya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Not explainable, indescribable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirvacanIya#}.
{#anirvAcya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-cyaH-cyA-cyam#}) Not explainable, indescribable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirvAcya#}.

{#anirvAha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) <sup>1</sup> Want of completion. <sup>2</sup> Want of logical connexion (in a sentence &c.). <sup>3</sup> Want of means of subsistence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirvAha#}.
{#anirvfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unaccomplished, un- terminated. <sup>2</sup> Unhappy, discontented, ill at ease. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirvfta#}.
{#anirvfti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Incompleteness, want of com- pletion. <sup>2</sup> Discontent, unhappiness. <sup>3</sup> Poverty. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirvfti#}.
{#anirveda#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-daH#}) Undauntedness, hopefulness, self- confidence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nirveda#}.

{#anila#}¦ m. ({#-laH#}) <sup>1</sup> Wind, viz. <sup>a.</sup> (in its usual acceptation) the motion of air; <sup>b.</sup> the deity of wind; <sup>c.</sup> one of the eight Maruts, and in this sense distinct from {#mAruta, vAyu#} &c. (see {#marut#}); <sup>d.</sup> one of the eight Vasus (see {#vasu#}); <sup>e.</sup> (in the plural {#anilAH#}) a class of the Gaṇadevatās, comprising forty-nine Anilas; <sup>f.</sup> (in medicine) one of the three Rasas or temperamental elements of the body (see {#rasa#}), subdi- vided into {#prARa, udAna, samAna, vyAna#} and {#apAna#}; in this sense used synonymously with {#mAruta, vAta, vAyu, samIraRa#} and other words meaning wind; <sup>g.</sup> (in the terminology of the Upanishads) the exterior wind or the surrounding air, in distinction from {#vAyu#} or {#prARa#}, the vital air of the body. <sup>2</sup> A proper name of <sup>a.</sup> a son of Tansu and father of Du- shwanta; <sup>b.</sup> a Rākṣasa; <sup>c.</sup> a Ṛṣi, author of a vaidik hymn; <sup>d.</sup> (in the mythology of the Jainas) the seventeenth Arhat of the past Utsarpiṇī. <sup>3</sup> (In arithmetic, sometimes used to denote) the numeral 49 (there being forty-nine Anilas). <sup>4</sup> A mystic denomination of the letter {#ya#}. E. {#an#}, uṇ. aff. {#ilac#}.

{#anilakumAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. pl. ({#-rAH#}) (In the mythology of the Jainas.) One of the ten kinds of Bhavanapatis (q. v.) or Bhavanādhīśas (q. v.), the first of the four classes of Jaina divinities. E. {#anila#} and {#kumAra#}.
{#anilaGna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-GnaH-GnI-Gnam#}) Removing disorders from wind (see {#anila#} 1. f.), as a medicine &c. Also {#vAtaGna#}, {#vAyuGna#} &c. E. {#anila#} and {#Gna#}.
{#anilaGnaka#}¦ m. ({#-kaH#}) A large tree (Terminalia belerica). See also {#viBItaka#}. E. {#anilaGna#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.

{#anilaparyAya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) (In Medicine.) An inflammation affecting the whole eye, described as produced from the vitiated Rasa wind (see {#anila#} 1. f.) ‘which pervades the eye- lids, eye and eyebrows and makes them diseased one after the other’. The less correct reading of this word is {#anilapayaya#}. See also {#mArutaparyAya#} and {#vAtaparyAya#}. E. {#anila#} and {#paryAya#}.
{#anilaprakfti#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tiH-tiH-ti#}) Of airy or windy nature; an epithet of the planet Saturn. E. {#anila#} and {#prakfti#}.

{#anilamBasamADi#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-DiH#}) A fanciful name of a Buddhistic samādhi or profound meditation. E. {#anilamBa#} and {#samADi#}, meaning perhaps ‘a meditation that sur- [Page082-b+ 56] passes all impediments or limits, one which nothing can resist’.

{#anilayana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) No-resting place, no-support (an epithet of the neuter Brahman, in an Upanishad, be- cause it is devoid of qualities, impersonal &c.). E. {#a#} neg. and {#nilayana#}.

{#anilavyADi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-DiH#}) (In Medicine.) Derangement of the Rasa wind (see {#anila#} 1. f.), produced, according to the native theory, by the continued use of dry, cold or light articles of food, taken in unusually small quantities &c. and causing, according to some authorities, eighty varieties of nervous diseases. See also {#anilAmaya#} and {#vAtavyADi#}. E. {#anila#} and {#vyADi#}.
{#anilasaKa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-KaH#}) A name of Fire. Cf. {#agnisaKa#}. E. {#anila#} and {#saKi#}, samāsānta aff. {#wac#}, ‘the friend of Wind’.
{#anilahan#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-hA-GnI-ha#}) The same as {#anilaGna#} q. v. E. {#anila#} and {#han#}.
{#anilahft#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-t-t-t#}) The same as {#anilaGna#} q. v. E. {#anila#} and {#hft#}.
{#anilAtmaja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of Hanumat. <sup>2</sup> A name of Bhīma. See also {#vAyuputra#} and similar synonymes. E. {#anila#} and {#Atmaja#}.
{#anilAntaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) The name of a plant. See {#iNgudI#} or {#aNgArapuzpa#}. E. {#anila#} and {#antaka#}, in the same sense as {#anilaGna#}.
{#anilApaha#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-haH-hA-ham#}) The same as {#anilaGna#} q. v. E. {#anila#} and {#apaha#}.
{#anilAmaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) The same as {#anilavyADi#} q. v. E. {#anila#} and {#Amaya#}.
{#anilASin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SI-SinI-Si#}) Feeding on the wind, fasting. E. {#anila#} and {#ASin#}.
{#anivartitva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> The not returning. <sup>2</sup> The not turning back, not running away, not flying. E. {#anivartin#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.
{#anivartin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rtI-rtinI-rti#}) <sup>1</sup> Not coming back, not returning. <sup>2</sup> Not turning back, not flying.
{#anivArita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unchecked, unim- peded, unopposed, unforbidden. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nivArita#}.
{#anivArya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ryaH-ryA-ryam#}) Not to be prevented or forbidden, necessary, unavoidable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nivArya#}.
{#aniviSamAna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Not reposing, not resting, restless. (ved.) E. {#a#} neg. and {#niviSamAna#}.
{#anivfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unchecked, unimpeded, unopposed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nivfta#}.
{#anivedita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not told, not mentioned, not pointed out. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nivedita#}.
{#aniveditavijYAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Known without having been told or pointed out. E. {#anivedita#} and {#vijYAta#}.
{#aniveSana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Without a resting place, without an abode, restless. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niveSana#}.

{#aniSa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SA-Sam#}) Continual, incessant. {#aniSam#} used adv. continually, without interruption. E. {#a#} priv. and {#niSA#}, according to some, implying here merely the period of time, according to others, the want of occu- pation or rest i. e. literally ‘without a night’ or ‘without rest’.

{#aniSita#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) (ved.) Restless, incessant(?). E. {#aniSi#} (a denom. from {#aniSa#}), kṛt aff. {#kta(?)#}. (Mean- ing and etymology of this word are doubtful. According to the native commentaries it would be a Tatpur. compounded of {#a#} neg. and {#niSita#}, sharpened, sharp, and would mean either: <sup>1</sup> not sharp, not injurious, or: <sup>2</sup> not difficult, easy, or <sup>3</sup> not slender, not little; but these explanations, when applied to the passages to which they refer, seem artificial.

{#aniSitasarga#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rgaH-rgA-rgam#}) (ved.) Of con- tinual effusion, continually flowing (an epithet of the wa- ters)(?). (This meaning is doubtful; according to the comm. it would be: of strong or abundant effusion. See the pre- ceding.) E. {#aniSita#} and {#sarga#}.

{#anizaNga#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-NgaH-NgA-Ngam#}) Without a quiver. (According to the vaidik comm.: not connected with or impeded by, scil. the Rākṣasas; this interpretation seems artificial.) E. {#a#} priv. and {#nizaNga#}.
{#anizidDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dDaH-dDA-dDam#}) Not prohibited, not forbidden. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizidDa#}.
{#anizu#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-zuH-zuH-zu#}) Having no arrow or hav- ing bad arrows. E. {#a#} priv. and {#izu#}.
{#anizedDra#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-dDraH-dDrA-dDram#}) (ved.) Without im- pediment, unchecked, unimpeded. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nizedDra#}.
{#anizkfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not completed, not ac- complished, not perfect. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizkfta#}.

{#anizwa#}¦ Tatpur. I. 1. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unwished, un- desirable, bad, wrong. <sup>2</sup> Bad, evil. <sup>3</sup> Unlucky. <div n="P">2. n. ({#-zwam#}) <sup>1</sup> Bad luck, evil occurrence, misfortune. <sup>2</sup> Evil deed, crime. <div n="P">3. f. ({#-zwA#}) The name of a plant (Sida alba). See {#nAga-#} {#valA#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#izwa#} ({#iz#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}). <div n="P">II. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not sacrificed. <sup>2</sup> Not honoured with a sacrifice (as a god). E. {#a#} neg. and {#izwa#} ({#yaj#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}).

{#anizwaduzwaDI#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-DIH-DIH-Di#}) Of a bad and wicked disposition or mind. (Another and apparently more correct reading of this word is {#arizwaduzwaDI#} q. v.) E. {#anizwa-#} {#duzwa#} (Dwandwa) and {#DI#}.

{#anizwaprasaNga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-NgaH#}) Connexion or association with what is undesirable, incongruous or wrong connexion, as that of a Yogin with worldly objects; or (in Nyāya) that of an inference with wrong premises, the former tending to prove the absurdity of the argument advanced; or (in gram- matical literature) connecting one rule with an other rule which has no relation to it. E. {#anizwa#} and {#prasaNga#}.
{#anizwaPala#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-lam#}) Evil consequence, evil result. E. {#anizwa#} and {#Pala#}.

{#anizwaSaNkA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-NkA#}) Apprehension of an unpleasant or unlucky occurrence, apprehension of danger; (in rhetoric one of the {#vyaBicAriBAva#} (q. v.) of the rasa {#vatsala#} (q. v.). E. {#anizwa#} and {#SaNkA#}.
{#anizwahetu#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tuH#}) An evil omen. E. {#anizwa#} and {#hetu#}.

{#anizwApAdana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) 1. Obtaining or getting what is not desirable. See {#prAptisama#}. E. {#anizwa#} and {#ApAdana#}. <div n="P">2. Not obtaining what is desirable. See {#aprAptisama#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#izwa-ApAdana#}.
{#anizwApti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ptiH#}) The same as the preceding. E. 1. {#anizwa#} and {#Apti#}, 2. {#a#} neg. and {#izwa-Apti#}.
{#anizwASaMsin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-sI-sinI-si#}) Boding ill or evil. E. {#anizwa#} and {#ASaMsin#}.
{#anizwin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zwI#}) One who has not performed a sacrifice. E. {#a#} neg. and {#izwin#}.
{#anizwfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) (ved.) Not hurt, not injured. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizwfta#}.
{#anizwotprekzaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) Apprehension of an unpleasant or unlucky occurrence, apprehension of danger, fear. E. {#anizwa#} and {#utprekzaRa#}.
{#anizWura#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Not contumelious. <sup>2</sup> Not harsh. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizWura#}.
{#anizRAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Unskilful, ignorant. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizRAta#}.
{#anizpatti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ttiH#}) Non-completion, non-termination. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizpatti#}.
{#anizpatram#}¦ Tatpur. ind. (Wounding) so as not to make the arrow come out on the other side of the body, i. e. not too violently. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizpatra#}.
{#anizpanna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-nnaH-nnA-nnam#}) Not accomplished, incomplete, imperfect. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nizpanna#}.
{#anisarga#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rgaH-rgA-rgam#}) Unnatural, unnaturally elated or depressed. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nisarga#}.
{#anistabDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-bDaH-bDA-bDam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not paralyzed, not overpowered. <sup>2</sup> Not stopped, not fixed. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nistabDa#}.

{#anistIrRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not got over. <sup>2</sup> (In law.) Not refuted, not answered (as a plaint, a charge). See the following. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nistIrRa#}.
{#anistIrRABiyoga#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-gaH#}) (In law.) A defendant who has not or not yet refuted the charge brought against him. E. {#anistIrRa#} and {#aBiyoga#}.

{#anIka#}¦ m. n. ({#-kaH-kam#}) <sup>1</sup> The face (ved.). <sup>2</sup> The fore part, front, the principal or conspicuous part (ved.). <sup>3</sup> The point (e. g. of an arrow) (ved.). <sup>4</sup> Multitude, assemblage, quan- tity (ved.). <sup>5</sup> An army, a host, forces (according to some, also: part of an army). <sup>6</sup> War, combat. E. {#an#}, to breathe (in 1. 2. 3.) and to go (in 4. 5. 6.), uṇ. aff. {#Ikan#}, the radical being {#kit#}.

{#anIkavat#}¦ m. ({#-vAn#}) (ved.) Having or occupying the pro- minent or principal place, principal, superior, first, an epithet of Agni, used chiefly when the god receives the first offerings in certain sacrifices, his name then also oc- curring as the first in the list of the gods invoked. E. {#anIka#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#anIkavidAraRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RaH#}) A proper name: a brother of Jayadratha. E. {#anIka#} and {#vidAraRa#} ‘destroyer of hosts’.

{#anIkasTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-sTaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A warrior, a combattant. <sup>2</sup> A royal body guard. <sup>3</sup> A trainer of an elephant, an elephant driver. <sup>4</sup> A large military drum. <sup>5</sup> A mark, a sign, a signal. <sup>6</sup> (According to one authority: {#aSvala#} q. v.) {#anutpattika#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kI-kam#}) (In Bauddha li- terature.) Having no origin or birth, not or not yet being produced. (The fem. {#-kI#} belongs to Bauddha writings; in the classic language, it would be {#-kA#}.) See the following. E. {#anutpatti#} II., samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.

{#anutpattikaDarmakzAnti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ntiH#}) (In Bauddha literature.) Enduring conditions which have not yet taken place i. e. reconciling one's mind to the conditions of a future life; one of the hundred-eight {#DarmAlokamuKa#} (q. v.) or means to comprehend the doctrine of Śākyamuni; ‘it leads to the reception of revelations’ i. e. it enables an enquirer to get possessed of the mysteries of the Bauddha doctrine. E. {#anutpattika-Darma#} and {#kzAnti#}.

{#anutpattisama#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. ({#-maH-mA#}) (In the Nyāya philosophy.) The sophism of the impossibility of origin or birth; viz. arguing that a thing cannot take origin, because a thing exists in consequence of an immaterial cause; as the latter, however, does not exist before the material cause and the instance proving the existence of such material cause, and as the material cause again depends upon what exists, and the instance upon the material cause, the thing itself can never come into existence: or origin in general is impossible. E. {#anutpatti#} and {#sama#}. (With respect to the gender of this word and the ellipsis required to explain it, see the E. of {#anityasama#}.)
{#anutpanna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-nnaH-nnA-nnam#}) Not born, not pro- duced &c. See {#utpanna#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#utpanna#}.
{#anutpAda#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-daH#}) The not taking origin or birth, the not arising. E. {#a#} neg. and {#utpAda#}.

{#anutpAdakzAnti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ntiH#}) (In Bauddha literature.) En- during non-birth i. e. reconciling one's mind to not being born again; one of the hundred-eight {#DarmAlokamuKa#} (q. v.) or means to comprehend the doctrine of Śākyamuni; it is conducive to a clear apprehension of all that may impede (sc. the attainment of this desirable end). E. {#anutpAda#} and {#kzAnti#}.
{#anutpAdana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Not producing, not bringing forth. E. {#a#} neg. and {#utpAdana#}.
{#anutpAdya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dyaH-dyA-dyam#}) Not producible, eternal (e. g. {#prakfti#} or {#puruza#} in the Sāṅkhya philosophy). E. {#a#} neg. and {#utpAdya#}.

{#anutsuka#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Not strongly attached to, not longing for &c. See {#utsuka#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#utsuka#}.

{#anudaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Without water, water- less. E. {#a#} priv. and {#udaka#}.

{#anudara#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) Thin, lank. E. {#a#} priv. and {#udara#}.

{#anudarSin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rSI-rSinI-rSi#}) Looking after, con- sidering, foreseeing. E. {#dfS#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini#}.

{#anudAtta#}¦ Tatpur. (In Grammar.) 1. m. f. n. ({#-ttaH-ttA-ttam#}) Not elevated, not being pronounced with the accent called {#udAtta#} (q. v.) or {#svarita#} (q. v.) (as the syllable of a word). <div n="P">2. m. ({#-ttaH#}) The not elevated accent, the accent (see {#svara#} and {#vAhyaprayatna#}) which is neither {#udAtta#} (q. v.) nor {#svarita#} (q. v.) and which by the depression of the voice, it requires, prepares, as it were, for the greater effort in the pronunciation of the syllables accented with the {#udAtta#} or {#svarita#}. This depression being the greatest when the syl- lable having the {#anudAtta#} accent, is immediately followed by a syllable accented with the {#udAtta#} or {#svarita#}, the {#anu-#} {#dAtta#} is called in this case {#anudAttatara#} ‘a very anudātta’. The mode of marking the {#anudAtta#}, is restricted, as is also the case with the other two accents, to the vaidik Sanhitās (Sanhitā-Pāṭhas) and Brāhmaṇas, and varies according to the different Vedas. In the Sanhitā, Pada and the Brāhmaṇas of the Ṛgveda, in the Sanhitā and Pada of the Yajur- and Sanhitā of the Atharvaveda the Anudātta is marked with a horizontal line under the syllable so accented ({%thus becoming%} {%comparable also in graphic value to the sign of the Virāma, the%} {%horizontal line representing as it were the repose in accentua-%} {%tion%}); in the Brāhmaṇas of the White Yajurveda, it is not marked at all; and in the Sanhitā of the Sāmaveda the anu- dātta syllable when anudāttatara before an udātta, or before a svarita syllable bearing the figures {#2#} or {#3#}, is marked with the figure {#3#} over it, except when it is preceded in the be- ginning of a verse by other anudātta syllables, in which case only the first anudātta syllable bears the figure {#3#}, while the following anudātta syllables are left unmarked. If the anudāttatara is followed by a svarita syllable bearing the sign {#2ra#}, the syllable so accented is marked with {#3ka#}. In the Pada-text of the Sāmaveda the sign {#3#} denotes the anudāttatara before an udātta, if the latter occupies the second syllable from the beginning, or the syllable before an anudāttatara, if the latter is followed by a svarita, or lastly the anudātta accentuation of a syllable so marked and of all the syllables following it until an udātta or svarita syllable comes; the sign {#3ka#} or {#ka#} denotes the anudāttatara immediately followed by a svarita. Compare also the terms {#nIca, nihata, nyasta, nyastatara, niyata, niGAta, nyAsa, niyama#} and the radd. {#han#} with {#ni#} and {#yam#} with {#ni#}.--In the native [Page090-b+ 56] lists of radicals, the Dhātupāthas, certain radicals have the anudātta accent as an {#it#} (q. v.) or {#anubanDa#} (q. v.) connected with them i. e. as a technical sign for certain rules they are subject to with respect to derivation &c. See also {#anu-#} {#dAttet#} and {#anudAttopadeSa#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#anudAtta#}.

{#anudAttatara#}¦ m. ({#-raH#}) The {#anudAtta#} accent (or {#svara#}) or a syl- lable so accented when immediately preceding a syllable having the {#udAtta#} or {#svarita#} accent. See under {#anudAtta#}. E. {#anudAtta#}, taddh. aff. {#tarap#}.
{#anudAttatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The having or being the accent {#anudAtta#}. E. {#anudAtta#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anudAttAdi#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-di#}) (In Grammar.) A nominal base which is {#anudAtta#} (q. v.) in the first syllable. E. {#anudAtta#} and {#Adi#}; scil. {#prAtipadika#}.

{#anudAttet#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-t#}) (In Grammar.) E. {#anudAtta#} and {#it#} (the technical denomination of {#anubanDa#}); scil. {#DAtu#}.
{#anudAttodaya#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-yam#}) (In Grammar.) A syllable fol- lowed by an {#anudAtta#} (q. v.) syllable. E. {#anudAtta#} and {#udaya#}; scil. {#akzara#}.
{#anudAttopadeSa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-SaH#}). The same as {#anudAttet#}. See s. v. {#upadeSa#}. E. {#anudAtta#} and {#upadeSa#}; scil. {#DAtu#}.

Being the ob- ject of an {#anudeSa#} (q. v.) in distinction from {#uddeSin#} (q. v.) the object of an {#uddeSa#} (q. v.); {#‘samAnAM samasaMKyAnAM samapari-#} {#paWitAnAmuddeSinAmanudeSinAM ca yaTAkramamuddeSiBiH sahAnude-#} {#SinaH saMbaDyante.’#}. {#anudvAha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) Celibacy. E. {#a#} neg. and {#udvAha#}.
{#anudvigna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-gnaH-gnA-gnam#}) Easy, free from ap- prehension or perplexity. E. {#an#} neg. and {#udvigna#}.

({#-yaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Salutation, courtesy, shewing respect or adoration to a guest or deity, submission, hu- mility. <sup>2</sup> Humble supplication, conciliatory entreaty, re- concilement. E. {#nI#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#ac#}. <div n="P">II. Avyayībh. ({#-yam#}) According to propriety, agreeably to what is required, to circumstance; e. g. {#abravIdanunayaM vacaH#}. {#anunAsika#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) (In Grammar.) Uttered through the nose, nasal (see also {#rakta#}), viz. <sup>1</sup> A nasal sound in general, it being pronounced through the nose and with the appropriate organ of speech, as {#N#} through the nose and the throat, {#Y#} through the nose and with the palate &c. <sup>2</sup> (Conditionally) a vowel or {#y, v, l#}; in this case the nasal nature of the sound is indicated by the sign {#M~#}. (N. B. {#yM~#} or {#vM~#} represent the value of {#y#} or {#v#} preceded by {#m; lM~#} that of {#l#} preceded by {#m#} or {#n#}. In the pause a final vowel may be anunāsika. A {%short%} anunāsika vowel, when not occurr- ing in a pause, represents apparently always the value of the same vowel and {#m#} or {#n#}; it must be, in general, the last vowel sound of the former part of a compound or of the word itself, followed by a final sibilant, e. g. {#saM~skartA#} instead of {#sams-kartA, puM~ScalI = pums-calI, tasmiM~stvA =#} {#tasmins-tvA#}. Only a few exceptions of this rule are mentioned by the vaidik grammarians, e. g. {#aminantaM~ evEH#}, when {#a#} of {#nta#} is anunāsika, although it does neither stand in a pause nor represent more than its own sound.--A {%long%} anunāsika vowel, when not occurring in a pause, may be generally considered as representing the value of its short vowel and an original {#nts#} or of its short vowel and {#nt#}, provided {#s#} or its substitute has been preserved; e. g. {#mahAM~ indraH = mahants#} {#indraH, daDanvAM~ yaH = daDanvants yaH, sargAM~ iva = sargants iva#} or {#mahAM~Scarati = mahants carati, dasyUM~rekaH = dasyunts ekaH#}. The material difference that prevails between the anunāsika ({#M~#}) and the anusvāra ({#M#}) sound, does not appear to have been kept alive beyond the period of the vaidik literature, when an interchange between both was not deemed legiti- mate; according to the grammarians of the classical period, in the latter the anunāsika may be replaced by the anu- svāra. The sign of the anunāsika ({#M~#}), however, is but seldom met with in the ordinary Mss. referring to the post- vaidik literature; and from the reasons stated, its use in vaidik Mss. is objectionable, when it occurs in words like {#yaSAM~si, DanUM~zi, viSvezAM~ hitaH#} or in {#maM~hizWa, vAjaM~ sanizat, indraM~#} {#stavAma#} and similar instances in which the long nasal vowel does not represent more than the value of a short vowel and a nasal, or in which the short nasal vowel is not fol- lowed by a final sibilant.) E. {#anu#} and {#nAsikA#}.
{#anunAsikatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The being nasal, nasality. E. {#anu-#} {#nAsika#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anupatana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Falling on or upon. <sup>2</sup> Following. <sup>3</sup> (In Arithmetic.) Proportion. E. {#pat#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#anupadasvat#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-svAn-svatI-svat#}) (ved.) Probably: not diminishing, not decaying. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upadasvat#}.
{#anupadin#}¦ m. ({#-dI#}) A searcher, an inquirer, one who follows or seeks for, with a noun in the genit., e. g. {#mfgasyAnupadI#}, {#anupadyuzwrARAm#}. E. {#anupada#} (III.), taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#anupadezwf#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zwA#}) One who does not advise or in- struct; e. g. {#hitAnupadezwA kutsitaH saKA#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upadezwf#}.

{#anupanAha#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-haH#}) (In Buddhistic doctrine.) One of the 108 {#DarmAlokamuKa#} q. v.; (perhaps) want of attachment(?). E. {#a#} neg. and {#upanAha#}.
{#anupanyasta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-staH-stA-stam#}) Not laid down, not established, not clearly shown. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upanyasta#}.

({#-ttiH#}) <sup>1</sup> The not taking place, failing to be, failure. <sup>2</sup> The not being applied or applicable (as a rule in grammar &c.). <sup>3</sup> The not being conclusive (as an argument &c. brought to support a doctrine). <sup>4</sup> Absence of the means of subsistence(?). E. {#a#} neg. and {#upapatti#}.

{#anupapanna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-nnaH-nnA-nnam#}) <sup>1</sup> Uneffected, unac- complished. <sup>2</sup> Not applicable, not relevant. <sup>3</sup> Inconclusive (as an argument). <sup>4</sup> Undemonstrated, unsubstantiated. <sup>5</sup> Not having means of subsistence(?). E. {#a#} neg. and {#upapanna#}.

E. {#a#} priv. and {#upapAdaka#} lit. ‘without a parent’.
{#anupaplava#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Free from misfortune, not distressed. E. {#a#} priv. and {#upaplava#}.
{#anupapluta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}). The same as the pre- ceding. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upapluta#}.
{#anupabADa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-DaH-DA-Dam#}) (ved.) Not obstructed, not injured. E. {#a#} priv. and {#upabADA#}.

{#anupamardana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Not refuting a charge. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upamardana#}.
{#anupamita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Incomparable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upamita#}.

{#anupayukta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) Useless, unsuitable, unserviceable. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upayukta#} (as according to a law book, ‘vaidik writings to fools’).

{#anuparata#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not stopped, not ceased. E. {#a#} neg. and {#uparata#}.
{#anupariDi#}¦ Avyayībh. Along or near the {#pariDi#} q. v. E. {#anu#} and {#pariDi#}.
{#anupalakzita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unseen, unper- ceived. <sup>2</sup> Unmarked, undiscriminated. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upalakzita#}.
{#anupalabDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-bDaH-bDA-bDam#}) <sup>1</sup> Unobtained. <sup>2</sup> Unperceived, imperceptible. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upalabDa#}.
{#anupalabDatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}). The same as {#anupalamBa#} q. v. E. {#anu-#} {#palabDa#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anupalabDisama#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. ({#-maH-mA#}) (In the Nyāya philo- sophy.) A sophism on non-perception; viz. arguing: ‘be- cause the non-perception of an object cannot be perceived, therefore the non-perception of the object does not exist [Page093-b+ 56] and consequently the non-existence of the object cannot exist i. e. the object itself must exist’. This sophism is at- tributed by the Nyāya e. g. to those who maintain the eter- nity of sound on the ground that ‘the non-perception of sound antecedently to pronunciation’--the reason alleged by the Nyāya for its non-eternity--may be refuted in the manner explained. E. {#anupalabDi#} and {#sama#} (m. scil. {#pratizeDa#} or {#vikalpa#} or {#prayoga#}; f. scil. {#jAti#}; comp. for the meaning of these words the E. of {#anityasama#}).
{#anupalaByamAna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Not being per- ceived, not being seen. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upalaByamAna#}.

{#anupalamBa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-mBaH#}) The not being perceived, ascer- tained, or the not being perceptible, ascertainable; e. g. {#tadanupalabDeranupalamBAdAvaraRopalabDiH#} ‘the perception of a covering is from the non-perception there of not being percep- tible’. See {#anupalabDi#} and {#anupalabDisama#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upalamBa#}.
{#anupavItin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tI#}) One who does not wear the cord of his caste. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upavItin#}.
{#anupaSaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) (In Medicine.) Any aggravating thing or circumstance that increases the disease. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upaSaya#}.
{#anupaSAnta#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. ({#-ntaH-ntA-ntam#}) Not calm, not tranquil. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-ntaH#}) The name of a Bauddha mendicant. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upaSAnta#}.
{#anupaSya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SyaH-SyA-Syam#}) Looking after, con- sidering attentively. See {#pratyayAnupaSya#}. E. {#dfS#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#Sa#}.

E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasaMhArin#}.

E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasarga#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. ({#-rgaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Without an {#upasarga#} q. v. (as a radical). <sup>2</sup> Without obstruction, free from impediment; an epithet of {#ISvara#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#upasarga#}.

{#anupaskfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not vitiated, not blamed, blameless (e. g. the law of Manu). <sup>2</sup> Not orna- mented, unfinished; e. g. {#rAjatamanupaskftam#} a silver vessel not enchased. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upaskfta#}.
{#anupasTAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Absence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasTAna#}.
{#anupasTApana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Not bringing near, not having ready or at hand. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasTApana#}.

{#anupasTAyin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yI-yinI-yi#}) Absent, distant. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasTAyin#}.

{#anupasTita#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not approached &c. <sup>2</sup> Not ready, not fresh in memory. <sup>3</sup> Sunk into oblivion (as a science &c.). <div n="P">II. n. ({#-tam#}) (In Grammar.) A word which is not {#upasTita#} (q. v.) i. e. which is not the word {#iti#} as it occurs in the writings referring to the recitation of the vaidik hymns. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasTita#}.
{#anupasTiti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) Absence. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upasTiti#}.
{#anupahata#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not injured, not impaired, not obstructed. <sup>2</sup> Not polluted, not vitiated, not made impure. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upahata#}.

{#anupahatakruzwa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-zwaH-zwA-zwam#}) Who has (in his aspect) nothing that indicates injury or anger (one of the eighty secondary signs (or {#anuvyaYjana#}) which characterize a great man, acc to the Buddhists. E. {#a#} priv. and {#upahata-kruzwa#}.

{#anupahUta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not summoned, not invoked. <sup>2</sup> Not summoned in a loud voice, invoked in a low voice. E. {#a#} 1. neg. 2. deter. and {#upahUta#}.

{#anupAkfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Not prepared or made fit for sacrificial purposes (as a victim before the muttering of prayers over it, or as the {#prAtaranuvAka#} before the com- pletion of the ceremonies required for it &c.). E. {#a#} neg. and {#upAkfta#}.

{#anupAkftamAMsa#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-sam#}) Flesh of an animal which has not been made fit for sacrificial purposes by the recital of vaidik hymns, flesh of an animal which has not been killed at a sacrifice. (A Brahmaṇa is forbidden to eat such flesh.) E. {#anupAkfta#} and {#mAMsa#}.
{#anupAKya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-KyaH-KyA-Kyam#}) Not clearly per- ceptible. E. {#a#} neg. and {#upAKya#}.

{#anupAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) <sup>1</sup> Falling subsequently upon, alight- ing or descending upon in succession. <sup>2</sup> Following. <sup>3</sup> (In arithmetic.) Proportion, the rule of three. E. {#anu#} and {#pAta#} or {#pat#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#Ra#}.

{#anupAtaka#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-kam#}) A heinous offence, one similar to the four great crimes ({#mahApAtaka#}) which are: <sup>a.</sup> Causing the death of a Brāhmaṇa (directly or indirectly). <sup>b.</sup> Drink- ing spirits. <sup>c.</sup> Stealing (acc. to the comm. ‘gold from a Brāhmaṇa’). <sup>d.</sup> Committing incest with the wife of a father, natural or spiritual. The {#anupAtaka#} mentioned by Manu are the following: 1. False boasting of superiority (as pretending to be a Brāhmaṇa or conversant with the four Vedas, if one is not); 2. Malignant report, before a king, of crimes (comm.: punishable by death)--omitted by Yājnavalkya--; 3. Falsely accusing a spiritual preceptor; 4. Forgetting the Veda; 5. Showing contempt of the Veda (comm.: by resorting to heretical writings); 6. Giving false evidence (omitted by Yājnav.); 7. Killing a friend (comm.: not a Brāhmaṇa, this case being the first {#mahApAtaka#}); 8. (Knowingly) eating things prohibited (i. e. food fit only for a Śūdra, as garlick &c.) or unfit to be tasted (as excrements &c.); [9. (According to Yājnavalkya) Kissing a woman [Page094-b+ 56] while in menstruation; 10. (Acc. to Yājn.) Deceitfulness (i. e. saying one thing and doing another)]; 11. Appro- priating a deposit (comm.: not the gold of a Brāhmaṇa (this case being the third {#mahApAtaka#}) or acc. to another author. a deposit not of gold, if it belongs to a Brāhmaṇa); 12--17. Stealing a man, a horse, silver, a piece of land, a diamond or a gem [acc. to Yājnavalkya, 12--17. a horse, a gem, a man, a woman, a piece of land, and a cow]; 18--22. Sexual intercourse with one's own sister, with little girls before they have attained to puberty, with women of the lowest tribe (comm.: a Chāṇdālī), with the wives of a friend or of a son [to which Yājnavalkya adds: 23--30. with a woman of the same gotra or family, the sister of a father or mother, the wife of a maternal uncle, the wife of one's father, the daughter or wife of a spiritual teacher or one's own daughter; Nārada adds moreover: 31--40. with a mother in law, the wife of a paternal uncle or of a pupil, the friend of a sister, one who comes for protection, the wife of one who carries on the government of the country--comm.: if he is not a Kshatriya--, a nurse, a female mendicant, a female devotee and a woman of the Brāhmaṇa class.]-- Similar to the first Mahāpātaka are the Anupātakas, acc. to Manu, 1--3, acc. to Yājnavalkya, 3--5 and 7. Similar to the second Mahāpātaka are the Anup., acc. to Manu, 4--8; acc. to Yājnav., 1. 8. 9. 10. Similar to the third Mahāp. are the Anup., acc. to Manu and Yājnav., 11--17. Similar to the fourth Mahāp. are, according to Manu, the Anupāt. 18--22, acc. to Yājnav. (and Nārada, Yama &c.), 18-40. E. {#anu#} and {#pAtaka#}.

{#anupAnatka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tkaH-tkA-tkam#}) Without shoes. E. {#a#} priv. and {#upAnah#}, samāsānta aff. {#kap#}.

{#anupAnIya#}¦ I. Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) To be drunk after. E. {#pA#} with {#anu#}, kṛtya aff. {#anIyar#}. <div n="P">2. n. ({#-yam#}) Drink which is near (see {#anupAna#}). E. {#anu#} and {#pAnIya#}. <div n="P">II. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) What is used as a vehicle (in medicine). E. {#anupAna#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#anupAlana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Preserving, guarding; e. g. {#vi-#} {#dyAnupAlana#} keeping to science, studying. E. {#pA#}, in the caus., with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

{#anupAlayat#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-n-ntI-t#}) <sup>1</sup> Preserving, taking care of; e. g. {#aBivarzati yo'nupAlayanviDivIjAni viveka-#} {#vAriRA#} &c. <sup>2</sup> (Accord. to a comm.) Neglecting, disregard- ing; e. g. {#anupAlayatAmudezyatIM praBuSaktiM dvizatAmanIhayA. a-#} {#payAntyacirAnmahIBujAM jananirvAdaBayAdiva SriyaH#} (the comm. referring {#anupAlayatAm = upekzamARAnAm#} not to {#dvizatAm#} but to {#mahIBujAm#}). {#anupAlin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-lI-linI-li#}) Preserving, cherishing, guarding; e. g. {#vidyAnupAlin#}. E. {#pA#}, in the caus., with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#Rini#}.

{#anupuruza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) <sup>1</sup> The man spoken of before, the said man. <sup>2</sup> A man who follows, a follower. E. {#anu#} and {#puruza#}.

{#anupravacanIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Referring to, having for its object the {#anupravacana#}. E. {#anupravacana#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#anupraveSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Returning. <sup>2</sup> Entering. See {#anu-#} {#praveSam#}. E. {#anu#} and {#praveSa#}.

{#anupraveSanIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Referring to the return or entering, having the return or entering for its object. E. {#anupraveSana#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.

{#anuprasakti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ktiH#}) Connexion with, esp. logical connexion. E. {#anu#} and {#prasakti#}.

{#anuprasTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-sTaH-sTA-sTam#}) Latitudinal. E. {#anu#} and {#prasTa#}.

{#anuprApta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ptaH-ptA-ptam#}) <sup>1</sup> Obtained, found. <sup>2</sup> Reached, arrived. E. {#Ap#} with {#pra#} and {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#kta#}.

{#anubanDa#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-nDaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Binding, confining. <sup>2</sup> Connexion, association, attachment; close relation; e. g. {#pUrvAByastasmftya-#} {#nubanDaH#} ‘connexion with the memory of things previously acquired’. {#nIvArAdizu codanAnubanDaH#} ‘the injunction relates to or concerns wild rice &c. (not {#vrIhi#}). <sup>3</sup> An uninterrupted series, e. g. {#vErAnubanDaH#} a series of hostilities or heroic deeds. <sup>4</sup> Consequence, result, e. g. {#pUrvakftaPalAnubanDAttadutpattiH#} ‘it (the body) is produced in consequence of the fruits of its former deeds’. <sup>5</sup> Cause esp. of a crime &c., e. g. {#anubanDaM#} {#parijYAya…daRqaM pAtayet#} let (the king) having ascertained the cause (comm.: of the offence) inflict punishment; or of an untoward event &c., e. g. {#virAtre cAgataM kasmAtko'nu-#} {#banDaSca te'Bavat#} ‘why hast thou come so late in the night and what was the cause (comm.: of the delay)?’ <sup>6</sup> Com- mencement, beginning. <sup>7</sup> A child (this meaning seems doubt- ful, at least as regards its etymol. interpretation; acc. to some it would be qualified as {#muKyAnuyAyin#} ‘following the chief i. e. the father &c. at the marriage ceremony &c.; the instance given however would not seem to countenance the meaning viz. {#bAlakAnubanDena yAtrABaNgo mA BUt#} ‘let the festival not be disturbed by the incumbrance of children’; accord. to others the meaning ‘child’ would imply the tie of af- fection). <sup>8</sup> (In the system of the native grammarians.) An indicatory letter which is annexed to radicals ({#DAtu#}), no- minal bases ({#prAtipadika#}), affixes ({#pratyaya#}), particles ({#nipAta#}), inserted letters ({#Agama#}) and substitutes ({#AdeSa#}), to mark some peculiarity in the accent, inflection or derivation; for instance an {%indicatory%} {#i#} denotes that verbs require the in- sertion of a nasal before their final consonant; the anu- bandha may be a vowel (in this case it is {#anunAsika#} q. v. in the system of Pāṇini) or a consonant. Being a mere technical element it cannot occur in real language. Instances of anubandhas may be gathered from the etymologies in this [Page096-b+ 56] Dictionary. See also {#it#}. <sup>9</sup> Any thing small or little, a part, a small part. <sup>10</sup> (In Medicine.) A secondary or sym- ptomatic affection, one supervening on the principal disease. <sup>11</sup> (In Arithmetic.) Junction or union; see {#BAgAnubanDa#}. <sup>12</sup> (In the Vedānta philosophy.) An indispensable element of the study of the Vedānta; it consists of <sup>a.</sup> the {#aDikArin#} or the competent person, one who is well versed in the vaidik writings, observes the ceremonies &c., is purified in his heart &c.; <sup>b.</sup> the {#vizaya#} or the object-matter viz. the identity of the individual soul and Brahman (neuter); <sup>c.</sup> the {#saMbanDa#} or the relation viz. between that identity to be proved and the authoritative evidence contained in the Upanishads, and <sup>d.</sup> the {#prayojana#} or the purpose viz. the cessation of ignorance and attainment of eternal bliss. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-nDI#}) <sup>1</sup> Hickup. <sup>2</sup> Thirst. E. {#banD#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#GaY#}, in the fem. with {#NIz#}.
{#anubanDana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Connexion, association. E. {#banD#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.

E. {#banD#} with {#anu#}, kṛtya aff. {#yat#}; with the ellipsis of {#paSu#} for the masc. and of {#go#} for the feminine. <div n="P">II. m. f. n. {#anubanDyapaSu#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-SuH#}) The sacrificial animal called {#anubanDya#}. See the preceding. E. {#anubanDya#} and {#paSu#}.

{#anuBaNgam#}¦ Avyayībh. According to defeat, fear &c.(?). Com- pare also {#AnuBaNgya#}. E. {#anu#} and {#BaNga#}.

{#anuBAva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Dignity, authority, power (such as results from wealth, a magisterial position &c.). <sup>2</sup> Cer- tainty, resolution (only in the positive sense of a good re- solution, e. g. {#mahAnuBAva#} q. v.). <sup>3</sup> (In rhetorical terminology.) ‘A symptom which indicated the feeling ({#BAva#}) produced by its appropriate causes’. These causes being naturally various from the character ({#rasa#}) of a poetical composition, the rhetorical works enumerate the anubhāvas which are the concomitants of the different sorts of rasas; thus the symptoms of the Erotic ({#SfNgAra#}) are according to them, motion of the eye-brows, side-glances &c.; of the Comic ({#hAsya#}), blinking with the eye, smiles &c.; of the Pathetic ({#karuRa#}), cursing one's fate, falling to the ground, crying &c.; of the Terrible ({#rOdra#}), abuse, fierce looks &c.; of the Heroic ({#vIra#}), looking for a companion &c.; of the Fearful ({#BayAnaka#}), change of colour, stammering &c.; of the Dis- gustful ({#bIBatsa#}), spitting, contracting the mouth, shutting the eyes &c.; of the Wonderful ({#adButa#}), wide opening of the eyes &c.; of the Quietistic ({#SAnta#}), horripilation (sic) &c.; of the Affectionate ({#vatsala#}), horripilation, joy, tears &c.--Compare {#BAva#} and {#viBAva#}. E. {#anu#} and {#BAva#}, lit. ‘following or connected with condition, feeling &c.’.

{#anuBAvin#}¦ I. Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-vI-vinI-vi#}) Perceiving, knowing (e. g. a witness). <div n="P">2. m. ({#-vI#}) (In law.) According to some, the same as {#sapiRqa#} q. v., a near kinsman (i. e. ‘one who feels grief at a death in the family’), according to others, the same as ‘a young son’ (i. e. ‘one who is or comes after’). {#anumAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) <sup>1</sup> Inferring, as the cause of {#anumiti#} or of a conclusion drawn from given premises. According to the Sāṅkhya and Yoga-philosophies it is one of the {%three%} means (see {#pramARa#}) by which true knowledge may be ob- tained (see also {#pratyakza#} or {#dfzwa#} and {#Agama#} or {#Aptavacana#}); according to the Nyāya and Vaiśeṣika phil., one of the {%four%} means for this end (see also {#pratyakza, upamAna#} and {#Sabda#}). Inference may be, according to the definitions of Sāṅkhya and Nyāya philosophers, either one by induction ({#pUrvavat#}) e. g. that it will rain because clouds have gathered, or one by analogy ({#sAmAnyato dfzwam#}), e. g. that moon and stars are locomotive because they change their place and that a person therefore who changes his place is locomotive; or one by ne- cessity ({#Sezavat#}), e. g. that the ocean will be salt, because a drop taken from it, is salt. According to the Vaiśeṣika philosophers, inference may be either purely consecutive or positive ({#kevalAnvayin#}), i. e. when the major term is not excluded by any other notion (comp. {#anupasaMhArin#}), e. g. all that can be known can be named, because only positive (not negative instances) can be alleged to prove the asser- tion; or purely exclusive or negative ({#kevalavyatirekin#}), i. e. when only negative proof can be adduced, e. g. in asserting that earth is distinguished from all the other elements, be- cause it is possessed of the quality of smell, for the ar- gument would be that all that is not distinguished from all the other elements, is not possessed of the quality of [Page098-b+ 56] smell; or positive and negative ({#anvayavyatirekin#}), i. e. when there exist positive and negative instances of the major term, e. g. where there is fire there is smoke, because the positive argument would be ‘on the hearth’ and the negative ‘in the lake’. (The Mīmānsā and Vedānta philosophies do not discuss these topics, as inference is not considered by them to be a means of arriving at true knowledge.) <sup>2</sup> (In rhetoric.) A logical anakolouthon by the way of inference, an {#alaMkAra#} or mode of writing elegantly, e. g. ‘wherever falls the look of woman, there fall sharpened arrows; I think therefore that the God of Love runs before them while shooting off his arrows’. E. {#mA#} with {#anu#}, kṛt aff. {#lyuw#}.
