{#annagati#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) (In Medicine.) The œsophagus, the gullet. E. {#anna#} and {#gati#}.

{#annaganDi#}¦ Bahnvr. m. ({#-nDiH#}) Diarrhœa, dysentery. E. {#anna#} and {#ganDa#}, samās. ādeśa {#i#}; the compound implying compari- son ‘smelling like boiled rice’; comp. similar formations as {#padmaganDi, karIzaganDi, utpalaganDi#}.
{#annagrAhaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) The seizer of food; an epithet of the vital air {#apAna#} q. v.; comp. {#annAyu#}. E. {#anna#} and {#grAhaka#}.

{#annaja#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-jaH-jA-jam#}) Produced by food or by the essence of the elementary creation; e. g. {#kaTamannajo#} {#'nnAtmA'nnapralayo'haM tasmAdannaM brahmeti#} ‘how (is it that men adore Brahman under the form of {#anna?#} it is when they think:) I am the product of {#anna#}, I have the nature of {#anna#}, I shall be merged again into {#anna#}, therefore {#anna#} is Brahman’. <div n="P">2. n. ({#-jam#}) (In Medicine.) Water in which rice has been boiled, rice gruel. E. {#anna#} and {#ja#}.
{#annajala#}¦ Dwandwa n. ({#-lam#}) Support, maintenance. E. {#anna#} and {#jala#}; ‘rice and water’.
{#annajAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) The same as {#annaja#} q. v. E. {#anna#} and {#jAta#}.
{#annajit#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-t-t-t#}) Conquering food; a vai- dik epithet of sacrificial horses. E. {#anna#} and {#jit#}.
{#annajIvana#}¦ Tatpur.(?) m. f. n. ({#-naH-nI(?)-nam#}) Living through or by {#anna#} q. v. 2. 2. E. {#anna#} and {#jIvana#}.
{#annatejas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-jAH-jAH-jaH#}) (ved.) Having the strength or power of {#anna#} q. v. 2. 2. E. {#anna#} and {#tejas#}.

{#annada#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-daH-dA-dam#}) Giving food &c., see {#anna#}; also m. as an epithet of Śiva and f. of Durgā. [Manu promises to a man who gives food, eternal happiness; Yā- jnavalkya, that he will be honoured in the Swarga; the Anu- [Page134-b+ 56] śāsanaparvan of the Mahābh. however (see the passages quoted s. v. {#anna#}), gives a detailed account of the various benefits which accrue to the giver of food, and which comprise nearly all conceivable happiness in this and the future world.] E. {#anna#} and {#da#}.
{#annadAtf#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-tA-trI-tf#}) The same as {#annada#}. E. {#anna#} and {#dAtf#}.
{#annadAna#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) The giving of food (enjoined as a meritorious act; compare {#annada#}). E. {#anna#} and {#dAna#}.
{#annadAyin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yI-yinI-yi#}) The same as {#annada#} q. v. E. {#anna#} and {#dAyin#}.
{#annadoza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) A sin committed with reference to the laws of diet, e. g. by eating garlick, onions, mush- rooms or other prohibited articles of food. E. {#anna#} and {#doza#}.
{#annadveza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) Dislike of food, want of appetite. E. {#anna#} and {#dveza#}.

{#annapati#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tiH#}) The protector of food (a vaidik epithet of Agni, and an epithet of Śiva in the Mahābh.); the Lord of food (an epithet of Savitṛ or the sun). Comp. {#annapU#}. E. {#anna#} and {#pati#}.
{#annaparivarta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rtaH#}) Change of diet (= {#AhAradravya-#} {#viparyayaH#}). E. {#anna#} and {#parivarta#}.

{#annapAnarakzA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kzA#}) Precaution in eating and drink- ing. (The {#annapAnarakzAkalpa#} is the introductory chapter of Suśruta to his toxicology; the bearing of the word is con- veyed by the verse: {#tasmAtparIkzaRaM kAryaM BftyAnAmAdito#} {#nfpEH . anne pAne#} &c.) Comp. {#annarakzA#}. E. {#anna-pAna#}, Dwandwa, and {#rakzA#}.
{#annapAnaviDi#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-DiH#}) The properties of eatable and drinkable substances (they are the subject of a chapter in Suśruta's Sūtrasthāna). E. {#anna-pAna#}, Dwandwa, and {#viDi#}.
{#annapU#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-pUH#}) Purifier of food, a vaidik epithet of the Sun; comp. {#annapati#}. E. {#anna#} and {#pU#}.

{#annapUrRA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-RA#}) <sup>1</sup> A name of Durgā or Pārvatī (lit. ‘full with food’). [“ <sup>2</sup> Hence applied to a female cook under whose management the daily provision seems blessed and increased. <sup>3</sup> A term for an alm's bag. <sup>4</sup> A particular drink- ing vessel used at Benares; so named after the goddess.”] E. {#anna#} and {#pUrRa#}.
{#annapUrvA(?)#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-rvA#}) A name of Durgā. Comp. the preceding. E. {#anna#} and {#pUrva#}.

{#annapeya#}¦ Bahuvr. n. ({#-yam#}) (ved.) A synonyme of the sacrifice {#vAjapeya#} q. v.; {#vAja#} in the latter word being a synonyme of {#anna#}; according to Sāyana: ‘because a spirituous liquor prepared from rice is drunk at that sacrifice’ ({#vAjaSabdo#} {#'nnavAcI . annamannavikAraBUtaM surAdravyaM pIyate'treti hi vyu-#} {#tpattiH#}). See {#anna#} 2. 9. and compare {#annamala#}. E. {#anna#} and {#peya#}.
{#annaprada#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-daH-dA-dam#}) The same as {#annada#} q. v. E. {#anna#} and {#prada#}.

{#annapralaya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Becoming merged into {#anna#} (2. 2) q. v., returning to it after death, the reverse of {#annaja#} q. v. (comp. the passage mentioned under the latter word). E. {#anna#} and {#pralaya#}.
{#annaprASa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-SaH#}) The same as the following. E. {#anna#} and {#prASa#}.

{#annaprASana#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nam#}) Giving food to eat, scil. to a [Page135-a+ 56] child: the seventh of the ten essential rites enjoined to the the three first castes (see {#saMskAra#}); it ought to take place according to Āsvālāyana, Manu, Yājnavalkya &c. in the sixth month after a child's birth; according to Kātyāyana and his school in the sixth (or, according to some, in the eighth month) if the child is a boy, in the fifth or seventh, if it is a girl. According to Āsvālāyana a father, if he desire plenty (for his child?) ought to give it a soup or sauce made of goat's flesh ({#‘AjamannAdyakAmaH’#}); if he de- sire holiness, a soup or sauce made of the flesh of a fran- coline patridge, called tittiri ({#‘tEttiraM brahmavarcasakAmaH’#}); if he desire strength, boiled rice sprinkled over with very little clarified butter, but not fried in butter, as it would then not be moist ({#‘GftOdanaM tejaskAmaH’#}) [The restriction made by the comm. in his explanation of the word {#GftOdana#} is not justified by himself, but countenanced by the gloss of Patanjali on a Vārttika ({#‘saMpratyayAcca tadarTADyavasAnam’#}) to Pāṇini II. 1. 34]; or if he have no particular desire, boiled rice mixed with curdled milk, honey and clarified butter ({#‘daDimaDuGftamiSramannaM prASayet’#}). [The word {#anna#} supplied at {#Aja#} and {#tEttira#} is, as the comm. observes, not to be taken there in its usual sense ‘boiled rice’ but in that of soup or sauce, {#vyaYjana#}.] When giving the food, whatever be its substance, the father speaks the verse: {#annapate'nnasya#} {#no dehyanamIvasya SuzmiRaH#} &c. (Vājas. Sanh. 11. 83.), if the child is a boy; if it is a girl, the ceremony is performed without the recital of the mantra ({#‘AvftEva kumAryE’#}).-- According to the school of Kātyāyana the food varies still more according to the nature of the desires: that cor- responding with the desire of eloquence is the flesh (pro- bably the sauce made of the flesh of) a skylark ({#BaradvAjI#}); with the desire of plenty, that of a partridge, called {#ka-#} {#piYjala#}; with the desire of quickness that of a fish; with the desire of long life that of the partridge called {#kfkaRA#}; with the desire of holiness that of the Śaralī bird ({#AwI#}); with the desire of all the advantages mentioned before that of all these animals together; the dish must moreover in general contain honey, clarified butter and bits of gold (Reṇuka in his Gṛhyakārikā: {#‘maDvAjyakanakopetaM sarvaM tadyuga-#} {#patpraBuH . mAMsaM tacca BaradvAjyA yadIcCedvAkprasAritAm . kA-#} {#piYjalaM cedannAdyaM mAtsyaM ca javanaM yadi . AyuScetkfkaRAyASca#} {#tadAwyAScedbrahmavarcasam . sarvaM cetsarvamAMsAni sahAnnaM prASayecCu-#} {#Bam’#}); the ceremony is performed while a mantra is in- audibly muttered and the child is sitting on the lap of its mother before the divinity of the family; preparatory pro- cedings are, according to Reṇuka, those connected with the fixing of an auspicious day, the Ābhyudayika-śrāddha (the same as the Vṛddhi-Śr.), austerities, as suspending the breath, meditation on the divinity and oblations (āhutis) with clarified butter while remembering the divine powers of speech ({#vAc#}), the vital airs {#prARa#} and {#apAna#}, eye ({#cakzus#}) and ear ({#Srotra#}), lastly an oblation of {#caru#} (q. v.) to Agni ({#agniH svizwakft#}).--According to Bhavadeva, as quoted by Rādhākānta, the order of the procedings is: fixing of an auspicious day, ablutions, performance of the Vṛddhi-Śrāddha, collecting of the sacrificial fire, making [Page135-b+ 56] a heap of Kuśagrass(?) (acc. to Reṇuka: of fifty leaves of this grass), then silently throwing into the fire a piece of fuel smeared with clarified butter, of a span's length, then the oblation (homa) which is accompanied with the three sacred words bhūr, bhuvar and svar, then five oblations (āhutis) with clarified butter, then the homa of the five vital airs ({#prARa#}), or instead of the two latter(?) the ceremony practised in the north which begins with the Śāṭyāyana- homa and ends with the hymn called Vāmadevya; these procedings are followed by the essential rite of giving the food and by, what is essential too, the presents to the of- ficiating priest. (Comp. also {#annaBukti#}.) E. {#anna#} and {#prASana#}.

{#annabuBukzu#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kzuH-kzuH-kzu#}) Desirous of eating food &c., see the meanings of {#anna#}; (the same notion may also be expressed by {#annaM buBukzuH#}). E. {#anna#} and {#buBukzu#}.
{#annabrahman#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-hma#}) Brahman (n.) or the Supreme Soul in its lowest form or {#anna#} (2. 2.) q. v. E. {#anna#} and {#brahman#}.
{#annabrahmavid#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-t#}) One who considers Brahman (n.) or the Supreme Soul to be the same as {#anna#} (q. v. 2. 2.). E. {#annabrahman#} and {#vid#}.
{#annaBakza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kzaH#}) The eating of food; e. g. {#aDa-#} {#ucCizwo'nnaBakzodakapAnezu gAyatrIjapaH#}. E. {#anna#} and {#Bakza#}.
{#annaBakzaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) The same as {#annaBukti#} q. v. and used also in the same manner. E. {#anna#} and {#BakzaRa#}.
{#annaBAga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A portion of food &c. <sup>2</sup> Sharing in food, a share in food &c. See {#anna#}. E. {#anna#} and {#BAga#}.

{#annaBukti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ktiH#}) The eating of food; the word oc- curs also as a synonyme of the ceremony {#annaprASana#}, the latter being the action of the father, and {#annaBukti#} that of the child. E. {#anna#} and {#Bukti#}.
{#annaBuj#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-k-k-k#}) Eating food; also as an epithet of Śiva. E. {#anna#} and {#Buj#}.

{#annamaya#}¦ 1. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yI-yam#}) <sup>1</sup> Made of, consisting of, the metaphysical or mystical {#anna#} (2. 2.) q. v.; e. g. {#annamayaM hi somyaM#} {#manaH#}; the quality of the Supreme Soul in its lowest form of manifestation; see {#anna#} 2. 2, {#prARamaya, manomaya, vijYAnamaya#} and {#Anandamaya#}; comp. also {#annarasamaya; annamayo rasaH#}, the same as {#annarasa#} (2. b.) q. v. <sup>2</sup> Chiefly (but not entirely) consisting of boiled rice &c. (see the meanings of {#anna#}); e. g. {#annamayo yajYaH#}. <div n="P">2. n. ({#-yam#}) Plenty of boiled rice, food &c. [The two latter meanings of this word result from the different inter- pretation of the commentators on Pāṇ. V. 4. 21; as regards the first, it may be observed that {#annamaya#} is not allowed to mean ‘made of, or consisting of, food, boiled rice &c.’ in the usual, non-mystical sense of this word; the word expressing this notion is {#Anna#}.] E. {#anna#}, taddh. aff. {#mayaw#}.

{#annamayakoSa#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-SaH#}) The sheath made of {#anna#} 2. 2., of the essence of the elementary creation, i. e. the material creation: the lowest form in which Brahman (n.) or the Supreme Soul is considered as manifesting itself in its world- ly and conscious existence.--In the Taittirīya-Upan. {#anna#} of which the material creation is made, is the product of herbs, these of earth and so on in retrogression, of the elements water, fire and æther, the latter being the first product of the Supreme Soul; it would appear therefore that Brahman (n.) as {#annamayakoSa#}, in this Upanishad, [Page136-a+ 56] is the totality of the {%animal kingdom%} only, since the vegetable kingdom precedes the creation of {#anna#} which is called also {#sarvOzaDa#} (see {#anna#} 2. 2.) and the beings ({#prajAH#} or {#BUtAni#}) originating in {#anna#}, are represented as {%living%} through it ({#‘aTo'nenEva jIvanti’#}); but as {#anna#} on the other hand, is the essence of the elements preceding it, this form of Brahman would become in the Upanishad, constructively, the same that it is in the Vedānta explicitly, viz. the to- tality of the whole material creation. Yet while the Upa- nishad uses the terms æther, air, fire, water and earth to denote the elements in a general sense, the Vedānta dis- tinguishes between ideal ({#sUkzma#}) and real ({#sTUla#}) elements and makes the {#annamayakoSa#} proceed from the latter which are an artificial mutual combination of portions of the former (see {#BUta, sUkzmaBUta#} and {#sTUlaBUta#}); and while the Upanishad contents itself with the general idea of totality, as expressed above, the Vedānta distinguishes between the conception that may be formed of the Supreme Soul as unity in this totality of the material creation (comp. {#samazwi#}) and the con- ception that may be formed of it as multiplicity in it (comp. {#vyazwi#}); as unity it is called {#vESvAnara#} or {#virAj#}, as multi- plicity {#viSva#}, in either case it is {#jAgrat#}.--The forms superior to the {#annamayakoSa#} are in successive gradation {#prARamayakoSa#}, {#manomayakoSa, vijYAnamayakoSa#} and {#AnandamayakoSa#} qq. vv. (the word {#koSa#} being supplied, in the Upanishad, by the comm. to {#annamaya#} &c.). Compare also {#sUkzmaSarIra#} and {#sTU-#} {#laSarIra#}. E. {#annamaya#} and {#koSa#}. Also written {#annamayakoza#}.
{#annamayakoza#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-zaH#}) The same as {#annamayakoSa#} q. v.

{#annamala#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-lam#}) <sup>1</sup> Offal, sweepings. <sup>2</sup> The worst kind of spirituous liquor, viz. {#surA#}. [The latter meaning requires an explanation: Manu 11. 93 says: {#surA vE mala-#} {#mannAnAM#} &c. and forbids the drinking of the spirituous liquor {#surA#} to a man of the three first castes; Kullūka in his com- ment seems to take {#malamannAnAM#} or {#annamala#} in the general sense of ‘extract of rice’, because {#surA#} is made from the flower of rice ({#taRqulapizwasADyatvAtsurA annamalam#}); but Pulastya, as quoted by Vijnāneśvara in the Mitākṣara names twelve sorts of intoxicating drinks, stating that {#surA#} is the very worst description amongst them: {#pAnasaM drAkzaM mADUkaM KArjUraM#} {#tAlamEkzavam . maDUtTaM sEramArizwamEreyaM nArikelajam . samA-#} {#nAni vijAnIyAnmadyAnyekAdaSEva tu . dvAdaSaM tu surAmadyaM sarve-#} {#zAmaDamaM smftam#}; and Vijnāneśvara in commenting upon the quoted passage of Manu and adducing Pāṇ. II. 1. 34. where the word {#anna#} means a preparation of rice &c. observes that it is intended to convey in this passage the sense of spirituous liquor, the latter being also an {#annavikAra#} or preparation of rice, and {#surA#} being used also in the Sautrā- maṇī libations in the sense of spirituous liquor made of rice: {#‘surA vE malamannAnAM pApmA ca malamucyata iti . annavikAra-#} {#syEva surAtvanirdeSAdannaSabdasya cAnnena vyaYjanamityAdizu vrIhyA-#} {#divikAra eva prayogadarSanAdguqamaDunoSca rasarUpatvAttaTA sO-#} {#trAmaRIgrahezu cAnnavikAra eva surASabdasya SrutatvAt . ’#}. For this meaning of {#anna#} compare also {#annapeya#}.] E. {#anna#} and {#mala#}.
{#annarakzA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-kzA#}) Precaution in eating; compare {#annapAnarakzA#}. E. {#anna#} and {#rakzA#}.

{#annarasa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) <sup>1</sup> The essential properties of food, esp. the good or salutary properties; e. g. {#apaTyEH saha saMBukte#} {#vyADirannarase yaTA#} ‘just as disease may lurk in the good essence of food when it is eaten with unwholesome sub- stances’; or {#yamastvannarasaM prAdAt#} ‘Yama gave (Nala) the distinguished properties of food’ (comm. {#‘annarasaM yAdfSe#} {#tAdfSe'pyanne viSizwarasavattAm’#}). <sup>2</sup> (In the Taittirīya Upan.) <sup>a.</sup> Semen virile, as the essence of {#anna#} 2. 2.; <sup>b.</sup> the same as {#anna#} 2. 2. q. v. See the following. E. {#anna#} and {#rasa#}.

{#annarasamaya#}¦ m. ({#-yaH#}) (In the Taittirīya Upanishad.) <sup>1</sup> Made of the essence of {#anna#} 2. 2., being the very essence of {#anna#} 2. 2. q. v., viz. man, {#‘annAdretaH . retasaH puruzaH . sa vA eza#} {#puruzo'nnarasamayaH .’#}. <sup>2</sup> The same as {#annamayakoSa#} q. v. {#‘tasmAdvA etasmAdannarasamayAdanyo'ntarAtmA prARamayaH’#}. E. {#annarasa#}, taddh. aff. {#mayaw#}.
{#annalipsA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-psA#}) Craving, appetite. E. {#anna#} and {#lipsA#}.
{#annavat#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-vAn-vatI-vat#}) Rich in food. E. {#anna#}, taddh. aff. {#matup#}.
{#annavastra#}¦ Dwandwa n. ({#-stram#}) Food and clothing, the ne- cessaries of life. Comp. {#annAcCAdana#}. E. {#anna#} and {#vastra#}.
{#annavAhisrotas#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-taH#}) (In Medicine.) The œso- phagus, the gullet. E. {#anna-vAhin#} and {#srotas#}.

{#annavikAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) <sup>1</sup> Transformation of food; used in general of any preparation of an article of food, e. g. of {#saktu, puroqASa, surA, yavasurA, pizwasurA#} (comp. s. v. {#anna-#} {#mala#}); according to an observation of Vardhamāna, however, only of an artificial preparation, of made dishes, e. g. of sweetmeats, {#SazkulImodaka#} &c. (which would include, too, the given instances {#saktu#} &c. occurring in the Mahābhāṣya, Kāśikā, Bhaṭṭikāvya &c.), not of preparations which re- present, as it were, the original substance only in a different shape, as of {#pfTuka#}, rice or grain flattened, {#apUpa#}, cake of flour &c. (This observation is in accordance, also, with the author of the gaṇa {#apUpAdi#} to Pāṇ. V. 1. 4. where the words {#apUpa#} and {#pfTuka#} occur besides {#annavikAra#}). <sup>2</sup> The seminal secretion. <sup>3</sup> Transformation of the metaphysical or mystical food; see {#anna#} 2. 2. and compare {#annavikAratva#}. E. {#anna#} and {#vikAra#}.

{#annavikAratva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The being a transformation of food; of the metaphysical or mystical food (see {#anna#} 2. 2.), e. g. {#annaM#} {#vE virAqiti SruterannavikAratvam#} ‘from the vaidik passage “Virāj is food” follows his being a transformation of food’; comp. {#annabrahman#} and the following. E. {#annavikAra#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}. This word ought perhaps to be read {#annavikAritva#}.
{#annavikArin#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-rI-riRI-ri#}) Being a transformation of food or metaphysical food; comp. the following. E. {#annavikAra#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#annavikAritva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The same as {#annavikAratva#}; e. g. {#asyEzA samazwiH sTUlaSarIramannavikAritvAdannamayakoSaH sTUla-#} {#BogAyatanatvAjjAgradityucyate#}; compare s. v. {#annamayakoSa#}. E. {#annavikArin#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.
{#annavid#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-t-t-t#}) Probably: Knowing (the properties of) food. (ved.) E. {#anna#} and {#vid#}.
{#annavfkza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kzaH#}) A tree of plenty (lit. a tree of food); e. g. {#annadasyAnnavfkzASca sarvakAmaPalapradAH#}. E. {#anna#} and {#vfkza#}.
{#annavyavahAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Law or custom relating to food, viz. to the practise of eating together or not, as followed by different castes. E. {#anna#} and {#vyavahAra#}.
{#annaSeza#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-zaH#}) Leavings, offal. E. {#anna#} and {#Seza#}.
{#annasaMskAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Consecration of food, by means of a sacrificial act; comp. the following. E. {#anna#} and {#saMskAra#}.
{#annasaMskArakarman#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-rma#}) A sacrificial act by which food becomes consecrated; e. g. the Vaiśvadevahoma. E. {#annasaMskAra#} and {#karman#}.

{#annasidDi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dDiH#}) The means of preparing food; e. g. {#yezAM…nEvAnnasidDirna taTAnnamasti#} (comm.: {#yezAmannaM#} {#nAsti yezAM ca satyanne nAtra sidDiH pAkasADanaM nAstItyarTaH#}). E. {#anna#} and {#sidDi#}.
{#annahartf#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rtA-rtrI-tf#}) One who steals food; e. g. {#annahartA mayAvI syAt#}. E. {#anna#} and {#hartf#}.

{#annahoma#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) An oblation forming part of the ceremonies in the Aśvamedha; it is made in the fire of the Uttaravedi (q. v.) and continued during a whole night, con- sisting in the first watch of the night, of clarified butter ({#Ajya#} or {#Gfta#}), in the second of fried rice ({#saktu#}), in the third of fried barley ({#DAnAH#}) and in the fourth of fried corn ({#lAjAH#}). Comp. {#annADISa#}. E. {#anna#} and {#homa#}.
[{#annAkAla#}.¦ A misreading for {#anAkAla#} q. v. See the following.]

[{#annAkAlaBfta#}.¦ A misreading for {#anAkAlaBfta#} q. v. As the reading {#annAkAlaBfta#} occurs in the present edition of the Vivādachintāmaṇi while the reading {#anAkAlaBfta#} is given in one E. [According to Vopadeva (7. 96.) {#anyatama#} is formed with the taddh. aff. {#qatama#} and would therefore be a pronoun, according to his rule 3. 9., which again would assimilate its declension to that of {#sarva#} (cf. 3. 35-37. 75); but as there is no evidence to this effect in Pāṇini or in the literature, and as Vopad. himself mentions {#anyatara#} in the rule 3. 9., the word {#anya#} in the rule 7. 96. must be an inaccuracy of this gram- marian, the correctness of the reading being placed beyond doubt by the comm. of Durgādāsa.] E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#tamap#}.

{#anyatara#}¦ 1. (see {#sarvanAman#}) m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-rad(-rat)#}; the dat., abl., gen. and loc. sing., the nom. and gen. plur. are similar to the corresponding cases of {#anya#} q. v.) <sup>1</sup> Either of two; e. g. {#uBayoH pakzayoranyatarasyADyApanAdapratizeDaH#}; or {#nityo-#} {#palabDyanupalabDiprasaNgo'nyataraniyamo vAnyaTA#} (Śaṅkara: {#a-#} {#nyatarasyAtmana indriyasya vA SaktipratibanDaH#} &c.); or {#svApyaya-#} {#saMpattyoranyatarApekzamAvizkftaM hi#} (i. e. either of profound sleep or of final emancipation).--In the rules of Pāṇini {#anyata-#} {#rasyAm#} (the locat. sing. of the femin.) ‘in either way’ means that a given rule is optional, may take place or not; comp. for synonymous terms {#vA, viBAzA#}, and the more precise terms {#aprAptaviBAzA, prAptaviBAzA, uBayatraviBAzA, vyavasTitavi-#} {#BAzA, mahAviBAzA, sarvaviBAzA#}, also {#viBAzita, uBayaTA#}, {#vikalpa#}. <sup>2</sup> {%The%} other of two (one having been mentioned) [this meaning is probably meant when the Amarakosha, He- machandra &c. make {#anyatara#} a synonyme of {#anya#} ‘other’]; e. g. in the Vārttika to Pāṇini V. 2. 47 {#eko'nyataraH#}, where {#anyataraH#} is opposed as {#nimeyam#} to the word expressing the {#nimAnam#}, as in the instance {#dvimayamudaSvidyavAnAm#}, where {#udaSvit#} ‘the object to be valued which is {#eka#} ‘one’, is {#nimeya#}, and the {#yava#} ‘the object determining the value ({#ni-#} {#mAnam#} or {#mUlyam#}) is {#nimAna#}’ (comp. Kaiyyaṭa: {#anyataraSa-#} {#bdena nimeyameva vivakzitam . eka eva yadi nimeyaguRo Bava-#} {#ti tadA pratyayaH#}). <sup>3</sup> One of two, each being one of many; in this sense its use is probably restricted to passages be- longing to the vaidik period, when it is followed by a cor- relate {#anyatara#}, both implying then ‘the one--the other, one--another’ (comp. {#anya--anya#}); e. g. Śatapathabr. I. 2. 1. 1. {#sa vE kapAlAnyevAnyatara upadaDAti . dfzadupale'nya-#} {#taraH#} (thus explained in the genuine comm. of Śāyaṇa: {#a-#} {#nyataraH . ftvijAM maDya ekaH . AgnIDraH . sa kapAlAnAmupa-#} {#DAtA . anyataro'DvaryuH . sa pezaRArTaM dfzadupale upadaDyAt#}). <div n="P">2. m. ({#-raH#}) A proper name; comp. {#Anyatareya#} (and {#itara#}, {#Etareya#}). E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#qatara#}.
{#anyataratas#}¦ ind. On one of two sides. Comp. {#anyatas#}. E. {#anyatara#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#tasil#}.

{#anyataratodanta#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ntaH-ntA-ntam#}) Having teeth on one side only, having but one row of teeth (as {#prajAH#}, living beings); opposed to {#uBayatodanta#} i. e. men, horses and other animals which have two rows of teeth; both [Page140-b+ 56] categories being intended in a vaidik passage to comprise all living beings in general. E. {#anyataratas#} and {#danta#}.

{#anyataratoyukta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) Having (the draught- beast) put to but one side of it; said in a vaidik passage of a cart which has one ox put to it. E. {#anyataratas#} and {#yukta#}.

{#anyataratva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) Eitherness, the relation of either--or, alternativeness; e. g. {#anyataratvenAnugatIkftataddarSanAdapi na#} {#saMSayaH#} ‘nor can doubt arise from comprehending an object and beholding it under the relation of either--or’; see the following. E. {#anyatara#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anyataraDarma#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rmaH#}) The quality or relation of {#a-#} {#nyatara#}, the same as {#anyataratva#}; e. g. {#samAnAnekaDarmADyavasA-#} {#yAdanyataraDarmADyavasAyAdvA na saMSayaH#} ‘doubt can not arise from apprehending mentally an object under the relation of sameness (with), or difference (from, other objects), nor can it arise from apprehending it under that of (being) either (one thing) or (another). Comp. {#vipratipatti#}. E. {#anyatara#} and {#Darma#}.
{#anyatarasyAm#}.¦ See s. v. {#anyatara#}.

{#anyataredyus#}¦ ind. Either of two days, on the one day or on the other. E. {#anyatara#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#edyusac#} (but more likely a Karmadh. {#anyatare#} (obsolete loc. of {#anyatara#}) and {#dyus#} (obsolete genitive of {#div#}); see the Preface).

{#anyatas#}¦ ind. Used in the same manner as 1. the ablative and 2. the locative of {#anya#}, absolutely or with the ellipsis of a word implying ‘place’, ‘manner’ &c., viz. <div n="P">1. = the ablative of {#anya#}, ‘from another’; e. g. {#BAvitaM#} {#pakzato'BIzwO tyaktvA varRO sarUpakO . anyato BAvitANkena#} {#tataH pakzO viBajya ca#} &c., i. e. ‘removing the factum from one side and the simple colours and absolute numbers from the other, as optionally selected, and dividing both sides of the equation by the coefficient of the factum &c.’; also with a noun depending on it in the ablative, e. g. in the comm. of the Kāsikā on Pāṇ. IV. 1. 40. ‘{#topaDAdanyataH prAtipadikA-#} {#dvarRavAcino'nudAttAtstriyAM NIzpratyayo Bavati#}. <div n="P">2. = the locative of {#anya#} and in the same sense as {#anyatra#}, viz. <sup>1</sup> In another, on another; e. g. {#anyato vfttO#} (comm. = {#anyatra jAtO#}) ‘in another way’; or in Hemachandra's explanation of {#vijYAna, ‘mokze jYAnaM vijYAnamanyataH#}, i. e. {#jYAna#} means (knowledge of what concerns) final emancipa- tion, {#vijYAna#} other (knowledge), where {#anyataH#} represents the locative {#anyasmin#}, the explaining words being put in the locative, and does not mean ‘in another case, else- where’. <sup>2</sup> (Scil. {#deSe#}) Elsewhere; e. g. {#pratipattiSUnyamutTA-#} {#pyAnyataH pravfttaH#}; or {#yAnto'nyataH…AtmavargyAH#}; also re- peated: ‘in one place--in another place’, e. g. {#aSfRvanna-#} {#nyataH SabdaM prapalAyanta cAnyataH . Akrandamanyato'kurvestenAhanyanta#} {#cAnyataH ..#}. Comp. {#anyatovAta#}. <sup>3</sup> (Scil. {#deSe#}) In one place, in one direction (ved.); comp. {#anyatoGAtin, anyatomuKa#}, {#anyato'raRya#}. <sup>4</sup> (Scil. {#deSe#}) On the other side, on the con- trary. <sup>5</sup> (Scil. {#prakAre#}) In another way or manner, otherwise; e. g. {#vAzpaBarastayA calitayA niHSvasya mukto'nyataH#}. E. {#anya#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#tasil#}.
{#anyatastya#}¦ m. ({#-tyaH#}) (ved.) An adversary, an enemy. (Ac- cording to a comm. lit. ‘one born from another mother’.) E. {#anyatas#}, taddh. aff. {#tyap#}.

{#anyatA#}¦ f. ({#-tA#}) The being other, otherness, difference; also {#anyatva#} q. v.; e. g. {#jAtilakzaRadeSEranyatAnavacCedAttulyayostataH#} {#pratipattiH#} (Difference) is understood through it (viz. through profound meditation), since it is impossible to remove the otherness which exists between two (apparently) like objects either with regard to species or characteristic properties or space; (as in the case, for instance of various atoms, or of Īśvara and the Yogin). E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#tal#}.
{#anyatABAva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) Non-existence of otherness; comp. the passage s. v. {#anya#}. E. {#anyatA#} and {#aBAva#}.
{#anyatoGAtin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-tI#}) (ved.) One who strikes in one direction. E. {#anyatas#} and {#GAtin#}.

{#anyatomuKa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-KaH#}) (ved.) Having the face only in one place; opposed to {#sarvatomuKa#} or (the sacrificer) who by shaving off his hairs, makes his scull, through its bald- ness, resemble the face and thus becomes as it were ‘face all over’ (according to the comm. of Sāyaṇa on Śatapa- thabr. II. 6. 3. 16, which unmutilated runs thus: {#ayaMSabda-#} {#stvarTe . ayaM tu puruzo yajamAno'nyatomuKaH . anyaSabda ekaSa-#} {#bdaparyAyaH . anyata ekatra sTitameva muKaM yasya sa taToktaH . tasya#} {#sarvatomuKatvasaMpattimAha . sa etaditi . yadyasmAtparitaH Siro#} {#vartayate keSAnvApayati . etat . etena . alomakatvasAmyAcCi-#} {#rasaH prAntadeSA api muKamiva BavantIti sa yajamAnaH sarvato-#} {#muKo Bavati ..#}). E. {#anyatas#} and {#muKa#}.

{#anyato'raRya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ryam#}) (ved.) A place which is forest only on one spot; (this is probably the meaning of this word in the vaidik passage {#vanAya vanapamanyato'raRyAya dA-#} {#vapam#} where it is opposed to {#vana#}). E. {#anyatas#} and {#araRya#}.

{#anyatovAta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) (In Medicine.) A disease of the whole eye ({#sarvAkziroga#}); symptoms and etymology are con- veyed by the following verse: {#yasyAvawUkarRaSirohanusTo ma-#} {#nyAgato vApyanilo'nyato vA . kuryAdrujo'ti Bruvi locane vA#} {#tamanyatovAtamudAharanti#} ‘when the {%air%} of the back of the neck, of ears, head, jaw, the tendons which form the nape of the neck or {%elsewhere%} produces excessive pain in the eye- brow and eye, they call this (disease of the eye) {#anyato-#} {#vAta#}’. The word occurs also in its uncompounded state, e. g. {#hatADimanTo'nilaparyAyaSca SuzkAkzipAko'nyata eva#} {#vAtaH#}. E. {#anyatas#} and {#vAta#}.

{#anyatkAma#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-maH-mA-mam#}) Having desire for something else; comp. {#anyakAma#}. (The correctness of this word is doubtful, as it is not mentioned by Pāṇini amongst those compounds in which {#anya#} retains the {#d#} of its neuter; see s. v. {#anya#}.) E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#} and {#kAma#}.

{#anyatkAraka#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-rakaH-rikA-rakam#}) I. Karmadh. Another agent (Kāsikā = {#anyaH kArakaH#}). <div n="P">II. Tatpur. Agent of another (Patanjali and Kāśikā = {#a-#} {#nyasya kArakaH#}). (With regard to the first part of the com- pound see s. v. {#anya#}.) E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#} and {#kAraka#}.

{#anyatra#}¦ (ved. also {#anyatrA#}) ind. Used in the same sense as the locat. of {#anya#}, absolutely or with the ellipsis of a word im- plying ‘place’, ‘manner’ &c.; comp. {#anyatas#}; viz. <sup>1</sup> In another or others, on another or others, e. g. {#anyatra jAtO#} (see the instance s. v. {#anyatas#}); {#anyatrArTe; sarvABedAdanyatreme#} (which Vedānta Sūtra is explained: {#sarvaSAKAsu prARopA-#} {#sanasyABedAdanyatra SAKAntare ime vasizWatvAdiguRAH samAhA-#} [Page141-b+ 56] {#ryAH#}); or {#sAhasasteyapAruzyago'BiSApAtyaye striyAm . vivA-#} {#dayetsadya eva kAlo'nyatrecCayA smftaH#} (comm. {#anyatra = vi-#} {#vAdAntarezu#}); also with a noun depending on it in the ablat. ‘in another than’, e. g. in the Sūtra of Pāṇ. {#tAByAmanyatro-#} {#RAdayaH#} (Kāśikā: {#uRRAdayaH pratyayAstAByAM saMpradAnApAdAnA-#} {#ByAmanyatra kArake Bavanti#}); or {#DAtvarTAnAM saMbanDe yatra kAle pra-#} {#tyayA uktAstato'nyatrApi Bavanti#}. <sup>2</sup> Elsewhere; in space or time, e. g. {#yadA CalaM vinEva kAryAtiSayAdanyatra gataH#} &c.; or {#etezAM#} (scil. {#rUparasaganDasparSAnAM#}) {#pAkajatvaM tu kzitO nA-#} {#nyatra kutracit#}; also with a noun in the ablat., e. g. (Kā- śikā on Pāṇini VIII. 1. 12. v. 10.) {#strInigadaBAvAdanyatrApi#} {#dfSyate#}. <sup>3</sup> In another manner, differently from; with a noun in the ablative, e. g. {#apatyADikArAdanyatra lOkikamapatyamAtraM#} {#gotram#}, i. e. {#gotra#} in Pāṇini's rule IV. 2. 39 is to be taken in the sense of a son only, differently from the chapter on {#apatya#} (IV. 1. 162) where it means the descendants beginning with the grandson ({#apatyamAtraM na tu pOtrapraBftyeva#} Kāś.). <sup>4</sup> In another or different sense; e. g. {#kAraskaro vfkzaH . anyatra kA-#} {#rakaraH#}; or {#ekatra rajo DUliranyatra guRaH#}. <sup>5</sup> Except, with a noun in the ablative, e. g. {#SabdArTayoH punarvacanaM punaruktamanya-#} {#trAnuvAdAt#} ‘repetition of word or sense is called {#punarukta#}, unless it be an {#anuvAda#} q. v.’; or {#ta indriyARi tadvyapadeSA-#} {#danyatra SrezWAt#} ‘these (eleven prāṇas) are the senses except the principal one, because exception of it is taken (in a vaidik passage)’; {#anyatra nityadravyeBya ASritatvamihocyate#} ‘dependence is said (to be the attribute of every thing) ex- cept (of) eternal substances. [More frequently used so in the Buddhistic than in the Brāhmanic writings, according to Burnouf, {%Lotus de la bonne loi,%} II. p. 653.] <sup>6</sup> Without; with a noun in the ablative; e. g. {#DenvEva hyupayuktaM tfRAdi#} {#kzIrIBavati na prahInamanaquhAdyupayuktaM vA . yadi hi nirnimi-#} {#ttametatsyAt . DenuSarIrasaMbanDAdanyatrApi tfRAdi kzIrIBavet#}. <sup>7</sup> In the contrary case, otherwise; comp. {#anyaTA#} and {#itaratra#}; e. g. {#devikAdizu tadAdigrahaRam . anyatra hi tadgrahaRAttadanta-#} {#grahaRAdvA#}. E. {#anya#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#tral#}.

{#anyatradattAkza#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kzaH-kzI-kzam#}) Turning the eyes elsewhere, e. g. {#anyEH pravartitAM SaSvatsAvaDAnA ca tatka-#} {#TAm . SfRotyanyatradattAkzI priye bAlAnurAgiRI#}. E. {#anyatra-#} {#datta#} and {#akzi#}, samās. aff. {#zac#}.

{#anyatramanas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-nAH-nAH-naH#}) Having the mind directed on another object, absent (mentally). [The passage of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upan. {#anyatramanA aBUvaM nASrOzam#} &c. is given as a proof by the Sāṅkhya Pravachana Bh. for the orthodoxy of the Sāṅkhya tenet that {#manas#} is capable of becoming multifarious.] E. {#anyatra#} and {#manas#}.

{#anyatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The being other, otherness, difference (the same as {#anyatA#}, but more frequently used as this word); e. g. {#anyatve'pyaByAsasyopacArAt#} ‘even if there were different (sounds, sound must be permanent) because it is possible to repeat it (in teaching)’; also with a noun in the ablative, e. g. {#vacanAttu tato'nyatvam#} ‘(if it is main- tained that {#itikartavyatA#} refers to profane things, the answer is:) but on account of a (distinct vaidik) passage its dif- ference from that (is established), i. e. it refers only to sacred or vaidik objects’; or {#tayoranyatve tucCatvam#} (comm. {#akA-#} {#ryasya prakftipuruzaBinnatve tucCatvam#} &c.).--The word occurs [Page142-a+ 56] for the most part, however, as the latter part of a com- pound--e. g. {#sPawikAnyatvABimAnavattadanyatvABimAnaH#}-- and especially in scientific writings, e. g. in the Vārttikas of Pāṇini in compounds as {#aNgAnyatva, kartranyatva, kArakAnyatva#}, {#kAlAnyatva#}, in the Vedānta Sūtras as in {#tadananyatva#}, in the Mīmānsā S. as in {#prayojanAnyatva, vedAnyatva, rUpAnyatva#} &c., in the Nyāya S. as in {#sTAnAnyatva, karmAnyatva#}, in the Sāṅkhya S. {#uBayAnyatva#}, in the Yoga S. as in {#kramAnyatva#} &c. &c. E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.
{#anyatvakara#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rI-ram#}) Producing other- ness or difference; as species, characteristic properties, space. E. {#anyatva#} and {#kara#} ({#kf#}, kṛt aff. {#wa#}).

{#anyaTA#}¦ ind. <sup>1</sup> In another manner, differently; e. g. {#kurvanneveha#} {#karmARi jijIvizecCataM samAH . evaM tvayi nAnyaTeto'sti na#} {#karma lipyate nare#}; or {#vipakzacittonmaTanA naKavraRAstirohitA#} {#viBramamaRqanena ye . hftasya SezAniva kuNkumasya tAnvikatTanIyA-#} {#ndaDuranyaTA striyaH#} ‘…the women made these wounds different, i. e. not concealed; they laid them open (comm.: {#prakASaM daDurityarTaH#}); or {#tarkApratizWAnAdapyanyaTAnumeyamiti cet#} &c.; comp. {#anyaTAnumiti; anyaTA--anyaTA#} ‘in one way --in another way’, e. g. {#anyaTA hi prakramante vAjasaneyinaH .#} {#anyaTA CandogAH#}; also with a noun depending in the abl., for the most part with {#atas (= asmAt)#}, e. g. {#apfzwo'pi#} {#hitaM brUyAdyasya necCetparABavam . eza eva satAM Darmo viparI-#} {#tamato'nyaTA#}. <sup>2</sup> Otherwise, or else; e. g. {#gaterarTavattvamuBa-#} {#yaTAnyaTA hi viroDaH#} ‘the result of the (divine) way is doubtful, otherwise there would be contradiction (with a vaidik passage)’; or…{#drazwumaByAgato hyeza Barato nAnya-#} {#TAgataH#} ‘…or else he would not have come’; {#gurvagniho-#} {#trArTakfte prasTitaSca sutastava . na nivAryo nivAryaH syAdanyaTA#} {#prasTito vanam#} ‘…he was not to be prevented or else he ought to have been prevented: (but now) he is gone to the forest’. Comp. {#anyatra#}. <sup>3</sup> On the other hand, on the contrary; e. g. {#asati#} (scil. {#hetO#}) {#pratijYoparoDo yOgapadyamanyaTA#} (comm.: {#anyaTA = hetO sati#}). <sup>4</sup> Untruly; e. g. {#yasyocuH sAkziRaH satyAM#} {#pratijYAM sa jayI Bavet . anyaTA vAdino yasya Druvastasya parA-#} {#jayaH . ukte'pi sAkziBiH sAkzye yadyanye guRavattamAH . dviguRA#} {#vAnyaTA brUyuH kUwAH syuH pUrvasAkziRaH#} (comm.: {#anyaTA = vE-#} {#parItyena miTyA#}). Comp. also {#anyaTAstotra#}. <sup>5</sup> Badly, wrongly, erroneously; comp. {#anyaTAsidDa#} and {#anyaTAsidDi#}. E. {#anya#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#TAl#}. Comp. {#itaraTA#}.
{#anyaTAkaraRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) Acting to the contrary, doing otherwise. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#karaRa#}.

{#anyaTAkAra#}¦ Tatpur. I. m. ({#-raH#}) Altering, changing, e. g. the sense of an expression, by punning on it; {#vakroktO parokte-#} {#ranyaTAkAraH#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#kAra#}. <div n="P">II. ind. ({#-ram#}) In another manner, differently; e. g. {#anyaTAkAraM BuNkte#} he eats in another manner. [According to the Kāśikā on Pāṇini III. 4. 27. {#kAram#} would in this case be a kind of expletive or superfluous, the word of the Sūtra {#sidDAprayogaH#} being thus commented by it: {#kaTaM puna-#} {#rasO sidDAprayogaH . nirarTakatvAnna prayogamarhati . evameva prayu-#} {#jyate#}; and similarly the Siddh. K.: {#kfYvyarTatvAtprayogAnarha#} {#ityarTaH#}; but Bhaṭṭoji in the Prauḍhaman. is probably more correct when he refers to the bearing of the word ({#SAbda-#} {#boDa#}) and says, that {#kAram#} effectuates a stronger connexion [Page142-b+ 56] between the verb and the adverb than would be expressed without it, when {#sidDAprayoga#} in the Sūtra of Pāṇini would not convey the notion of ‘absolute superfluity’ but rather that of ‘not excessive necessity’: {#SAbdaboDe tu vElakzaRyamastyeva .#} {#taTA hi . kriyAsAmAnyavacanaH karotiH . tadIyaSca prakAro#} {#'nyaTAdiSabdacatuzwvenocyate . evaM ca . anyaTAkAramityAdiBi-#} {#ScaturBiH prakAraviSezaviSizwakriyA boDyate . sA ca BuNktePala-#} {#viSizwakriyAM prati viSezaRatayA saMbaDyate . ekasyA api kri-#} {#yAyA viSezaRoparAgeRa BinnAyA viSezaRaviSezyaBAvasaMBavAt .#} {#kaTaM tarhi sidDAprayogaScedityuktamiti cet . anatiprayojanatvA-#} {#diti gfhARa ..#} &c. Patanjali and his comm. give no gloss on this Sūtra.] E. {#anyaTA#} and {#kAram#} ({#kf#}, kṛt aff. {#Ramul#}).
{#anyaTAkfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Altered, changed, as the sense of a word, by punning on it. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#kfta#}.

{#anyaTAKyAti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) (In the Sāṅkhya philosophy.) Erroneous conception, maintaining that a substance is other than what it appears to be by its form; {#‘anyaTAKyAtiH#} {#svavacovyAGAtAt’#}, comm.: {#anyadvastvanyarUpeRa BAsata ityapi#} {#na yuktaM svavacovyAGAtAt ..#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#KyAti#}.
{#anyaTAKyAtivAdin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-dI#}) One who maintains that a substance is other than what it appears to be by its form. See the preceding. E. {#anyaTAKyAti#} and {#vAdin#}.

{#anyaTAtva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> Difference, variety; e. g. in a Vedānta Sūtra {#anyaTAtvaM SabdAditi cennAviSezAt#}. <sup>2</sup> Change, al- teration; e. g. {#budDeranyaTAtvam (= budDiviplavaH)#}; or in a Mīm. Vārtt. of Kumārila: {#stokenApyanyaTAtvena SAstrArTo nizPalo#} {#Bavet#}. Comp. {#anyaTABAva#}. E. {#anyaTA#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anyaTAnupapatti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ttiH#}) Otherwise not taking place, or existing, or being applicable; e. g. {#kARqasamAKyayA saMniDiM#} {#parikalpya tatsaMniDyanyaTAnupapattyA#} &c.; or {#nanu vESizwyapratyakza-#} {#viSizwabudDyanyaTAnupapattiSca pramARam#}. The reverse of {#anyaTo-#} {#papatti#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#anupapatti#}.
{#anyaTAnumiti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) Inferring or concluding in a different manner; e. g. {#anyaTAnumitO ca jYaSaktiviyogAt#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#anumiti#}.
{#anyaTABAva#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) The same as {#anyaTAtva#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#BAva#}.
{#anyaTABUta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Become different, changed, altered; e. g. {#putrasnehAdanyaTABUtaH (= vikftaH)#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#BUta#}.

{#anyaTAvAditva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) (In Law.) Stating a cause or com- plaint in a different manner than originally; e. g. {#yaTA yena#} {#prakAreRa pUrvamAvedanakAle AveditaM taTA . na punaranyaTA . a-#} {#nyaTAvAditvena BaNgaprasaNgAt#}. E. {#anyaTAvAdin#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.
{#anyaTAvAdin#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-dI#}) (In Law.) A plaintiff who states his cause or complaint in a different manner than he did originally. Comp. {#anyavAdin#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#vAdin#}.
{#anyaTAvftti#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-ttiH-ttiH-tti#}) Changed, altered; e. g. {#cetaH#}. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#vftti#}.

{#anyaTAsidDa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-dDaH-dDA-dDam#}) I. (In the Vaiśeṣika philosophy.) Wrongly established, referred to a cause which is not the true cause (as an effect). See {#anyaTAsidDi#} I. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#sidDa#}. <div n="P">II. Not established otherwise, not proved otherwise. See {#anyaTAsidDi#} II. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#asidDa#}.
{#anyaTAsidDatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The same as the following. E. {#anya-#} {#TAsidDa#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anyaTAsidDi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-dDiH#}) I. (In the Vaiśeṣika philosophy.) The being wrongly established or the establishing wrongly, i. e. the being referred of an effect, or the referring an effect, to a cause which is not the true cause. This may happen in five ways, viz. <sup>a.</sup> by taking for cause what is prior to the effect but only accidental to the real cause ({#‘saha tena’#}), as by taking a potter's stick for the cause of a jar; or <sup>b.</sup> by taking for cause something inherent to what is ac- cidental to the real cause ({#‘yasya’#}), as by taking the shape of a potter's stick for the cause of a jar; or <sup>c.</sup> by taking for cause what is prior but is known to be the cause of another effect ({#‘anyaM prati’#}), as by taking æther for the cause of a jar, æther being the known cause of sound; or <sup>d.</sup> by taking for cause what is prior but prior in so far only as the real cause is produced by it ({#‘janakaM prati’#}), as by tak- ing the potter's father for the cause of a jar; or <sup>e.</sup> by taking for cause any thing foreign to the effect ({#‘atiriktam’#}), as by taking the donkey carrying the earth of which the jar is made, for the cause of the jar. The last error comprises, indeed, in its generality all the preceding and is therefore called {#‘AvaSyaka’#}, the absolute error. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#sidDi#}. <div n="P">II. Not being established or proved otherwise; in the Sān- khya Sūtra: {#uBayatrApyanyaTAsidDerna pratyakzamanumAnaM vA#} (comm. {#uBayatrApi vESizwyapratyakze tadanumAne ca svarUpeREvAnyaTAsidDerna#} {#taduBayaM samavAye pramARamityarTaH . ayaM BAvaH . yaTA samavAyavE-#} {#SizwyabudDirapi guRAdisvarUpeREvezyatAm . atastatrApi pratyakzA-#} {#numAne'nyaTAsidDe#} &c.). E. {#anyaTA#} and {#asidDi#}.

{#anyaTAstotra#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-tram#}) Untrue or ironical praise, a sneer; as saying to a deformed man ‘thou art a handsome one’ (comm.: {#yatra vikftAkftireva darSanIyastvamasItyucyate .#} {#tadanyaTAstotram#}). E. {#anyaTA#} and {#stotra#}.

{#anyaTi#}¦ denom. parasm. ({#-Tayati#}) To change, to alter, e. g. the sense of a word, by punning on it: {#gopanIyaM kamapyarTaM dyota-#} {#yitvA kaTaMcana . yadi SlezeRAnyaTA vA'nyaTayetsApyapahnutiH#}. E. {#anyaTA#}, denom. aff. {#Ric#}.
{#anyaTopapatti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ttiH#}) Otherwise taking place, exist- ing, being applicable; the reverse of {#anyaTAnupapatti#} q. v. E. {#anyaTA#} and {#upapatti#}.
{#anyad#}¦ ind. Beside, moreover; e. g. {#devadatta AyAto'nyadya-#} {#jYadattaH#}; and see s. v. {#anya#}. E. The neuter of {#anya#}.

{#anyadarTa#}¦ I. Karmadh. m. ({#-rTaH#}) Another sense &c. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. m. ({#-rTaH#}) The sense &c. of another. <div n="P">III. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rTaH-rTA-rTam#}) Having another sense &c. (see the meanings of {#arTa#}). Comp. also {#anyArTa#} and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#arTa#}.

{#anyadA#}¦ I. ind. At another time; e. g. {#anyadA BUzaRaM puMsaH kzamA#} {#lajjeva yozitaH . parAkramaH pariBave vEyAtyaM suratezviva#} (where {#anyadA#} is opposed first to {#pariBave#} and then to {#suratezu#} and therefore must not be taken in a general sense ‘sometimes’ --which it has not--but in the sense ‘at another time than that of defeat’, ‘at another time than that of amorous sport’; comm.: {#anyadA suratavyatirikte kAle yozito lajjeva#} {#puMso'nyadA apariBave Samo BUzaRaM pariBave tu yozitaH suratezu#} {#vEyAtyaM DArzwyamiva#}); or {#BartA tu yadA durBikze strIDanaM vinA#} {#vartanAkzamastadApi grahItumarhati nAnyadA#} ‘when the husband at a time of dearth cannot support himself without the property [Page143-b+ 56] of his wife, he may take it, not {%at another time%}’. <sup>2</sup> At one time, once. Compare {#anyadina#}. E. {#anya#}, vibhakti-taddh. aff. {#dA#}. See the Preface. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. f. ({#-dA#}) A virtuous wife. [According to a comm. of the Bhaṭṭikāvya: {#anyezAM patiSvaSurAdInAM dA Su-#} {#dDiryAByastAH#} (acc. plur. in the passage referred to) {#anyadAH#} {#sADvIrityarTaH#}.] Comp. {#anyadIya#}. E. {#anya#} and {#dA#} (from {#dE#}, kṛt aff. {#kvip#}).
{#anyadASA#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-SA#}) Another hope &c. (see the mean- ings of {#ASA#}) (Kāśikā = {#anyA ASA#}). Comp. {#anyASA#}; and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#ASA#}.
{#anyadASis#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-SIH#}) Another blessing &c. (see the meanings of {#ASis#}) (Kāśikā = {#anyA ASis#}). Comp. {#anyASis#}, and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#ASis#}.
{#anyadAsTA#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-sTA#}) Another place &c. (see the meanings of {#AsTA#}) (Kāśikā = {#anyA AsTA#}). Comp. {#a-#} {#nyAsTA#}, and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#AsTA#}.

{#anyadAsTita#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) I. Karmadh. Another who has obtained &c. <div n="P">II. Tatpur. One who has obtained another &c. (see the meanings of {#AsTita#}). Comp. {#anyAsTita#}, and see {#anya#}. [The meaning II. is given as a conclusion from Pāṇ. VI. 3. 99; but it is not mentioned by the commentaries; the first (I.) is supported by the explanation of the Kāśikā: {#anya AsTitaH#}.]
{#anyadina#}¦ Karmadh. m. n. ({#-naH-nam#}) Another day; {#anyadine#} ‘the other day, once upon a time’; comp. {#anya#} 1. a. and {#anyadA#} I. E. {#anya#} and {#dina#}.

{#anyadIya#}¦ I. m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) <sup>1</sup> Being in another (Kāśikā = {#anyasminBava#}). <sup>2</sup> Belonging to another (Kāśikā = {#anyasye-#} {#dam#}); e. g. {#anyadIyasyAdattasya grahItA na syAt#} (scil. {#dvijaH#}); also used in the same sense as the genitive of {#anya#} ‘of an- other’; e. g. {#anyadIyapAWamAkarRya svayaM vA SAstramAkalpya ya-#} {#jjYAnaM jAyate taditi#}; or {#parasvAnyArjayannArIranyadIyAH parA-#} {#mfSan#}. E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#} and āgama {#duk#}; see s. v. {#anya#}. <div n="P">II. f. ({#-yA#}) A virtuous wife. [This interpretation of the word is given, besides the usual one ‘wife of another’ (see meaning I.), by a comm. of the Bhaṭṭikāvya who after having explained the meaning and etym. of {#anyadA#} II. q. v. adds: {#tataH#} (i. e. from {#anyadA#}, a virtuous wife) {#svArTe IyaH#}.] E. {#anyadA#} II., taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.

{#anyadutsuka#}¦ Karmadh. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Another who is zealous &c. (see the meanings of {#utsuka#}) (Kāś. = {#anya utsukaH#}). Comp. {#anyotsuka#}, and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#utsuka#}.
{#anyadurvaha#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-haH-hA-ham#}) Difficult to be borne by another; e. g. a bow. E. {#anya#} and {#durvaha#}.
{#anyadUti#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-tiH#}) Another protection &c. (see the meanings of {#Uti#}) (Kāśikā = {#anyA UtiH#}). Comp. {#anyo-#} {#ti#}, and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#Uti#}.
{#anyadeva#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) Having other gods. E. {#anya#} and {#deva#}.
{#anyadevata#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Referring to another divinity, addressed to another divinity (as a hymn). E. {#anya#} and {#devatA#}.
{#anyadevatya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-tyaH-tyA-tyam#}) Referring to another divinity; e. g. {#aByAso vA prayAjavadekadeSo'nyadevatyaH#}. E. {#anya-deva-#} {#tA#}, taddh. aff. {#yat#}.
{#anyadehacikitsA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tsA#}) Administering remedies to others, exercising the practice of medicine. E. {#anya-deha#} and {#cikitsA#}.
{#anyadEvata#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) The same as {#anya-#} {#devata#}. E. {#anya#} and {#dEvata#}.

{#anyadrAga#}¦ Karmadh. m. ({#-gaH#}) Another affection &c. (see the meanings of {#rAga#}) (Kāśikā = {#anyo rAgaH#}). Comp. {#anya-#} {#rAga#}, and see {#anya#}. E. {#anya#}, āgama {#duk#}, and {#rAga#}.

{#anyaDarma#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-rmaH#}) The quality or characteristic of another, of something else. <div n="P">II. Karmadh. m. ({#-rmaH#}) Another quality or characteristic. <div n="P">III. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rmaH-rmA-rmam#}) Having other or dif- ferent qualities or characteristics. See the following. E. {#anya#} and {#Darma#}.

{#anyaDarmatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> The being the quality or characteristic of another or something else; e. g. {#vicitraBogAnupapattira-#} {#nyaDarmatve#}; comm.: {#duHKayogarUpabanDasya cittamAtraDarmatve vici-#} {#traBogAnupapattiH#}. <sup>2</sup> The having different qualities or charac- teristics; e. g. {#atiprasaktiranyaDarmatve#}; comm.: {#banDatatkAraRa-#} {#yorBinnaDarmatve'tiprasaktimuktasyApi banDApattirityarTaH#}. <sup>3</sup> The being another quality or characteristic. E. {#anyaDarma#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.
{#anyanABi#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-BiH-BiH-Bi#}) One who is not of the same family; the reverse of {#sanABi#}; comp. also {#nABi-#} {#sambanDa#} and {#sodara#}. E. {#anya#} and {#nABi#}.
{#anyanAmacihnita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Signed with the name of another, signed by another; as a deed &c.; comp. {#anyakfta#}. E. {#anya-nAman#} and {#cihnita#}.
{#anyanAmANka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-NkaH-NkA-Nkam#}) The same as the preceding. E. {#anya-nAman#} and {#aNka#}.
{#anyanindaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ndakaH-ndikA-ndakam#}) Censorious, detracting. E. {#anya#} and {#nindaka#}.

{#anyapadArTa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-rTaH#}) (In Grammar.) The sense of another word; this term is used by Pāṇini and his com- mentators to qualify the nature of a {%Bahuvrihi%} compound which always depends on, or refers to, the meaning of an- other word, the word {#anyapadArTa#} being thus used in contra- distinction of {#svapadArTa#}; e. g. Patanjali: {#aTAnyagrahaRaM kima-#} {#rTam . anekaM padArTe . itIyatyucyamAne svapadArTe'pi bahuvrIhiH#} {#syAt . rAjapuruzaH . takzapuruza iti nEtadasti prayojanam . tatpu-#} {#ruzaH svapadArTe bADako Bavizyati . #}; Kaiyyaṭa: {#aTAnyagrahaRa-#} {#miti . antaraNgatvAtsvapadArTe samAse sidDe padArTagrahaRasAmarTyA-#} {#danyapadArTo lapsyata iti praSnaH . svapadArTe'pIti . apiSabdA-#} {#danyapadArTe'pItyarTaH . padArTagrahaRaM vyAptisamASrayaRArTaM syA-#} {#diti svapadArTAnyapadArTayoH samAsaH syAt . tatpuruza iti .#} {#bahuvrIhestvanyapadArTo'vakASaH#}. [This word occurs only as a Tatpurusha. The quotation {#anyapadArTo bahuvrIhiH#} which is printed somewhere, is a misreading for {#anyapadArTapraDA-#} {#no#} &c. See the following.] E. {#anya-pada#} and {#arTa#}.

{#anyapadArTapraDAna#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-naH#}) (In Grammar.) Essentially qualified by, or essentially resting on the sense of another word, viz. a {%Bahuvrīhi%} (see the preceding); in contradis- tinction from {#pUrvapadArTapraDAna#}, the quality of an {%Avyayībhāva,%} {#uttarapadArTapraDAna#}, the quality of a {%Tatpurusha,%} and {#uBaya-#} {#padArTapraDAna#}, the quality of a {%Dwandwa%} (Patanjali: {#iha ka-#} {#ScitsamAsaH pUrvapadArTapraDAnaH . kaSciduttarapadArTapraDAnaH . ka-#} [Page144-b+ 56] {#ScidanyapadArTapraDAnaH . kaSciduBayapadArTapraDAnaH . pUrvapadArTapra-#} {#DAno'vyayIBAvaH . uttarapadArTapraDAnastatpuruzaH . anyapadArTa-#} {#praDAno bahuvrIhiH . uBayapadArTapraDAno dvandvaH ..#}). E. {#anya-#} {#padArTa#} and {#praDAna#}; scil. {#samAsa#}.

{#anyapadArTapraDAnatA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tA#}) (In Grammar.) The pre- ponderance of the sense of another word, viz. in a Bahuvr.; see the preceding; e. g. {#unmattagaNgamityAdAvanyapadArTapraDAnatA#} (Kaiyyaṭa). Comp. the following. E. {#anyapadArTa#} and {#praDAnatA#}.

{#anyapadArTaprADAnya#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-nyam#}) (In Grammar.) The same as {#anyapadArTapraDAnatA#}; e. g. {#sa ca yadi samAharaRaM samAhAra#} {#iti BAvarUpastadAnyapadArTaprADAnyam#} (Kaiyyaṭa). E. {#anyapa-#} {#dArTa#} and {#prADAnya#}.

{#anyapara#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-raH-rA-ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Having some one or something else for one's object (e. g. of worship). (Comp. the following.) <sup>2</sup> Expressing something else, having another sense, e. g. figurative speech; e. g. {#BedO Dvanerapi dvAvudIritO#} {#lakzaRABiDAmUlA . avivakzitavAcyo'nyo vivakzitAnyaparavA-#} {#cyaSca .#} (comm. on the latter word: {#vAcyaM vivakzitam . anya-#} {#paraM vyaNgyanizWam . atra hi vAcyo'rTaH svarUpaM prakASayanneva vya-#} {#NgyArTasya prakASakaH#}). E. {#anya#} and {#para#}.

{#anyaparatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> The having some one or something else for one's object; e. g. {#anyaparatvamavivekAnAM tatra#}. <sup>2</sup> The ex- pressing something else; e. g. in a Mīm. Vārtt. of Kumārila: {#adarSanAdviroDasyArTavAdAnAM cAnyaparatvena guRavAdaprAyatvAt#}. E. {#anyapara#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anyapuzwa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. ({#-zwaH-zwA#}) The Kokila or Indian cuckoo (supposed to be reared by a crow). Comp. {#kAkapuzwa, anya-#} {#Bfta, anyavApa#}; e. g. {#uditEranyapuzwAnAmArutErme hftaM manaH . u-#} {#ditErapi te dUti mArutErapi dakziREH ..#}. E. {#anya#} and {#puzwa#}.

{#anyapUrvA#}¦ Bahuvr. f. ({#-vA#}) A woman who has been given to, or has had intercourse with, another man than the one to whom she is married; this may be the case if she is either a {#punarBU#} or a {#svEriRI#}; as a {#punarBU#} (q. v.) again, she had either ceased to be a virgin before the nuptial ceremonies, or she had remained a virgin and become blemished through the repeated celebration of the marriage ceremonies; she is {#svEriRI#} or licentious, if she leaves her husband and goes, out of lust, to a man of the same caste. A woman, how- ever, is not considered to be a {#punarBU#}, if she is left without a son and, by order of her Guru, is approached, for the sake of getting a son, by her brother-in-law, or a relative of the class of the Sapiṇḍas or a man of the same Gotra, either of them having been previously anointed with clari- fied butter. (According to the Mitākṣara as founded on Yājnavalkya; Manu applies the term {#parapUrvA#}, the same as {#anyapUrvA#}, only to the licentious woman who leaves her hus- band for another man; Nārada uses the synonymous term {#parapUrvA#} in a similar manner as the Mitākṣara {#anyapUrvA#}, but divides the {#punarBU#} into three and the {#svEriRI#} into four cate- gories; for according to him a {#punarBU#} may be either a virgin- woman who is blemished by having gone through the mar- riage ceremonies for a second time, or a woman who first has been given to one and then on account of her love, to another, or a woman who, in want of a brother-in-law, is given by her relations to a Sapiṇḍa-relative of the same caste; a {#svEriRI#} a woman, whether having had children or [Page145-a+ 56] not, who, while her husband is alive, goes to another from lust, or a woman who leaves her infant husband for another man and later returns to the house of her husband; or a woman who after the death of her husband slights her brother- in-law and the other relations (she may approach) and goes from lust to another man, or lastly, a woman who has come from the country and, purchased with money, under the pressure of hunger and thirst gives herself up to another man. E. {#anya#} and {#pUrva#}; scil. {#strI#}.

{#anyaBAva#}¦ I. Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) The condition &c. of another; e. g. {#anyaBAvavyAvftteSca#} (comm.: {#anyasya BAvo'nyaBAvaH . anyaBA-#} {#vAdvyAvfttiH#} &c.). <div n="P">II. Karmadh. m. ({#-vaH#}) Another condition &c. (see the meanings of {#BAva#}). <div n="P">III. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-vaH-vA-vam#}) <sup>1</sup> Having another con- dition. See {#AnyaBAvya#}. <sup>2</sup> Having affection or love for another; e. g. {#ananyaBAve nijaDarmaBAvite manasyavasTApya Bajasva pUruzam#} (comm. {#nAnyasminBAvo yasya tasmin#}). E. {#anya#} and {#BAva#}.

{#anyaBft#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-t#}) A crow (lit. nourishing another, viz. the Kokila, the crow being supposed to hatch the eggs of the cuckoo. Comp. {#anyapuzwa, anyaBfta, anyavApa#}. The gender of this word is not defined in Hemachandra where it occurs; but it can scarcely be the masc.). E. {#anya#} and {#Bft#}.
{#anyaBfta#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-taH#}) The Kokila or Indian cuckoo. See {#anyapuzwa#} and the preceding. E. {#anya#} and {#Bfta#}.
{#anyamanas#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-nAH-nAH-naH#}) <sup>1</sup> Otherwise-minded, fickle-minded, versatile. <sup>2</sup> Absent (mentally), inattentive, distracted. E. {#anya#} and {#manas#}.
{#anyamanaska#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-skaH-skA-skam#}) The same as {#anyamanas#}. E. {#anya#} and {#manas#}, samās. aff. {#kap#}.
{#anyamAtfja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}) A son born of another mother; the same as {#sApatna, Binnodara, anyodarya#}. E. {#anya-mAtf#} and {#ja#}.
{#anyamAnasa#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-saH-sA-sam#}) The same as {#anya-#} {#manas#}. E. {#anya#} and {#mAnasa#}.

{#anyayoga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) The junction or union with another or something else; e. g. {#anyayoge'pi tatsidDinAYjasyenAyo-#} {#dAhavat#} (in the junction of the Soul with the other, i. e. with the Prakṛti &c.). E. {#anya#} and {#yoga#}.

{#anyarAga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Passion &c. (see the meanings of {#rAga#}) of another. <sup>2</sup> Passion (&c.) for another (not: another passion &c., see {#anyadrAga#}). E. {#anya#} and {#rAga#}.
{#anyarAjan#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-jA-jA-ja#}) Having some one for a master, subject to another. Comp. {#svarAj#}. E. {#anya#} and {#rAjan#}.
{#anyarAzwrIya#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-yaH-yA-yam#}) Belonging to another king- dom. E. {#anya-rAzwra#}, taddh. aff. {#Ca#}.
{#anyarUpa#}¦ I. Karmadh. n. ({#-pam#}) Another shape. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-paH-pA-pam#}) Having another shape. E. {#anya#} and {#rUpa#}.
{#anyarUpin#}¦ m. f. n. ({#-pI-piRI-pi#}) Having another shape. E. {#anyarUpa#}, taddh. aff. {#ini#}.

{#anyarhi#}¦ ind. Another time; the same as {#anyadA#}. E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#rhil#}. (This word is probably an irregular com- pound of {#anya#} and an obsolete locative of {#ahan#}, another form of which is {#ahar#}, the latter having passed into the state of an affix {#rhi#}.)

{#anyalakzaRopapatti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-ttiH#}) The taking place (of some- [Page145-b+ 56] thing) in consequence of the symptom i. e. the existence (of something else) being found somewhere else; in a Nyāya Sūtra, where the possibility of non-existence is argued from the circumstance that the existence of the counter-entity might be elsewhere: {#asatyarTe nABAva iti cennAnyalakzaRopapatteH#} ‘if (you say that there is) no non-existence since the thing is not, it is not so, for (non-existence) might be, since (the counter-entity) might exist elsewhere’. E. {#anya#} (in the sense of a locative) {#-lakzaRa#} (of an instrum.) and {#upapatti#}.

{#anyaliKita#}¦ Karmadh. n. ({#-tam#}) Another deed, another written document; e. g. {#CinnaBinnakfttonmfzwanazwadurliKitezu#} {#ca . kartavyamanyaliKitaM hyeza leKyaviDiH smftaH ..#}. E. {#anya#} and {#liKita#}.

{#anyaliNga#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-NgaH-NgA-Ngam#}) Used in either of the three genders (as an adjective; lit. having the gender of the other word to which it refers); the same as {#vAcyaliNga#}. E. {#anya#} and {#liNga#}.
{#anyaliNgaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) The same as the preceding; e. g. {#apazWuH puMsi kAle ca vAme syAdanyaliNgakaH#}. E. {#anya#} and {#liNga#}, samās. aff. {#kap#}.
{#anyaloha#}¦ Karmadh.(?) m. n.(?) ({#-haH-ham#}) Bell metal (accord- ing to a medical dictionary). E. {#anya#} and {#loha#}.

{#anyavarRa#}¦ I. Karmadh m. ({#-rRaH#}) <sup>1</sup> Another colour &c. (see the meanings of {#varRa#}); e. g. (in Arithmetic) another symbol, {#rASiM tena samutTApya kuryAdBUyo'parAM kriyAm . sarUpeRAnya-#} {#varRena kftvA pUrvapadaM samam ..#}. <div n="P">II. Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-rRaH-rRA-rRam#}) Having another colour &c. E. {#anya#} and {#varRa#}.

{#anyavAditva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) <sup>1</sup> Speaking differently, e. g. speaking one thing and doing another, as: {#jEhmyaM kOwilyam . anyA-#} {#BisaMDAnenAnyavAditvamanyakartftvam#}. <sup>2</sup> (In Law.) {#anyavAdin#}¦ Tatpur. 1. m. f. n. ({#-dI-dinI-di#}) Speaking dif- ferently (e. g. speaking one thing and doing another); comp. the preceding. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-dI#}) (In Law.) A plaintiff who states his cause or complaint in a different manner than he did originally. Comp. {#anyaTAvAdin#}. E. {#anya#} and {#vAdin#}.
{#anyavApa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-paH#}) (ved.) The Kokila or Indian cuckoo (lit.: who sows for others, i. e. who gets eggs which are hatched by the crow; comp. {#anyaBft#} &c. E. {#anya#} and {#vApa#}.
{#anyavikrIta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Sold by another (applied to property which has been sold without owner- ship; comp. {#asvAmivikrIta#}). E. {#anya#} and {#vikrIta#}.

{#anyavIjaja#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-jaH#}) Liter. born from another's seed, i. e. a boy who may be adopted as a son in want of a legitimate son (see {#Orasa#}) and become heir to the property, but who remains nevertheless the son of his real father; such sub- stituted sons are the following eleven, each succeeding being inferior in degree to each preceding (according to the order assigned to them by Manu): the {#kzetraja, datrima#} (or {#dattaka#}), {#kf-#} {#trima, gUQotpanna#} (or {#gUQaja#}), {#apavidDa, kAnIna, sahoQa#} (or {#sahoQaja#}), {#krItaka#} (or {#krIta#}), {#pOnarBava, svayaMdatta#} and {#pAraSava#} qq. vv. See also {#anyavIjotpanna, anyavIjasamudBava, anyaSAKodBava, dvyAmu-#} {#zyAyaRa#} and {#putrapraticCandaka, putrapratiniDi#}. E. {#anya-vIja#} and {#ja#}.
{#anyavIjasamudBava#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) The same as the preceding. E. {#anya-vIja#} and {#samudBava#}.
{#anyavIjotpanna#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-nnaH#}) The same as {#anyavIjaja#}. E. {#anya-vIja#} and {#utpanna#}.

{#anyavrata#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-taH#}) One who has other vows or fol- lows other practices. The vaidik commentators explain the word according to where it occurs either ‘one whose practices are different from those enjoined by the sacred books i. e. impious, a demon’ or ‘one whose practices are different from human practices i. e. the Supreme Spirit’. E. {#anya#} and {#vrata#}.

{#anyaSAKaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-kaH#}) <sup>1</sup> A Brāhmaṇa who has been {{abandonned->abandoned|||Dr. Sampada Savardekar|https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/50|}} by his school (comm. = {#svakIyaSAKArahitaH#}). <sup>2</sup> One who has been given up by his own family (comm. {#atra SAKASabdaH pakzAntare saMtativiSezArTaH#}); comp. the follow- ing. E. {#anya#} and {#SAKA#}, samās. aff. {#kap#}.

{#anyaSAKodBava#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-vaH#}) Lit. Produced by another family, the same as {#anyavIjaja#}; e. g. {#anyaSAKodBavo dattaH#} {#putraScEvopanAyitaH . svagotreRa svaSAKoktaviDinA svasvaSAKa-#} {#BAk .#} (where in the two latter words {#SAKA#} means the vaidik school). E. {#anya-SAKA#} and {#udBava#}.

{#anyasaNgama#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-maH#}) <sup>1</sup> Meeting another man. <sup>2</sup> Inter- course with another wife than one's own (in the latter meaning the word deserves notice for the shortening of {#anyA#} to {#anya#}); e. g. {#nirAsa BfNgaM kupiteva pahminI na mAni-#} {#nISaM sahate'nyasaMgamam#} (comm. {#anyASabdasya puMvacCreriti#}-- Vopad. 6. 4.--{#puMvat#}). E. {#anya#} and {#saNgama#}.
{#anyasADAraRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) Similar to others, common. E. {#anya#} and {#sADAraRa#}.

{#anyasAmAnya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-nyaH-nyA-nyam#}) Having the same qualities as others, common; e. g. {#sA kftasAmAnyena#} {#SrAvitAvatatyamumananyasAmAnyena . svaM rahasA mAnyena svayaMvaraM#} {#smarati nAYjasA mAnyenaH ..#}. E. {#anya#} and {#sAmAnya#}.

{#anyasfzwi#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-zwiH#}) (In the Sāṅkhya philosophy.) The evolution (of Pradhāna or Matter) for the sake of another (i. e. Purusha or Soul) viz., after one Purusha has been liber- ated: {#anyasfzwyuparAge'pi na virajyate prabudDarajjutattvasyevoragaH#}. E. {#anya#} and {#sfzwi#}.

{#anyastrI#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-strI#}) A woman not one's own. [In Rhetoric she is one of the three categories of the principal female character in a poetical composition (the two other being {#svastrI#} or {#svIyA#} and {#sADAraRastrI#} or {#sAmAnyanAyikA#} qq. vv.; the {#anyastrI#} or {#parakIyA#} is either ‘another's wife’ or a ‘damsel’; as ‘another's wife’ ‘she is fond of festivals and the like opportunities, is a disgrace to her family, bare of modesty’; the ‘damsel’ is ‘one not yet married, bashful and arrived at the period of youth’. Each of these two has again eight subdivisions; ‘she may be one who has an obsequious lover, or one who is ill-treated, or one who goes after her lover, or one who is separated from him by a quarrel, or one who is neglected, or one whose lover is abroad, or one who is prepared in her house to receive him, or one who is longing in absence of her lover’). E. {#anya#} and {#strI#}.
{#anyastrIga#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-gaH#}) An adulterer. E. {#anyastrI#} and {#ga#}.
{#anyastrIputrotpAdaka#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-kaH#}) The father of a child by another man's wife. E. {#anyastrI#} and {#putra-utpAdaka#}.

{#anyA#}.¦ The feminine of {#anya#} ‘other, different’ &c. q. v. This word deserves notice only from the circumstance that it oc- curs in some vaidik passages with the udātta accent on the first syllable, instead of having this accent on the last syllable. [Sāyaṇa is not the author of the meaning ‘never drying-up’ and of an etym. ‘{#a#} and {#nyA#}, contracted of {#ni-yA#}’ which have been lent to this word by a new kind of vaidik exegesis.]

{#anyAda#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-daH-dA-dam#}) Without food, food- less; e. g. {#AdareRa gamaM cakrurvizamezvapyasaMGasAH . vyApnuvanto#} {#diSo'nyAdAnkurvantaH savyaDAnharIn#}. E. {#a#} priv. and {#nyAda#}.

{#anyAdfkza#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kzaH-kzA-kzam#}) The same as {#anyA-#} {#dfS#}. [This word is given on the authority of the Siddhānta Kaum. fol. 181 a. 1. 14. ed. Calc. and on that of Durgādāsa's comm. on Vopadeva 26. 83. 85; it is not mentioned, however, in the commentaries of the Dhātupāṭhas, nor by the author of the Kāśikā who in his gloss on a Vārttika to Pāṇ. III. 2. 60. gives only the words: {#tAdfkza, yAdfkza, Idfkza#} and {#kIdfkza#}; Patanjali and his commentators do not even speak of the Vārttika on which the Kāś. has founded {#tAdfkza#} &c., the only word of a similar formation, viz. {#sadfkza#}, being men- tioned by Patanjali in his gloss on a Vārtt. to Pāṇ. VI. 3. 89. It will appear therefore, that {#anyAdfkza#} does not belong to the older period of the classical Sanskṛt.] E. {#anya#} and {#dfkza#} ({#dfS#}, kṛt aff. {#ksa#}) with the prolongation of the middle vowel.

{#anyAdfS#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-k-k-k#}; the nom. sing. in the ved. {#-N-N-N#}) Looking different, looking as if being another. (According to a comm. also in the sense: seeing like another, being an object of knowledge(?): {#anyamivemaM#} {#paSyanti janA ityanyAdfk . anyAdfSaSca . anya ivAyaM paSyati#} {#jYAnavizayo Bavati iti vA#}.) Comp. the preceding and the following. E. {#anya#} and {#dfS#} ({#dfS#}, kṛt aff. {#kvin#}) with the prolongation of the middle vowel.
{#anyAdfSa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-SaH-SI-Sam#}) The same as {#anyA-#} {#dfS#}. E. {#anya#} and {#dfSa#} ({#dfS#}, kṛt aff. {#kaY#}) with the pro- longation of the middle vowel.

{#anyADizWita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Occupied &c. by another, e. g. {#anyADizWite pUrvavadaBilApAn#} (comm. {#anyE-#} {#rjIvEraDizWite vrIhyAdO saMsarga eva tezAM na tu nizpezAdiduH-#} {#Kam#} &c.). E. {#anya#} and {#aDizWita#}.

{#anyADIna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Subject to others, dependant. E. {#anya#} and {#aDIna#}; but according to the gramm. authorities from {#anya-aDi#}, taddh. aff. {#Ka#}; or {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#saDInan#}; see s. v. {#aDIna#}.
{#anyAnuzWAna#}¦ Tatpur. ({#-nam#}) Doing something else, e. g. {#anya-#} {#duddiSyAnyAnuzWAnam#}. E. {#anya#} and {#anuzWAna#}.

{#anyAya#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-yaH#}) <sup>1</sup> No-rule, no authority, a word, a sentence &c. which is not binding; used in this sense especially in philosophical Sūtras; e. g. in the Mīmānsā Sū- tras, {#anyAyaScAnekaSabdatvam#}; or {#anyAyaSca kfte'ByAsaH#}; or {#anyAyo vAnAraByaviDAnAt#} &c. &c. <sup>2</sup> Unlawfulness, in- justice, an unlawful act; e. g. {#nyAyApetaM yadanyena rAjYA jYAna-#} {#kftaM Bavet . tadapyanyAyavihitaM punarnyAye niveSayet#}; or {#anyA-#} {#yena hftA BUmiranyAyena tu hAritA . harato hArakasyApi daha-#} {#tyAsaptamaM kulam#}. <sup>3</sup> Impropriety, improper conduct; e. g. {#iti#} {#matimAnASvasyAnyAyamanASaNkya vikftimAnASvasyAm#} (comm. {#asyAM damayantyAmanyAyaM parastryaBilAzalakzaRamanASaNkya#} &c.); or [Page147-a+ 56] {#narakasyAvatAro'yaM pratyakzo'smAkamAgataH . acezwA yadi hA-#} {#nyAyAdanenAtsyAmahe vayam#} (comm. {#anyAyAdanOcityAt#}). E. {#a#} neg. or deter. and {#nyAya#}.
{#anyAyadaRqa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-RqaH#}) Unjust punishment. E. {#anyAya#} (in the sense of an instrum.) and {#daRqa#}.
{#anyAyavartin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-rtI-rtiRI-rti#}) <sup>1</sup> Acting unlaw- fully. <sup>2</sup> Following evil courses, indecorous. E. {#anyAya#} and {#vartin#}.
{#anyAyavftta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ttaH-ttA-ttam#}) The same as the preceding. E. {#anyAya#} and {#vftta#}.
{#anyAyin#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yI-yinI-yi#}) The same as {#anyA-#} {#yavartin#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyAyin#}.

{#anyAyya#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-yyaH-yyA-yyam#}) <sup>1</sup> Not binding, not authoritative, not admissible; see the following. <sup>2</sup> Unlaw- ful, unjust, e. g. {#nyAyyaM svaM necCate kartumanyAyyaM vA karoti yaH#}. <sup>3</sup> Improper, indecorous. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyAyya#}.

{#anyAyyatva#}¦ n. ({#-tvam#}) The not being authoritative, not having binding power, not being admissible; e. g. {#brAhmaRavAkyasya#} {#viDAyakatvAdaprAptArTatvena viDO lakzaRAyA anyAyyatvAt#} &c. or {#svAyatte cEkAMSapade prayoktavye'vAcakapadaprayogasyAnyAyyatvA-#} {#dvittasyEvArDaM yuktam#}. <sup>2</sup> Unlawfulness, injustice. <sup>3</sup> Impropriety. E. {#anyAyya#}, taddh. aff. {#tva#}.

{#anyArTa#}¦ I. Karmadh. m. ({#-rTaH#}) Another or different sense, meaning, purpose; e. g. {#taTA cAnyArTadarSanam#} (comm. {#anyA-#} {#rTo'pi cEtamarTaM darSayati#}) or {#anyArTe ca#} (a Vārttika to several rules of Pāṇini as to VI. 3. 2, VI. 3. 5, VI. 3. 9). ({#-rTaH-rTA-rTam#}) Having another or different sense, meaning, purpose; e. g. {#anyArTA vA punaH#} {#SrutiH#}; or {#anyArTaSca parAmarSaH#} (comm. {#ityatra jIvaparAmarSo#} {#'nyArTo brahmopadeSaprayojanakaH#}); or {#anyArTaM tu jEminiH praSna-#} {#vyAKyAnAByAmapi cEvameke.--anyArTam#} on behalf of some one or of something else. Also {#anyadarTa#}. E. {#anya#} and {#arTa#}.

{#anyArTaka#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Having another or different sense, meaning, purpose; e. g. {#anyasyAnyArTakaM vA-#} {#kyamanyaTA yojayedyadi . anyaH SlezeRa kAkvA vA sA vakrokti-#} {#stato dviDA#}. E. {#anya#} and {#arTa#}, samās. aff. {#kap#}.

{#anyArTasvIkAra#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-raH#}) Adopting another sense, taking (a passage) in a different or opposite sense than its own; e. g. {#parisaMKyA…dozatrayaduzwA . svArTatyAgo'nyA-#} {#rTasvIkAraH prAptabADaSceti trayo dozAH .#}. E. {#anyArTa#} and {#svIkAra#}.
{#anyASA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-SA#}) The hope &c. (see {#ASA#}) of an- other. Comp. {#anyadASA#}. E. {#anya#} and {#ASA#}.
{#anyASis#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-SIH#}) <sup>1</sup> A blessing &c. (see {#ASis#}) of another. <sup>2</sup> A blessing &c. (see {#ASis#}) from another. Comp. {#anyadASis#}. E. {#anya#} and {#ASis#}.

{#anyASrayaRa#}¦ Tatpur. n. ({#-Ram#}) <sup>1</sup> Resorting to, or going to, an- other. <sup>2</sup> Devolving on another (as an inheritance); e. g. {#putre sati dravyasyAnyASrayaRAsaMBavAt#} &c. E. {#anya#} and {#A-#} {#SrayaRa#}.

{#anyASrita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) <sup>1</sup> Resorted to, or gone to, another; e. g. a wife (comp. {#anyapUrvA#} and {#parapUrvA#}): {#anyASritezu dArezu parapatnIsutezu ca . mftezvAplutya SuDyanti tri-#} {#rAtreRa dvijottamAH#}. <sup>2</sup> Devolved on another (as an inherit- ance); see the following. E. {#anya#} and {#ASrita#}.

{#anyASritadravya#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-vyaH#}) (In Law.) One whose pa- ternal or maternal inheritance has devolved upon another; as is the case for instance, when the son is incapacitated for receiving the patrimony through blindness, deafness or other legal disabilities (comm.: {#anyamASritamanyASritaM mAtf-#} {#pitfsaMbanDidravyaM yasyAsAvanyASritadravyaH#}). E. {#anya-ASrita#} and {#dravya#}.
{#anyASritaDana#}¦ Bahuvr. m. ({#-naH#}) (In Law.) The same as the preceding. E. {#anya-ASrita#} and {#Dana#}.
{#anyASritaBAryA#}¦ Karmadh. f. ({#-ryA#}) A wife who has gone to another man than her husband. Comp. {#anyapUrvA#} and {#para-#} {#pUrvA#}. E. {#anya-ASrita#} and {#BAryA#}.
{#anyAsa#}¦ Tatpur. m. ({#-saH#}) Not comprehending mentally &c. (see the meanings of {#nyAsa#}); e. g. {#KAnyAsa#} q. v. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyAsa#}.
{#anyAsakta#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-ktaH-ktA-ktam#}) <sup>1</sup> Attached to some one or something else. <sup>2</sup> Intent on something else, absent (mentally). E. {#anya#} and {#Asakta#}.
{#anyAsADAraRa#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-RaH-RA-Ram#}) Not common with others, uncommon, own, peculiar. E. {#anya#} and {#asA-#} {#DAraRa#}.
{#anyAsTA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-sTA#}) The residence &c. (see {#AsTA#}) of another. Comp. {#anyadAsTA#}. E. {#anya#} and {#AsTA#}.
{#anyAsTita#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-taH-tA-tam#}) Occupied &c. (see {#AsTita#}) by another. Compare {#anyadAsTita#}. E. {#anya#} and {#AsTita#}.

{#anyUna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-naH-nA-nam#}) Not deficient, not de- fective, entire, complete, much; e. g. {#anyUnaM guRamamftasya#} {#DArayantI saMPullasPuritasaroruhAvataMsA#}. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyUna#}.
{#anyUnANga#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-NgaH-NgA#} or {#-NgI-Ngam#}) Not being deficient in a limb, not having a limb too little. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyUnANga#}.
{#anyUnADika#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Neither deficient nor exuberant, neither too little nor too much. E. {#a#} neg. and {#nyUna-aDika#} (Dwandwa).
{#anyUnonnati#}¦ Bahuvr. m. f. n. ({#-tiH-tiH-ti#}) Of great elevation, very high; e. g. {#anyUnonnatayo'timAtrapfTavaH pfTvIDaraSrIBftaH#} &c. E. {#anyUna#} and {#unnati#}.

{#anyedyuzka#}¦ 1. m. f. n. ({#-zkaH-zkA-zkam#}) Occurring every other or following day, diurnal, daily. <div n="P">2. m. ({#-zkaH#}) (In Medicine.) A fever which recurs at the same hour daily, a quotidian fever (scil. {#jvara#}); comp. {#E-#} {#kAhikajvara#}. E. {#anyedyus#}, taddh. aff. {#kan#}.

{#anyedyus#}¦ ind. <sup>1</sup> On the other or following day. <sup>2</sup> The other day, one day, once (past or future); e. g. {#paredyavyadya pUrvedyu-#} {#ranyedyuScApi cintayan . vfdDikzayO munIndrARAM priyaMBAvukatA-#} {#magAt#} (where {#anyedyus#} is explained {#cirAtikrAnte ciragA-#} {#mini divase#}). E. {#anya#}, taddh. aff. {#edyusac#}; but more pro- bably a Karmadh. of an obsolete loc. of {#anya#} and an ob- solete genitive of {#div#}; see the Preface.
{#anyoQA#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-QA#}) The wife of another; in Rhetoric a female character as a subdivision of the {#anyA#} or {#anyastrI#} q. v. Also {#paroQA#}. E. {#anya#} and {#UQA#}.
{#anyoti#}¦ Tatpur. f. ({#-tiH#}) <sup>1</sup> Assistance &c. (see {#Uti#}) of an- other. <sup>2</sup> Assistance &c. (see {#Uti#}) by another. Comp. {#anya-#} {#dUti#}. E. {#anya#} and {#Uti#}.
{#anyotpanna#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-nnaH-nnA-nnam#}) The same as {#anya-#} {#vIjaja#}; e. g. {#nAnyotpannA prajAstIha#} (scil. {#SAstrIyA#}). E. {#anya#} and {#utpanna#}.
{#anyotsuka#}¦ Tatpur. m. f. n. ({#-kaH-kA-kam#}) Sorrowing &c. (see {#utsuka#}) for another. Comp. {#anyadutsuka#}. E. {#anya#} and {#utsuka#}.
